children.translated_text: Homage to the supreme god, whose self is unconquered by the three <s>guṇa</s>s (constituent qualities),
who in every respect has the form of <s>yoga</s> and is the cause of the absence of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly wandering).
To the cause of preservation, dissolution, and creation, who spreads within,
to the twenty-sixth principle, the supreme source, wise <s>Mahādeva</s>.
In the great sacred field of <s>Prajāpati</s>, at the confluence of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Kālindī</s>,
at supremely holy <s>Prayāga</s>, on the path to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>,
sages of disciplined selves, whose stains had been worn away by austerity,
having performed their daily rites on the full-moon day for the sake of bathing at the sacred ford,
saw the purāṇic narrator <s>Sūta</s>, devoted to truth,
who, after bathing in that great <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford), had come there to pay homage.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā te sūtam āyāntam ṛṣayo hṛṣṭamānasāḥ
children.translated_text: When those seers saw <s>Sūta</s> approaching, their minds were delighted,
and, after welcoming him, they prepared a suitable place for him to sit.
Then <s>Sūta</s>, after bowing to all those foremost sages,
took the seat that had been offered, endowed with every <s>dharma</s> (virtue and sacred duty).
When he was seated, the sages, strengthened by austerity, asked him,
"Long ago, good sir, at the <s>brahmasattra</s> of the dwellers in <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s>,

children.text: kathitaṃ bhāratākhyānaṃ purāṇaṃ ca paraṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: you told the tale called the <s>Bhārata</s> and also the supreme <s>Purāṇa</s>.
Because of that, you appear to us as <s>Satyavatī</s>'s son himself.
You know the highest meaning of all sacred traditions, and you are devoted to truth and <s>dharma</s>.
You are always intent on honoring twice-born men; therefore you are worthy of being questioned by us.
That account which, among Purāṇic subjects, is like the <s>Bhārata</s> narrative and yet surpasses it,

children.text: tattvā pṛcchāma vai janma kārttikeyasya dhīmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: we ask you about that: the birth of wise <s>Kārttikeya</s>.
For all these sages are devoted to attending upon you,
their minds filled with eagerness born from the desire to hear of <s>Skanda</s>'s origin."
Thus addressed then by those perfected foremost sages,
<s>Sūta</s> spoke these words to all the sages, words declaring the true matter:
"Listen, all you sages, to the origin of <s>Kārttikeya</s>,
to his brahminical character, his greatness, and his valor, which is greater than that of the thirty gods.
When the great-souled <s>Śuka</s>, desiring liberation, had gone to the supreme place,
<s>Vyāsa</s>, scorched by grief for his son, beheld <s>Tryambaka</s>.
As soon as he saw <s>Maheśāna</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s> became free from distress;
then that sage, the son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, wandered through the worlds.
Then, on the peak of <s>Meru</s>, he saw the eldest son of <s>Brahmā</s>,
<s>Sanatkumāra</s>, giver of boons, endowed with the sovereign power of <s>yoga</s>,
standing in a sun-like aerial car, shining with the brilliance of fire,
together with great-souled sages perfected in <s>yoga</s> and joined to austerity,
knowers of the truth of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, endowed with all sacred teachings of <s>dharma</s>,
and possessed of every branch of knowledge, surrounding him as if he were the four-faced one.
Seeing that very great-souled sage standing there, <s>Vyāsa</s>
bowed with supreme devotion, as if to <s>Pitāmaha</s> himself.
Then the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, seeing mighty <s>Vyāsa</s> arrived,

children.text: pariṣvajya paraṃ premṇā provāca vacanaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: embraced him with deep affection and spoke an auspicious word:
"By good fortune, knower of <s>dharma</s>, through the favor of <s>Pārameśvara</s>,
you have come here free from sorrow. Ask, and I shall explain."
Then, after hearing the words of <s>Brahmā</s>'s son, the foremost sage,
O brahmins, spoke this word that had long remained in his heart:
"How was the birth of <s>Kumāra</s>, wise <s>Kārttikeya</s>?
For what reason, and from where, did it occur? I wish to know this.
How is he the son of <s>Rudra</s>, and how the son of <s>Vahni</s> and <s>Gaṅgā</s>?
And how is he the child of <s>Umā</s>, and again of <s>Svāhā</s>?

children.text: suparṇyāścātha mātṝṇāṃ kṛttikānāṃ kathaṃ ca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: How is he also the child of <s>Suparṇī</s>, of the Mothers, and of the <s>Kṛttikā</s>s?
Who was he, having arisen before? What austerity did he practice, and what was his prowess?
This is indeed bewildering to beings; tell it just as it truly was."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus questioned, the splendid and excellent son of <s>Brahmā</s>,
the omniscient one, told everything to tireless <s>Vyāsa</s>;
hear it, sinless ones, as it is in truth, while I recount it.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I take refuge in the god <s>Īśāna</s>, omniscient and unconquered,
great <s>Mahādeva</s>, the great-souled lord of the whole universe.
His power is unobstructed, and his sovereignty is complete in every way;

children.text: svāmitvaṃ ca vibhutvaṃ ca svakṛtāni pracakṣate ||
children.translated_text: mastery and pervasiveness too are proclaimed to be his own creations.

children.text: tasmai devāya somāya praṇamya prayataḥ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Having bowed, intent and pure, to that god <s>Soma</s>,
I shall tell the auspicious origin of <s>Skanda</s> for one who desires to know the Purāṇic narrative.
The bodily descent of the god <s>Rudra</s>, the supreme self,
the consecration connected with <s>Prajāpati</s>, and likewise the severing of the head;
the sight of the six-family beings, and the discharge of the discus;
the origin of <s>Naimiṣa</s> and the completion of the sacrificial session;
<s>Brahmā</s>'s arrival there, and also the practice of austerity;
the vision of <s>Śarva</s> and the arising of the <s>Devī</s>;
the dispute involving <s>Satī</s>, and likewise <s>Dakṣa</s>'s curse;
how the birth from <s>Menā</s> took place, and how the <s>Devī</s>'s svayaṃvara occurred;

children.text: devānāṃ varadānaṃ ca vasiṣṭhasya ca dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: the granting of boons to the gods and to wise <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>;
the birth of <s>Parāśara</s> and of great-souled <s>Vyāsa</s>;
and the ending of the enmity between <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Kauśika</s>;
the emptiness of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and the description of the greatness of that sacred field;
<s>Rudra</s>'s presence here and also <s>Nandin</s>'s favor;
the vision of the <s>gaṇa</s>s (divine attendants) and the narration in full;
<s>Kālī</s>'s utterance and the practice of austerity as well.
The account of <s>Somanandin</s>, and likewise the granting of boons;
the becoming of <s>Gaurī</s>, the obtaining of a son, and the birth of the goddess;
the becoming of <s>Kauśikī</s> as mother of beings, and the lions and charioteers likewise;
the dwelling of <s>Gaurī</s> on <s>Vindhya</s>, and the meeting of <s>Vindhya</s> and the Sun;
the greatness of <s>Agastya</s>, and the slaying of <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Nisunda</s>;
the departure of <s>Niśumbha</s> and <s>Śumbha</s>, and the slaying of <s>Mahiṣa</s>;
the consecration of <s>Kauśikī</s>, and then the granting of boons;
also the birth of <s>Andhaka</s>, and the binding of the earth;
the slaying of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, and also that of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>;

children.text: balisaṃyamanaṃ caiva devyāḥ samaya eva ca
children.translated_text: the restraint of <s>Bali</s>, and the agreement of the goddess;
the going of the gods, and the very office of messenger assigned to Fire;

children.text: devānāṃ varadānaṃ ca śukrasya ca visarjanam
children.translated_text: the granting of boons to the gods, and the dismissal of <s>Śukra</s>;
then the birth of a son, and the goddess's sight of <s>Andhaka</s>;
the crushing of the demons beginning with <s>Śailādi</s>, and the goddess's becoming a hundred-formed one;
the granting of boons by <s>Āryā</s>, and the hymn of <s>Śailādi</s>;
the coming of the god, and likewise the telling of what had happened;
the account of the devoted wife, and of attendance upon the guru;
the account of <s>Pañcacūḍā</s>, and also the unassailability of splendor;
the arrival of the messenger, then the conversation and the dismissal;
the dialogue with the demon <s>Andhaka</s>, and the journey to <s>Mandara</s>;
the arrival of the gaṇas, and the hearing of their enumeration;
then the subduing of <s>Andhaka</s> by a great battle;
the granting of half the body, and the taking in of <s>Aśoka</s>'s son;
the origin of <s>Bhasmasoma</s>, and the dwelling in the cremation ground;
<s>Rudra</s>'s becoming blue-throated, and the description of the sacred abode;
the birth of the king of yakṣas, and of wise <s>Kubera</s>;
the subduing of the chief serpents, and the falling of the peak;
the bringing under control of the three worlds together with <s>Śakra</s>;
the presentation of <s>Devasenā</s>, and the consecration to generalship;
the coming of <s>Nārada</s>, who had indeed been sent by <s>Tāraka</s>;
the terrible slaying of <s>Tāraka</s>, and the pilgrimage to <s>Bhadravaṭa</s>;
the slaying of <s>Mahiṣa</s>, and the destruction of <s>Krauñca</s>;
the drawing out of the spear, and the auspicious slaying of <s>Tāraka</s>;
the arising of fear among gods and demons, and the battle concerning the three cities;
the conflict with <s>Prahlāda</s>, and the account called 'The Ungrateful One';
and the great blessedness of brahmins is proclaimed in detail.
Knowing this exactly as it is, one becomes an attendant of <s>Kumāra</s>;
he becomes strong and endowed with understanding, and obtains a son who is approved.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Hear this divine story, which destroys all sin,
as I tell it: wondrous, rich in meaning, and equal to sacred revelation;

children.text: yāṃ śrutvā pāpakarmāpi gacchec ca paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: having heard it, even one whose deeds are sinful may go to the highest state.
In no way should one repeat this story to an atheist, to one without faith, to a rogue,
or likewise to a man who is envious.
This should be told, O great brahmin, to a son, to a disciple, to a righteous and unenvious person,
or it may be told to one devoted to the gods,
and likewise to one devoted to <s>Kumāra</s> and full of faith.
Long ago <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of creatures, was born in this cosmic egg.
Because of ignorance, <s>Brahmā</s>, enveloped in darkness, did not know his father.
Thinking, 'I alone am ... all ...,'
he saw no other there, though he was endowed with the power of austerity and yoga.

children.text: putra putreti cāpyukto brahmā śarveṇa dhīmatā
children.translated_text: When <s>Brahmā</s> was addressed by wise <s>Śarva</s> with the words, 'Son, son,'
he bowed, stood with joined palms, and went to him alone for refuge.

children.text: sa dattvā brahmaṇe śambhuḥ sraṣṭṛtvaṃ jñānasaṃhitam
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s>, having given <s>Brahmā</s> the state of creator, together with knowledge,
and sovereignty over the worlds, the supreme Lord disappeared.
This eternal upaniṣad (secret teaching) has been spoken by me, O <s>Vyāsa</s>;
having heard it, yogins through meditation attain <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: brahmaṃ ca yo vidadhe putramagre jñānaṃ ca yaḥ prahiṇoti sma tasmai
children.translated_text: He who first made <s>Brahmā</s> his son, and who sent knowledge forth to him,

children.text: tamātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrāsteṣāṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām ||
children.translated_text: those wise ones who perceive him abiding in the self have eternal peace, not others.

children.text: sa vyāsa pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā svadīptyā parayā yutam
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, seeing his father endowed with supreme radiance,
and desiring a son for the sake of progeny, he performed severe austerity.
For that greatly noble one, intent on great yoga and austerity,
in a short time his father became fully pleased.
He came into his sight and said, 'I am the giver of boons.'

children.text: sa tuṣṭāva nato bhūtvā kṛtvā śirasi cāñjalim ||
children.translated_text: Bowing down, he praised him, placing his joined palms upon his head:
Homage to the supreme god, the creator even of the gods;

children.text: sraṣṭre vai lokatantrāya brahmaṇaḥ pataye namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: homage to the creator of the system of worlds, to the lord of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Homage to the one endowed with power and free from powerlessness,
to the infinite, the immeasurable, beyond the range of the senses;
to the all-pervading one, who has pervaded before, the overseer and impeller;
to the maker of consciousness itself, the arranger of the principles;
to the impeller of primordial matter, and the giver of peace to those possessed of qualities;

children.text: dṛṣṭidāya ca sarveṣāṃ svayaṃ vai darśanāya ca ||
children.translated_text: to the giver of sight to all, and to him who is himself vision;
to the apprehender of objects, and the maker of restraint;

children.text: manasaḥ karaṇānāṃ ca tatraiva niyamasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and to the restraint there of the mind and the instruments of action and perception;

children.text: bhūtānāṃ guṇakartre ca śaktidāya tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: to the maker of the qualities of beings, and likewise the giver of power;

children.text: kartre hy aṇḍasya mahyaṃ ca acintyāyāgrajāya ca
children.translated_text: to the maker of the cosmic egg and of me, to the inconceivable first-born one;

children.text: aprameya pitar nityaṃ prīto no diśa śakvarīm ||
children.translated_text: O immeasurable father, being ever pleased, show us the śakvarī.
As he was praising him thus, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, the god of gods, <s>Maheśvara</s>,
Being pleased, <s>Brahmā</s> himself spoke to his son, who was bowing down in that way:
"Because this subtle matter is known to you, child of great splendor,
therefore you shall become renowned among the worlds by the name <s>Brahmā</s>.
And because I have been called father by you, best of the wise,
therefore your status as grandfather shall become famous in the world.

children.text: prajārthaṃ yac ca te taptaṃ tapa ugraṃ suduścaram
children.translated_text: And because this fierce austerity, very difficult to perform, has been practiced by you for the sake of creatures,
therefore I grant you, whose self is restrained, the status of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
Having spoken thus, that lord of the gods created women embodied in form:
those eight prakṛtis (primary natures), and the modifications together with the senses,
and all the states of being, having taken their own forms, attended upon the god.
Then the god, the lord, endowed with his own splendor, said to them:
"By consecration establish him today, without delay."

children.text: tābhiḥ svaṃ svaṃ samādāya bhāvaṃ divyamatarkitam
children.translated_text: Taking up, each her own, an inconceivable divine state of being,
by them the exceedingly brilliant <s>Prajāpati</s> was consecrated.

children.text: tatraivaṃ yoginaḥ sūkṣmaṃ dṛṣṭvā divyena cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: There, seeing this subtle thing with divine sight,
the yogins, knowers of the truth of yoga, sing the ancient lore endowed with the three guṇas:

children.text: rudraḥ sraṣṭā hi sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ tava ca prabho
children.translated_text: "<s>Rudra</s> is indeed the creator of all beings and of you, lord;
and together with us you are the one who sets the world in motion.
That god, properly satisfied and bearing supreme lordly yoga,
consecrated his first-born son <s>Brahmā</s> in the office of <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: yaḥ kṛtvā bahuvidhamārgayogayuktaṃ tattvākhyaṃ jagad idam ādarād yuyoja
children.translated_text: He who, having made this world named the tattva, joined with many kinds of paths and yogas, carefully set it in order,

children.text: devānāṃ paramamanantayogayuktaṃ māyābhis tribhuvanam andham aprasādam ||
children.translated_text: also set the three worlds of the gods, joined with supreme endless yoga, in a dark, ungracious state through his māyās.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ manasi sadāvatiṣṭhamāno jānānaḥ śubhamaśubhaṃ ca bhūtanāthaḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of beings, always abiding in the minds of all and knowing both the good and the bad,

children.text: taṃ devaṃ pramathapatiṃ praṇamya bhaktyā nityaṃ vai śaraṇamupaimi sūkṣmasūkṣmam ||
children.translated_text: I approach that god, the lord of the <s>Pramathas</s>, the subtle beyond the subtle, as my refuge always, bowing with devotion."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: prājāpatyaṃ tato labdhvā prajāḥ sraṣṭuṃ pracakrame
children.translated_text: Then, having obtained the office of <s>Prajāpati</s>, he set about creating creatures.

children.text: prajāstāḥ sṛjyamānāśca na vivardhanti tasya ha ||
children.translated_text: But those creatures, as they were being created, did not increase for him.
While making creation in this way, <s>Pitāmaha</s>, lacking power,
then again began to practice austerity for the sake of creation.
Knowing of his austerity for the purpose of creation, the lord of the three worlds
entered the world with his splendor and came to his vicinity.
The creator, the lord of the world, showed the world within his own body to him.
The lord of the gods, <s>Hara</s>, lord of the great elements, came in person;
as if pervading the whole world with his supreme native splendor,

children.text: śambhuḥ prāha varaṃ vatsa yācasveti pitāmaham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s> said to <s>Pitāmaha</s>, "Ask for a boon, child."
In his mind <s>Brahmā</s> said to him, for the sake of creating the worlds, "Be my son."

children.text: sa jñātvā tasya saṃkalpaṃ brahmaṇaḥ parameśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing that intention of <s>Brahmā</s>, the supreme lord
himself, the giver of boons, thought, "This one is deluded," and said:

children.text: āgataṃ pitaraṃ mā tvaṃ yasmātputraṃ samīhase
children.translated_text: "Since you desire as a son the father who has come to you,
therefore, by my command, a son who is my own form will be born.

children.text: sa ca te putratāṃ yātvā madīyo gaṇanāyakaḥ
children.translated_text: And he, becoming your son, my leader of the gaṇas,
will take embodied form as <s>Rudra</s> and, deluded one, will discipline you.
The lordship over all knowledge, and over yogas in every way,
lordship over strength, and the agency in the use of weapons,
all these, granted by me, will quickly attend upon him in every respect:

children.text: dhanuḥ pinākaṃ śūlaṃ ca khaḍgaṃ paraśureva ca ||
children.translated_text: the bow <s>Pināka</s>, the spear, the sword, and the axe,
likewise the water-pot and staff, and the <s>Pāśupata</s> weapon,
the world-ending thunderbolt and the cyclic discus.
Thus endowed with every prosperity, he will be your son."
When that great-souled one, having spoken thus, had gone into invisibility,

children.text: brahmā cakre tadā ceṣṭiṃ putrakāmaḥ prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Prajāpati</s>, then performed a sacrifice, desiring a son.
As he was offering oblations, filled with weariness and met with obstruction,
he wiped his forehead with his hand that held a fuel-stick.
A drop of sweat from his forehead, produced from contact with the fuel-stick,
fell into that fire, doubled by his splendor.

children.text: taddhi māheśvaraṃ tejaḥ saṃdhitaṃ brahmaṇi srutam
children.translated_text: For that was the splendor of <s>Maheśvara</s>, lodged in <s>Brahmā</s> and flowing forth;
impelled by the god of gods, it fell into the oblation-eater.
At that moment, when <s>Maheśa</s> remembered that supreme boon,
the <s>Gaṇapa</s> <s>Rudra</s>, sent forth, came into being at once.

children.text: tac ca saṃsvedajaṃ tejaḥ pūrvaṃ jvalanayojitam
children.translated_text: And that sweat-born splendor, at first joined to the fire,
quickly became red and then at that time became blue.
Therefore that lord became known precisely as <s>Nīlalohita</s>, the Blue-Red one.
Three-eyed, ten-armed, splendid, he seemed to cover <s>Brahmā</s>.
With names beginning with <s>Śarva</s> and with bodies made of water and the other elements,
<s>Brahmā</s> praised that all-pervading, imperishable god <s>Nīlalohita</s>.
Afterwards, knowing him to be the creator of all and established in the great elements,
that lord created various other creatures in the world.
He too, resorting to yoga and endowed with lordly power,
entered all the worlds and continually upheld them.
Then the auspicious sons of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and the others,
created all creatures, crowded with gods and humans.

children.text: atha kālena mahatā kalpe 'tīte punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after a great stretch of time, when the kalpa had passed again and again,
while he was sustaining creatures by yoga, when this kalpa had arrived,
when livelihood had been established and the production of rain had begun,

children.text: prajāsu ca vivṛddhāsu prayāge yajataśca ha ||
children.translated_text: and while creatures had increased and he was sacrificing at <s>Prayāga</s>.
those seers of the six families of <s>Brahmā</s>, strict in their vows,
the <s>Marīcis</s>, the <s>Atris</s>, the <s>Vasiṣṭhas</s>, and likewise the <s>Kratus</s>,
the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s>, whose sins had been burned away by austerity,
approached <s>Brahmā</s> together and spoke during a pause in the rite:
Blessed one, we are enveloped in a great darkness;

children.text: khinnā vivadamānāśca na ca paśyāma yatparam ||
children.translated_text: we are wearied and disputing, and we do not see what is supreme.

children.text: etaṃ naḥ saṃśayaṃ deva ciraṃ hṛdi samāsthitam
children.translated_text: This doubt of ours, O god, has long remained lodged in our heart.

children.text: tvaṃ hi vettha yathātattvaṃ kāraṇaṃ paramaṃ hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: For you know in truth the supreme cause for us.
What is supreme for all beings, and stronger than everything?

children.text: kena cādhiṣṭhitaṃ viśvaṃ ko nityaḥ kaśca śāśvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: By whom is the universe presided over? Who is eternal, and who everlasting?
Who is the creator of all beings and the impeller of <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature)?
What great-minded one sets us to work in all undertakings?
Whose subjects are beings? Who assigns everything?

children.text: kathaṃ paśyema taṃ caiva etan naḥ śaṃsa sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And how may we see him? Tell us all this in full.
Thus addressed, then <s>Brahmā</s>, in the presence of all
the gods and seers, gandharvas, serpents, and rākṣasas,

children.text: yakṣāṇāmasurāṇāṃ ca ye ca kutra pravartakāḥ
children.translated_text: of yakṣas and asuras, and of whatever agents were there,
of birds together with piśācas and others who were near him,

children.text: utthāya prāñjaliḥ prāha rudreti triḥ plutaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: rose up with joined palms and uttered the word '<s>Rudra</s>' three times, in a prolonged tone.

children.text: sa cāpi tapasā śakyo draṣṭuṃ nānyena kenacit
children.translated_text: And he too can be seen by austerity, not by anything else.
He is the creator of all beings; he is mighty, and the world is made of him.

children.text: tasya vaśyāni bhūtāni tenedaṃ dhāryate jagat ||
children.translated_text: Beings are subject to him; by him this world is sustained.
Then all the lords of the worlds bowed to that great-souled one.
The seers said:

children.text: kiṃ tanmahattapo deva yena dṛśyeta sa prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: What is that great austerity, O god, by which that lord may be seen?

children.text: tan no vadasva deveśa varadaṃ cābhidhatsva naḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell it to us, and declare to us the boon-giver.
The Grandfather said:
Undertake a great <s>sattra</s> (sacrificial session), free from faults of speech and mind.

children.text: deśaṃ ca vaḥ pravakṣyāmi yasmindeśe cariṣyatha ||
children.translated_text: And I shall tell you the place, the place in which you should practice it.

children.text: tato manomayaṃ cakraṃ sa sṛṣṭvā tānuvāca ha
children.translated_text: Then, having created a mind-made wheel, he said to them:
Follow without delay this wheel which I have thrown.

children.text: yatrāsya nemiḥ śīryeta sa deśastapasaḥ śubhaḥ
children.translated_text: The place where its felly breaks apart is the auspicious place for austerity.

children.text: tato mumoca tac cakraṃ te ca tat samanvavrajan ||
children.translated_text: Then he released that wheel, and they followed it.

children.text: tasya vai vrajataḥ kṣipraṃ yatra nemir aśīryata
children.translated_text: As it was moving swiftly, at the place where the felly broke,

children.text: naimiṣaṃ tatsmṛtaṃ nāmnā puṇyaṃ sarvatra pūjitam ||
children.translated_text: that place became known by the name <s>Naimiṣa</s>, holy and honored everywhere.
It is honored by gods, humans, and siddhas, by fierce rākṣasas and divine serpents,
by yakṣas, gandharvas, hosts of piśācas, all apsarases, and the sons of <s>Diti</s>,
by restrained brahmins endowed with tranquility and yoga, and by all tīrthas and mountains,

children.text: gandharvavidyādharacāraṇaiś ca sādhyaiśca viśvaiḥ pitṛbhiḥ stutaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: and praised by gandharvas, vidyādharas, cāraṇas, sādhyas, viśvedevas, and ancestors.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Having reached that <s>Naimiṣa</s>, the seers of blazing splendor
sat down to a divine <s>sattra</s>, a great one lasting a thousand years.
All were single-pointed in mind, free from possessiveness and egotism,
always meditating on the Lord of lords, with wives, sons, and sacred fires present.
All were fixed on him, intent on him, joined to him, and taking refuge in him;
performing all rites, they went to him alone in their minds.
Seeing that disposition of theirs, <s>Mātariśvan</s>, mighty in austerity,
the splendid one who moves among all living beings and sets all beings in motion,

children.text: dadau sa rūpī bhagavāndarśanaṃ sattriṇāṃ śubhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the blessed, auspicious one, assuming form, gave a vision of himself to the sacrificers.
Having seen and worshiped that imperishable <s>Mātariśvan</s>,
seated on a holy seat, the seers strict in their vows
asked about the whole origin of the world and likewise its dissolution,

children.text: sthitiṃ ca kṛtsnāṃ vaṃśāṃśca yugamanvantarāṇi ca
children.translated_text: its entire continuance, the lineages, the ages and manvantaras,
the complete accounts of the lineages and also the divine measure of time,
the origin and dissolution of the eight classes of divine beings,
the whole creation of the ancestors and the measure of <s>Brahmā</s>'s life,
all the movements of the moon and sun, and the movements of stars and planets,
the establishment of all the lords, and the dharma of the continents in full,
the ordering of the classes and life-stages, and the institution of sacrifices.
That lord related all this completely and without remainder;

children.text: divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ ca teṣāṃ tad abhiyāt tathā ||
children.translated_text: and for them a divine thousand years passed in that way.
Then, in a divine form, with <s>Sāman</s> as her voice and the directions as her gaze,
with <s>Yajus</s> as her nose, <s>Atharvan</s> as her head, and sound as her tongue, auspicious and virtuous,
with <s>Nyāya</s> as her ears, <s>Nirukta</s> as her skin, and moving on feet of <s>Ṛk</s> and pada,
with time as her arms, the years as her hands, and days as the fingers she bore,
with kalās and other joints, and months as fingernails,
divine, supporting the kalpa, with breasts raised by the science of <s>Śikṣā</s>,
with the analysis of meters as her waist, and with <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> as her navel,
with the vast <s>Purāṇa</s> as her hips and <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> as her chariot of the mind,
with āśramas as her thighs, varṇas as her knees, sacrifice as her ankles, and fruits as her toes,
with the worlds and Vedas as her body, and with auspicious chandas as her hairs,
clothed in faith and good conduct, speaking of yoga and dharma,
she came forth from the middle of the altar and proceeded with supreme waters.
At its conclusion, after plunging at the avabhṛtha final bath, they came together with <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: tāmapṛcchanta kā nv eṣā vāyuṃ devaṃ mahādhiyam ||
children.translated_text: They asked that great-minded god <s>Vāyu</s>, 'Who indeed is this woman?'
That greatly radiant one spoke to the sages, who were imbued with dharma.

children.text: śuddhāḥ stha tapasā sarve mahāndharmaśca vaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are all purified by austerity, and a great <s>dharma</s> has been performed by you.
For this holy river has come here from <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
This is named <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the adornment of <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
She has first come into this mortal world for the sake of your accomplishment.

children.text: nāsyāḥ puṇyatamā kācit triṣu lokeṣu vidyate ||
children.translated_text: There is no river more holy than she in the three worlds.
The sages said:
How did this very holy one, who goes to <s>Brahmaloka</s>, begin to flow?
And what was the cause there? We wish to know this.
<s>Vāyu</s> said:
I shall relate to you here an ancient tale,

children.text: brahmaṇaścaiva saṃvādaṃ purā yajñasya caiva ha ||
children.translated_text: the dialogue of <s>Brahmā</s> and, long ago, of <s>Yajña</s> as well.

children.text: yajñairiṣṭvā purā devo brahmā dīptena tejasā
children.translated_text: Long ago the god <s>Brahmā</s>, after sacrificing with sacrifices and blazing with splendor,
created all beings, both stationary and moving.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā dīptimāndevo dīptyā paramayā yutaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing himself radiant, the god, endowed with supreme brilliance,
looked over his own worlds with his four lotus-like faces.
Seeing again and again the gods and the humans and the rest, the great-minded one

children.text: amanyata na me 'nyo 'sti samo loke na cādhikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thought, "There is no other equal to me in the world, nor anyone superior."
"I am the one who established all these creatures in the seven worlds,
among gods, humans, and animals; I consume and send them forth."

children.text: ahaṃ sraṣṭā hi bhūtānāṃ nānyaḥ kaścana vidyate
children.translated_text: "I am indeed the creator of beings; no one else exists.

children.text: niyantā lokakartā ca na mayāsti samaḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: I am the controller and maker of the worlds; nowhere is there anyone equal to me."
As he was thinking in this way, the great-minded <s>Yajña</s> came to him.

children.text: uvāca cainaṃ dīptātmā maivaṃ maṃsthā mahāmate
children.translated_text: The radiant one said to him, "Do not think so, great-minded one.

children.text: ayaṃ hi tava sammoho vināśāya bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: For this is your delusion, and it will lead to destruction."
"Such a thought is not fitting for you now, self-born one, established in goodness.

children.text: sraṣṭā tvaṃ caiva nānyo 'sti tathāpi na yaśaskaram ||
children.translated_text: You are indeed the creator, and there is no other; nevertheless this is not conducive to fame."

children.text: ahaṃ kartā hi bhūtānāṃ bhuvanasya tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: "I too am the maker of beings and likewise of the world,

children.text: karomi na ca sammohaṃ yathā tvaṃ deva katthase ||
children.translated_text: yet I do not fall into delusion as you boast, O god."

children.text: tamuvāca tadā brahmā na tvaṃ dhārayitā vibho
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> said to him, "You are not the upholder, lord.

children.text: ahameva hi bhūtānāṃ dhartā bhartā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: I alone am indeed the holder and sustainer of beings,
and beings have been created by me. You are the one deluded here."
Then <s>Veda</s>, greatly radiant, came there in agitation,

children.text: uvāca caiva tau vedo naitadevamiti prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the lord <s>Veda</s> said to those two, "It is not so."

children.text: ahaṃ śreṣṭho mahābhāgau na vadāmyanṛtaṃ kvacit
children.translated_text: "I am the highest, noble ones, and I never speak falsehood anywhere.

children.text: śṛṇudhvaṃ mama yaḥ kartā bhūtānāṃ yuvayośca ha ||
children.translated_text: Listen to who is the maker of beings, and of you two as well."
"It is the supreme lord, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the all-pervading master,

children.text: yenāhaṃ tava dattaśca kṛtastvaṃ ca prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: by whom I was given to you, and by whom you were made <s>Prajāpati</s>."
"This <s>Yajña</s> too is born from him, and in him the cosmic egg stands established.

children.text: sarvaṃ tasmātprasūtaṃ vai nānyaḥ kartāsti naḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: Everything indeed is born from him; there is no other maker for us anywhere."
To <s>Veda</s>, who was speaking in this way, the god <s>Brahmā</s> replied:

children.text: ahaṃ śrutīnāṃ sarvāsāṃ netā sraṣṭā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: "I am the guide and creator of all the revelations.
By my favor you are <s>Veda</s>, and this one is <s>Yajña</s>, without doubt."
"You two are deluded, or else <s>adharma</s> has been done otherwise by you.
Perform expiation; then you will be released from your sin."

children.text: evamukte tadā tena mahāñchabdo babhūva ha
children.translated_text: When he had spoken thus, a great sound arose.
A disk appeared, having the form of the solar orb,
standing above in the sky with a great and mighty sound.
And that too, falling from there, reached the surface of the earth.
Coming to a glen of <s>Himavat</s>, resounding with many kinds of birds,

children.text: vyomagaśca ciraṃ bhūtvā bhūmigaḥ saṃbabhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: after long remaining sky-going, it became earth-going.

children.text: tato brahmā diśaḥ sarvā nirīkṣya mukhapaṅkajaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandsire, looked over all the directions with his lotus-faces;
with the four of them he did not see that one standing in the sky.
He created a radiant fifth face situated on his head.
With it he saw that one standing in the sky, equal in splendor to ten thousand suns,
having the form of the solar orb, sounding, and terrible to behold.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā pañcamaṃ tasya śiro vai krodhajaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: When he saw that fifth head of his, great and born of anger,
it grew as if it would devour him, like the fire of universal destruction.
As it was growing then, resembling a submarine fire's mouth,
that god, the blazing disk, radiant and sounding,
quickly with the nail of the thumb of his left hand, and with disdain,
cut off that great and dreadful fifth head of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Then he, whose radiant head had been cut off, afflicted by intense pain,
fell down, confused in mind and deprived of the discipline of yoga.

children.text: tataḥ suptotthita iva saṃjñāṃ labdhvā mahātapāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, as if risen from sleep, the great ascetic regained consciousness
and praised <s>Mahādeva</s>, who stood in the disk, with a humble voice.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Homage to the thousand-eyed one; homage indeed to the hundred-eyed one.
Homage to the one with open mouth; homage indeed to the hundred-mouthed one.
Homage to the thousand-mouthed one; homage indeed to the one whose mouths are all mouths.
Homage to the thousand-footed one; homage indeed to the one whose feet are everywhere.
Homage to the thousand-handed one, and homage to the one whose hands are everywhere.

children.text: namaḥ sarvasya sraṣṭre ca draṣṭre sarvasya te namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the creator of all, and homage to you, the seer of all.
Homage to the one sun-colored, and to the cutter-off of the head.
Homage to the maker of creation and dissolution, and likewise to the maker of preservation.
Homage to the thousand-<s>liṅga</s> one and to the thousand-footed one.
Homage indeed to the one bearing the <s>liṅga</s> of destruction and to the water-<s>liṅga</s>.
Homage to the one moving within, to the all, and to the impeller of <s>prakṛti</s>.
Homage to the one pervading all beings and to the impeller of <s>puruṣa</s>.
Homage to the one who differentiates the objects of the senses, and likewise to the maker of regulation.
To the one who is what has been and what will be, to <s>Śarva</s>, and always to the one endowed with being.

children.text: tvameva sraṣṭā lokānāṃ mantā dātā tathā vibho
children.translated_text: You alone are the creator of the worlds, their thinker and giver also, O mighty lord.
You ought to show favor to one who has come for refuge and is restrained.
As he was thus praising him properly, with supreme devotion,
the Lord of the gods of gods then gave him divine sight.

children.text: cakṣuṣā tena sa tadā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: With that sight, <s>Brahmā</s>, the Grandfather of the worlds, then
saw, in a vehicle like the sun, a mass of splendor.
Then from its midst he heard a great voice,
deep, sweet, well-joined, and endowed with the marks of perfection,

children.text: viśadāṃ putra putreti pūrvaṃ devena coditām ||
children.translated_text: clear, first addressed by the god with the words, "Son, son."
The son <s>Nīlalohita</s> was born from sweat for you,

children.text: yac ca pūrvaṃ mayā proktastvaṃ tadā sutamārgaṇe ||
children.translated_text: and what I formerly said to you at the time when you sought a son,
that gaṇapa of mine who is yours and will be my own form,

children.text: sa prāpya paramaṃ jñānaṃ mūḍha tvā vinayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: having obtained supreme knowledge, O deluded one, will discipline you.
The fruition of that is this: the cutting off of your head.
It was brought about by me through him; therefore be content now.
And as for that sacrifice of yours, O great-minded one, which has strayed from the path,
he himself will cut off its head on some other occasion.

children.text: stavenānena tuṣṭo 'smi kiṃ dadāni ca te 'nagha ||
children.translated_text: I am pleased by this praise. What shall I give you, O sinless one?
<s>Vāyu</s> said:

children.text: tataḥ sa bhagavānhṛṣṭaḥ praṇamya śubhayā girā
children.translated_text: Then that blessed one, delighted, bowed down and, with auspicious speech,
stood with joined palms and spoke to that lord who is both perceptible and imperceptible.
O blessed lord, no sorrow troubles me because of your vision.

children.text: icchāmi śiraso hy asya dhāraṇaṃ sarvadā tvayā
children.translated_text: For I desire that this head always be borne by you,
and indeed, O mighty lord, may I remember this severing of the head.
And again, from deeds of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), I desire restraint by you alone.

children.text: tathā ca kṛtyamuddiśya paśyeyaṃ tvā yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: And, when some duty is at hand, may I see you at will.
Hearing <s>Brahmā</s>'s request, the Lord of the worlds spoke:
That one, called your son, my form <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
will cut off the head of the sacrifice, and he will bear your head.
Having spoken thus, the Lord of the gods of gods disappeared right there.
When that great god had gone, <s>Brahmā</s>, the Grandfather of the worlds,
together with the sacrifice and together with the Veda, returned to his own world.
<s>Vāyu</s> said:
The mortal who hears this secret account, equal to the meaning of the Veda,
upon reaching the separation of the body, will attain union with <s>Brahmā</s>.
And whoever recites this daily in the presence of brahmins,
freed from all sins, will be honored in the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
This lordly narrative is not to be told to those who are not sons, pupils, or yogins,

children.text: ākhyeyaṃ nāpi cājñāya na śaṭhāya na mānine ||
children.translated_text: nor to the ignorant, nor to the deceitful, nor to the arrogant.

children.text: idaṃ mahad divyam adharmaśāsanaṃ paṭhetsadā brāhmaṇavaidyasaṃsadi
children.translated_text: One should always recite this great divine chastisement of <s>adharma</s> in an assembly of brahmins and physicians.
A human being who has gained occasion here, at the breaking of the body, will enter the Grandfather.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then that blessed god, the matted-haired <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
by command of the supreme lord, took <s>Brahmā</s>'s head.
Having taken that blazing head and assumed a distorted form,
he engaged in the sport of yoga and went about for alms.

children.text: sa devaveśmani tadā bhikṣārtham agamad dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Then he went to the house of the gods for alms, O twice-born ones,
but no one gave a suitable alms-offering to that mighty lord.
In due course he came to the house of great-souled <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
He stood at his door, uttering the auspicious call for alms.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā tadupasthaṃ tu viṣṇurvai yogacakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: Seeing his arrival there with the eye of yoga, <s>Viṣṇu</s>
split a vein from his forehead and let fall a stream of blood.

children.text: papāta sā ca vistīrṇā yojanārdhaśataṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: And that broad stream then fell for fifty yojanas.
As it was falling in a stream for many years, O best of brahmins,
it did not fill even half of the Grandfather's skull.

children.text: tamuvāca tato devaḥ prahasya vacanaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: Then the god, laughing, spoke these auspicious words to him:
Maidens are given only once; fire is kindled only once.
Kings speak only once; alms are given only once.
I am pleased with this fitting gift of yours, O giver of honor.

children.text: varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te varado 'smi tavādya vai ||
children.translated_text: Choose a boon. Blessings on you. Today I am the giver of boons to you.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> said:

children.text: eṣa eva varaḥ ślāghyo yadahaṃ devatādhipam
children.translated_text: This alone is a praiseworthy boon: that I
behold <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the god, the fierce <s>Śarva</s>, the matted-haired lord of deities.

children.text: devaśchāyāṃ tato vīkṣya kapālasthe tadā rase
children.translated_text: Then the god, seeing the reflection in the fluid contained in the skull,
created a blazing man, strong and similar in form to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Then he said to him, "You are imperishable, ageless, and immortal,
unopposed in battles and the unsurpassed friend of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Splendid accomplisher of the gods' work, go about together with him.
Because your birth was from the waters that arose from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s body,
therefore by name you will be <s>Nara</s>, and you will be dear to him."
<s>Vāyu</s> said:

children.text: taṃ tadāśvāsya nikṣipya naraṃ viṣṇoḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having reassured that <s>Nara</s> and placed him with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord himself
went to the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, and those two entered the house.

children.text: ya idaṃ narajanmeha śṛṇuyādvā paṭheta vā
children.translated_text: Whoever here hears or recites this birth of <s>Nara</s>

children.text: sa kīrtyā parayā yukto viṣṇuloke mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: will be endowed with supreme fame and honored in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s world.
<s>Vāyu</s> said:
Having reached <s>Brahmā</s>'s world, the blessed protector of all worlds
said, "Alms, alms," and stood at the door.
Seeing him, distorted and adorned with a skull in his hand, <s>Brahmā</s>,
knowing him through great yoga, praised the Lord of the worlds.
Then the god, pleased with him, said, "I am a giver of boons."
"Choose, undisturbed, the boon that is in your mind."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
"Lord of gods and god of gods, I desire this sign made by you,

children.text: yena cihnena loko 'yaṃ cihnitaḥ syāj jagatpate ||
children.translated_text: a sign by which this world may be marked, lord of the universe."
Hearing that word of his, the blessed lord, best of speakers,

children.text: sarvaśrutimayaṃ brahma oṃ iti vyājahāra ha ||
children.translated_text: uttered the <s>brahman</s> (sacred formula) made of all revelation: "<s>oṃ</s>."
At the mere utterance of <s>Śambhu</s>, this speech, a goddess of divine form,
came forth from the god's mouth and stood there bowing.
Then the god addressed her, as if bringing her to life with his speech:
"Because, becoming an imperishable syllable, you have come forth from my speech,
therefore, goddess, you shall be the presiding deity of all learning.
Because you have resorted to this mouth of mine, the lake of <s>brahman</s>,
therefore in the world you will become renowned precisely as <s>Sarasvatī</s>.

children.text: imaṃ lokaṃ varāmbhobhiḥ pāvayitvā ca suprabhe
children.translated_text: Having purified this world with excellent waters, radiant one,
you shall again be the savior who carries all worlds across; there is no doubt here.
The gods, together with the Grandfather, will give you a share in the sacrifice,

children.text: puṇyā ca sarvasaritāṃ bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and you shall be holy among all rivers; there is no doubt."
Then, permitted by <s>Śaṃkara</s>, that radiant one
made the holy <s>Brahmasaras</s> in <s>Brahmaloka</s>, exceedingly purifying,
well filled with nectar-like water and adorned with golden lotuses,
thronged with flocks of many birds, its water stirred by fish;
then, coming forth again from there, she purified this world.
Taking up that skull, <s>Mahādeva</s> of immeasurable splendor
reached this world and settled in an excellent region.
There the lord of the gods, the master with blazing radiance,
established that great divine skull in front of the hosts.
Then, seeing it established there, all the hosts of the great-souled one
roared a tremendous roar, resounding through the ten directions,
like a churning ocean and a thunderbolt, by which the sky seemed to split apart.
Because of that terrible sound, an asura, a tormentor of the gods,
known as <s>Hālāhala</s>, came to that region.
Unable to endure it, blinded by anger, wicked and a destroyer of sacrifices,
and possessing a boon given by <s>Brahmā</s>, he was unslayable by all beings:
a buffalo surrounded by hundreds of asuras whose forms were concealed.
Seeing that angry buffalo, tormentor of the gods, rushing upon them,
the chief of the hosts spoke to all the hosts of <s>Pinākin</s>:
"This evil daitya, lords of the hosts, a tormentor of gods and asuras in the three worlds,
is coming swiftly. Therefore kill him."
Then all those lords of the hosts, enraged at the approaching enemy of the gods,

children.text: bhittvā śūlena saṃkruddhā vigatāsuṃ ca cakrire ||
children.translated_text: pierced him with a spear and made him lifeless.

children.text: hate tasmiṃstadā devo diśaḥ sarvā avaikṣata
children.translated_text: When he had been killed, the god looked toward all the directions.
From them came round-mouthed piśācas and mighty piśācī women,
approaching the lord of gods; to them he presented that being.
Used and appointed by them in every way,
they went to that very dwelling assigned by the god.

children.text: bhakṣayanti sma mahiṣaṃ mitvā mitvā yatastu tāḥ
children.translated_text: Because those women ate the buffalo, cutting him piece by piece,
therefore they were called the <s>Kapālamātṛs</s> by the wise god.
Because the skull was established in that place by <s>Pinākin</s>,

children.text: mahākapālaṃ tat tasmāt triṣu lokeṣu gadyate ||
children.translated_text: therefore it is called <s>Mahākapāla</s> in the three worlds.
When the skull had been established, it turned out just as had been foretold.
That <s>Śivataḍāga</s>, famous as releasing from all sins, came into being.
Then <s>Brahmā</s> came there, surrounded by hosts of deities,
addressed the matted-haired one, and blessed that region.
"This sacred field, extending half a yojana in every direction,
will without doubt become the siddha-field of the great-souled one.

children.text: śmeti hi procyate pāpaṃ kṣayaṃ śānaṃ vidurbudhāḥ
children.translated_text: For 'śma' is said to be sin, and the wise know 'śāna' as destruction;
because of meditation and restraints, therefore it is designated <s>śmaśāna</s>.
It is the secret, supreme, unsurpassed, and most beloved place of the god above gods.

children.text: evaṃ tatra naraḥ pāpaṃ sarvameva prahāsyati
children.translated_text: Thus there a man will cast off every sin entirely,
and, after fasting for three nights and worshipping the bull-bannered lord,
he will obtain the fruit that comes from the <s>rājasūya</s> and <s>aśvamedha</s> sacrifices.
And any human who gives up his dear life-breaths there
will attain equality with the gods of the secret hosts."
<s>Vāyu</s> said:

children.text: tataḥ sa tatra saṃsthāpya devasyārcādvayaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: Then, having established there an auspicious pair of images of the god,
<s>Śūleśvara</s> and <s>Mahākāya</s>, the auspicious abode of <s>Rudra</s>,
by merely going there one brings about the destruction of sin
and attains <s>Rudraloka</s>; so the Grandfather declared.
And where <s>Bhuvaneśvara</s> cut off his head,
that region, always supremely holy, became named <s>Kaśmīra</s>.

children.text: tato devaḥ saha gaṇai rūpaṃ vikṛtamāsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the god, together with the hosts, assumed a distorted form,
and the lord vanished while all the gods were watching.
When the lord of gods had gone, he joined the imperishable skull-place
with the fruit of bathing in all tīrthas.
Even today that great divine lake is seen there.
O best of brahmins, it is <s>Mahākapāla</s>; imperishable heavens are remembered there.
This auspicious, divine <s>Mahākapāla</s>, destroyer of adharma, bearing great fruit and worshipped by <s>Indra</s>, gods, and asuras,
reveals the present reality and is beneficial for entering the world of the lord of gods and the other heavenly realms.
A man who reads or always hears this, praised by ascetics rich in austerity and by hosts of siddhas in an assembly of twice-born kings equal to those dwelling in heaven,

children.text: paṭhennaro yaḥ śṛṇuyācca sarvadā tripiṣṭapaṃ gacchati so 'bhinanditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: goes to <s>tripiṣṭapa</s>, honored and rejoiced over.
<s>Vāyu</s> said:
Thus this blessed goddess, following the world of <s>Brahmā</s>,
came forth from the middle of the altar for the accomplishment of your <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then, when their thousand-year <s>sattra</s> was completed,
and when <s>Sarasvatī</s> had set forth, the Grandfather came there.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Again, with another <s>sattra</s>, sacrifice to the god, the Lord.

children.text: yadā vo bhavitā vighnaṃ tadā niṣkalmaṣaṃ tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When an obstacle will arise for you, then your austerity will become stainless.

children.text: vighnaṃ taccaiva saṃtīrya tapastaptvā ca bhāsvaram
children.translated_text: Having crossed that very obstacle, and having practiced radiant austerity,
having obtained great yoga and being disciplined, you will then see <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
After he had gone, they said, "So be it," and then undertook sacrificial sessions,
many and of various forms, intent and strict in their great vows.

children.text: niḥsomāṃ pṛthivīṃ kṛtvā kṛtsnāmetāṃ tato dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having made this entire earth without Soma, the twice-born sages
brought <s>Soma</s> the king and desired to consecrate him.
Then that <s>Soma</s> too, though received with hospitality, was seized
by the evil-minded invisible <s>Svarbhānu</s>, and therefore they became distressed.
All those sages, dwelling in <s>Kalāpagrāma</s>, went
and brought <s>Purūravas</s>; they consecrated him as king.

children.text: ūcuścainaṃ mahābhāgā hṛtaḥ somo hi naḥ prabho
children.translated_text: The greatly fortunate ones said to him, "O lord, our <s>Soma</s> has been stolen.
Let your majesty bring him here quickly, by someone or other; do not delay."
Thus addressed, that lord searched, but did not find him.
Then, bowing to the brahmins, he spoke, afflicted by fear:
"With the utmost effort I have sought <s>Soma</s>,

children.text: na ca taṃ vedmi kenāsau kva vā nīta iti prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: but I do not know by whom he was taken, or where he has been carried, O lords."
When he spoke in this way, the angry sages, firm in their vows,
all greatly enraged, spoke to the wise son of <s>Ilā</s>:
"Why have you been made king and protector by us, who are afflicted with fear,
if you are not able to remove that fear of ours even quickly?
Your mind is excessively attached to sense-objects, so you do not perceive him through yoga.
Therefore, by setting yourself against the twice-born, you will meet death from them.
We ourselves will bring the king, hard to find.

children.text: tapasā svena rājendra paśya no balamuttamam ||
children.translated_text: O king of kings, behold our supreme power through our own austerity."
Then all those sages, their sins burned away by austerity,
praised <s>Gāyatrī</s>, whose nature is the Veda, with words dear to her.
As they praised her, <s>Gāyatrī</s>, whose nature is the Veda,
appeared in embodied form and spoke these words to those twice-born sages:

children.text: tuṣṭāsmi vatsāḥ kiṃ vo 'dya karomi varadāsmi vaḥ
children.translated_text: "I am pleased, my children. What shall I do for you today? I am your giver of boons.
Speak; that very thing will be done here, without doubt."
The sages said:
"O goddess, our <s>Soma</s> has been stolen by some very evil being.

children.text: tamānaya namaste 'stu eṣa no vara uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Bring him back. Reverence to you. This is our highest boon."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: sā tathoktā viniścitya dṛṣṭvā divyena cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, she determined the matter and saw with divine sight.
Becoming a female hawk, she quickly went toward <s>Svarbhānu</s> the asura.
While the asuras were distracted, she seized <s>Soma</s> and returned.
Having come to those sages, she said, "Here is <s>Soma</s>; let him be pressed."

children.text: te tamāsādya ṛṣayaḥ prāpya yajñaphalaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Having obtained him, the sages attained the great fruit of sacrifice,
and the twice-born ones thought, "Our austerity is stainless."
Then <s>Brahmā</s> himself, together with the gods, serpents, and others,
came there and said to those sages, "Practice austerity without delay."

children.text: te saha brahmaṇā gatvā mainākaṃ parvatottamam
children.translated_text: They went with <s>Brahmā</s> to <s>Maināka</s>, the best of mountains,
and together with all the hosts of gods they practiced austerity with collected minds.
After a long time, for them, whose selves were purified by austerity,
the undertaking of yoga arose; from then on they were joined to subtle concentration.

children.text: te yuktā brahmaṇā sārdhamṛṣayaḥ saha devataiḥ
children.translated_text: Those disciplined sages, together with <s>Brahmā</s> and with the deities,
fixed their minds on <s>Maheśvara</s> and stood like motionless stones.
Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>, blue and red in hue,
approached that place in a celestial vehicle with the brilliance of the sun.
Knowing that they had been shaped by devotion to him, with supreme good will,
he spoke, with the roar of a cloud and the sound of a hundred kettledrums:
"Ho, ho! O gods with <s>Brahmā</s>, with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, sages, and cāraṇas,

children.text: divyaṃ cakṣuḥ prayacchāmi paśyadhvaṃ māṃ yathepsitam ||
children.translated_text: I grant you divine sight. Behold me as you desire."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then they all saw, equal in splendor to ten thousand suns,
a celestial vehicle like <s>Meru</s>, adorned with many jewels.
In its midst stood a very great blazing mass of fire,
encircled by a garland of flames and made splendid with rays.
His face was terrible with tusks, and his eyes were blazing fires.
His tawny matted hair was like the three sacred fires, and a serpent was bound as his girdle.
He wore polished earrings, and his great hand held a spear.
He bore <s>Pināka</s>, held a staff, and had a hammer and thunderbolt in his hands.
He had sword and shield in hand, bore a discus, and had an uplifted phallus.
He also held a rosary in his hand, and was hard to behold by those whose selves were unformed.
He was adorned with a garland made of the moon, sun, and planets.

children.text: tamapaśyanta te sarve devā divyena cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: All those gods saw him with divine sight,
him after seeing whom there would never be death even for a mortal.
The sages, yogins directed by austerity, bowed to <s>Bhava</s>, spotless as the moon,
their sight granted by the Lord in the sky, and were filled with joy together with the gods.

children.text: prasamīkṣya mahāsureśakālaṃ manasā cāpi vicārya durvisahyam
children.translated_text: Having carefully observed the unbearable time of the great lord of Asuras and also pondered it in their minds,
with thoughts of selfhood gone, they bow down together with the gods, praising the origin of the world.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: te dṛṣṭvā devadeveśaṃ sarve sabrahmakāḥ surāḥ
children.translated_text: When all the gods, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, saw the lord of the lord of gods,
they praised the bull-mounted one with desired words, after bowing down.
The grandsire said:
Homage to <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Soma</s>, the remover of fear from devotees;
homage to the one whose hand bears the point of a trident, and to the one who carries a water-pot.
Homage to the staff-bearing one, the blue-throated one, and the one with dreadful teeth;
to the three-eyed <s>Hara</s>, whose eyes blaze like the three sacred fires.
Homage to the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>, and homage to the wielder of the thunderbolt;
to the one whose sacred thread is a serpent, and to the one adorned with earrings.
Homage also to the discus-bearing one, and to the one clad in a tiger skin;
to the one whose upper garment is a black antelope skin, and likewise to the one whose girdle is a serpent.
Homage to the boon-giver, to <s>Rudra</s>, and likewise to the creator of <s>Sarasvatī</s>;
to the one whose garland is the moon, sun, and stars, and to the one who holds a rosary in his hand.
Homage indeed to the one with a thousand garlands of flame and with upward <s>liṅga</s>;

children.text: namaḥ parvatavāsāya śirohartre ca me purā ||
children.translated_text: homage to the mountain-dweller and to the one who formerly cut off my head.
To the destroyer of the <s>Hālāhala</s> poison, to the bearer of the skull and boon,
to the one whose excellent vehicle is an aerial car, and to my very own father,
homage to the boon-giving, most excellent one, who delights in the cremation ground.

children.text: namo narasya kartre ca sthitikartre namaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: Homage to the maker of man, and always homage to the maker of preservation;
to the maker of creation and dissolution, and to the one who endures all.
To the lord of seers and deities, and to the overlord of all beings:

children.text: śivaḥ saumyaśca deveśa bhava no bhaktavatsala ||
children.translated_text: be auspicious and gentle to us, O lord of gods, affectionate toward your devotees.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then, while <s>Brahmā</s> was praising him in this way, the god of gods, protector of the worlds,
being pleased, spoke to those gods and to the sages, who were strengthened by austerity:
"I am fully pleased with this austerity of yours, O sages and gods.

children.text: varaṃ brūta pradāsyāmi suniścintya sa ucyatām ||
children.translated_text: Ask for a boon; I shall grant it. Let it be stated after you have considered it well."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then, looking upon all of them, who were satisfied and strengthened by austerity,
and by the mere sight of him, O best of Brahmins, <s>Brahmā</s> spoke these words.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: yadi tuṣṭo 'si deveśa yadi deyo varaśca naḥ
children.translated_text: "If you are pleased, O lord of gods, and if a boon is to be given to us,
then become auspicious, gentle, and visible to us.
Be easy to deal with, always satisfied in mind,

children.text: sarvakāryeṣu ca sadā hitaḥ pathyaśca śaṃkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in all matters always beneficial, wholesome, and beneficent.
Together with the goddess, with your son, and with the hosts of gods as well,

children.text: eṣa no dīyatāṃ deva varo varasahasrada ||
children.translated_text: let this boon be given to us, O god, giver of a thousand boons."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Thus addressed by <s>Brahmā</s>, that blessed one, best of gods,
knower of all yoga, emitted his own great divine radiance.

children.text: ardhena tejasaḥ svasya mukhādulkāṃ sasarja ha
children.translated_text: With half of his own radiance he sent forth a flame from his mouth,
and the blessed one, bearing the form of the universe, said to it, "Become a woman."

children.text: sākāśaṃ dyāṃ ca bhūmiṃ ca mahimnā vyāpya viṣṭhitā
children.translated_text: Pervading the sky, heaven, and earth with her greatness, she stood there,

children.text: upatasthe ca deveśaṃ dīpyamānā yathā taḍit ||
children.translated_text: and, blazing like lightning, approached the lord of gods.
The god, smiling, said to that lotus-eyed goddess,
"O goddess of pure smile, worship <s>Brahmā</s>, the giver of boons."
She agreed, saying "So be it," and began to perform austerity.
And <s>Rudra</s> said to those sages, "Listen, in regard to my satisfaction,
O best of those who bear fruit, O treasures of austerity, to the fruit that I declare.
Immortal, abandoned by old age, free from disease, and exempt from birth,
devoted to me and joined with austerity, you shall dwell right here.
And this best hermitage, the excellent mountain <s>Svarṇaśṛṅga</s>,

children.text: puṇyaṃ pavitraṃ sthānaṃ vai bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will become a holy and purifying place; of this there is no doubt.
Because on the best mountain <s>Maināka</s> I became golden,

children.text: svarṇākṣīṃ cāsṛjaṃ devīṃ svarṇākṣaṃ tena tat smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and created the goddess <s>Svarṇākṣī</s> and <s>Svarṇākṣa</s>, therefore it is remembered as <s>Svarṇākṣa</s>.
At <s>Svarṇākṣa</s>, O sages, you six-family ascetics,

children.text: nivatsyatha mayājñaptāḥ svarṇākṣaṃ vai tataśca ha
children.translated_text: commanded by me, shall dwell; and then <s>Svarṇākṣa</s>,
a sacred field for a yojana all around, will exist; of this there is no doubt.
It will be frequented by gods and Gandharvas and served by hosts of Apsarases,
filled with lions, elephants, and śarabhas, and crowded with tigers, bears, and deer,
filled with many birds and crowded with creepers, trees, and shrubs.
A celibate person, observant of vows, having conquered anger and mastered the senses,

children.text: upoṣya triguṇāṃ rātriṃ caruṃ kṛtvā nivedya ca
children.translated_text: who fasts for three nights, prepares a <s>caru</s> (sacrificial porridge), and offers it,

children.text: yatra tatra mṛtaḥ so 'pi brahmaloke nivatsyati ||
children.translated_text: even if he dies anywhere there, shall dwell in <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
And even one who, filled with desire, sees the bull-bannered one there in just this way
shall, by my favor, obtain the fruit of a thousand cows.
And if he dies here in observance, he shall move about together with me.
As long as the worlds shall stand, and as long as this mountain <s>Maināka</s> shall stand,
so long, O gods, by my favor you shall move about together with me."

children.text: evaṃ sa tānṛṣīnuktvā dṛṣṭvā saumyena cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to those sages and looked at them with a gentle eye,
he disappeared right there, while all of them were watching.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
The mortal who hears this, or causes twice-born men to hear it,
also obtains that fruit and moves about free from death.

children.text: jayati jaladavāhaḥ sarvabhūtāntakālaḥ śamadamaniyatānāṃ kleśahartā yatīnām
children.translated_text: Victorious is the cloud-borne one, the death at the end of all beings, the remover of affliction for ascetics restrained by tranquility, self-control, and discipline;

children.text: jananamaraṇahartā ceṣṭatāṃ dhārmikāṇāṃ vividhakaraṇayuktaḥ khecaraḥ pādacārī ||
children.translated_text: the remover of birth and death for striving righteous people, endowed with various organs of action, moving in the sky and walking on foot;
the splitter of the city of <s>Madana</s>, the one who knocked out the eye and tooth, free from fear and despondency, conscious of all beings.
constantly speaking, discerning with self-possessed mind, adorned in hands and feet, the all-seeing god of gods.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: sā devī tryambakaproktā tatāpa suciraṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: That goddess, instructed by <s>Tryambaka</s>, practiced austerity for a very long time.
At times she went without food, and again she ate a single leaf;

children.text: vāyvāhārā punaścāpi abbhakṣā bhūya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: again she lived on air, and yet again she consumed only water.
Knowing her to be engaged in the practice of austerity and exceedingly radiant, <s>Brahmā</s>

children.text: uvāca brūhi tuṣṭo 'smi devi kiṃ karavāṇi te ||
children.translated_text: said, "Speak; I am pleased, goddess. What shall I do for you?"
She said, "Having obtained the god <s>Tryambaka</s>, moon-bright, as my husband,
may I wander happily through all the worlds, O god. Homage to you."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: na hi yena śarīreṇa kriyate paramaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: "Not with the very body by which supreme austerity is performed
is that supreme lord, husband <s>Śambhu</s>, obtained.
Therefore, by <s>yoga</s>, be born here as the daughter
of <s>Dakṣa Prajāpati</s>; having become his daughter, you will obtain <s>Rudra</s> as your husband."

children.text: tataḥ sā tadvacaḥ śrutvā yogāddevī manasvinī
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that word, the high-minded goddess, through <s>yoga</s>,
was born as <s>Dakṣa</s>'s daughter, named <s>Satī</s>, an exceedingly great yoginī.
<s>Dakṣa</s> gave that blameless woman as wife to <s>Tryambaka</s> himself;
by <s>Brahmā</s>'s command, he begot mental sons in her:
many thousands of <s>Rudras</s>, equal to himself in strength, blazing, free from old age and death,
and of immeasurable energy.
Seeing them being created, <s>Brahmā</s> restrained him,
saying, "Do not create, O lord of the gods of gods, offspring exempt from death.

children.text: anyāḥ sṛjasva bhadraṃ te prajā mṛtyusamanvitāḥ
children.translated_text: Create other offspring, welfare to you, offspring endowed with death."

children.text: tena coktaṃ sthito 'smīti sthāṇustena tataḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when he said, "I stand still," from that he was thereafter remembered as <s>Sthāṇu</s>.
The god said:
"I will not in any way create offspring connected with death, O <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: sthito 'smi vacanātte 'dya vaktavyo nāsmi te punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By your word I stand still today; you must not speak to me again.

children.text: ye tv ime mānasāḥ sṛṣṭā mahātmāno mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: But these great-souled, mighty ones who were created from my mind

children.text: cariṣyanti mayā sārdhaṃ sarva ete hi yājñikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: will all move about together with me, for all of them are connected with sacrifice."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: atha kāle gate vyāsa sa dakṣaḥ śāpakāraṇāt
children.translated_text: Then, after time had passed, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, that <s>Dakṣa</s>, because of a curse,
summoned his other sons-in-law with their wives and honored them in his house.
But, filled with anger, he did not invite <s>Satī</s> together with <s>Tryambaka</s>.

children.text: satī jñātvā tu tatsarvaṃ gatvā pitaramabravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Satī</s>, learning all this, went to her father and said:

children.text: ahaṃ jyeṣṭhā variṣṭhā ca jāmātrā saha suvrata
children.translated_text: "I am the eldest and most excellent, together with my husband, O pious one.

children.text: māṃ hitvā nārhase hy etāḥ saha bhartṛbhirarcitum ||
children.translated_text: Leaving me aside, you ought not to honor these women together with their husbands."
Then, possessed by anger, his senses overcome by anger,
<s>Dakṣa</s> looked at her and spoke, as if burning her with his eye:
"These women, O <s>Satī</s>, worship me affectionately along with their husbands;

children.text: na tvaṃ tathā pūjayase saha bhartrā mahāvrate ||
children.translated_text: you, great-vowed one, do not worship me in the same way together with your husband.
These ascetic women enter my houses with their husbands;
therefore I always consider them the best, and so I honor them.

children.text: tasmādyatte karomyadya śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever I do for you today, whether auspicious or inauspicious,

children.text: pūjāṃ gṛhāṇa tāṃ putri gaccha vā yatra rocate ||
children.translated_text: accept that worship, daughter, or go wherever you please."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then she, her face blazing with anger and greatly enraged, did not accept
that dishonorable and inferior worship; the fair one said this to him:
"Because you perform toward me this dishonorable worship,

children.text: ślāghyāṃ caivāpyaduṣṭāṃ ca śreṣṭhāṃ māṃ garhase pitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and because you censure me, your praiseworthy, faultless, and best daughter, father,
therefore I, your daughter, now abandon this own body.
What use is this inauspicious life to me today, dishonored as I am?"
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: tataḥ kṛtvā namaskāraṃ manasā tryambakāya ha
children.translated_text: Then, having made obeisance mentally to <s>Tryambaka</s>,
she, greatly enraged, spoke this speech, a fire-stick of words:
"Wherever I may be born again in a body by my own choice,
there too, born as a righteous <s>Satī</s>, undeluded in this way,
may I attain the state of lawful wife of wise <s>Tryambaka</s> alone."

children.text: tataḥ sā dhāraṇāṃ kṛtvā āgneyīṃ sahasā satī
children.translated_text: Then <s>Satī</s> suddenly entered into a fiery concentration,

children.text: dadāha vai svakaṃ dehaṃ svasamutthena vahninā ||
children.translated_text: and burned her own body with fire arisen from herself.

children.text: tāṃ jñātvā tryambako devīṃ tathābhūtāṃ mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing that the goddess had become such, the glorious <s>Tryambaka</s>
went to <s>Dakṣa</s> and, skilled in speech, said these words:
"Because I have been censured by you, while the others have separately been praised,
your sons-in-law with their wives, therefore in the interval of <s>Vaivasvata</s>
these sons-in-law of yours will be born again at your sacrifice.

children.text: tvaṃ caiva mama śāpena kṣatriyo bhavitā nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: And you, by my curse, will become a kṣatriya, a king,
and also the son of the <s>Pracetasas</s>, again in the daughter of the trees.

children.text: dharmavighnaṃ ca te tatra kariṣye krūrakarmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There I will make an obstruction to your <s>dharma</s>, cruel-doer."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: tamuvāca tadā dakṣo dūyatā hṛdayena vai
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dakṣa</s>, his heart pained, said to him:

children.text: mayā yadi sutā svā vai proktā tyaktāpi vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: "If my own daughter was addressed by me, or even abandoned again,

children.text: kiṃ tavātra kṛtaṃ deva ahaṃ tasyāḥ prabhuḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: what have you done here, O god? I am always her lord.
Because you have cursed me, therefore you too, O <s>Śaṃkara</s>,

children.text: bhūrloke vatsyase nityaṃ na svarloke kadācana ||
children.translated_text: shall dwell forever on the earth-world, never at any time in heaven.

children.text: bhāgaṃ ca tava yajñeṣu dattvā sarve dvijātayaḥ
children.translated_text: And after giving you a share in sacrifices, all twice-born men
will touch water everywhere, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, O greatly radiant one."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then the three-eyed god laughed and said to him:
"The earth-world is said to be the root of all worlds.
I alone support it, desiring the welfare of the worlds;

children.text: bhūrloke hi dhṛte lokāḥ sarve tiṣṭhanti śāśvatāḥ
children.translated_text: for when the earth-world is supported, all the worlds stand forever.
Therefore I remain here always, not by your command."
Having given shares to others, and likewise desiring to give to me, the twice-born

children.text: apaḥ spṛśanti śuddhyarthaṃ bhāgaṃ yacchanti me tataḥ
children.translated_text: touch water for purification; then they give me a share.
After giving it, they touch water again, precisely for the increase of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
For just as the pure wear the remnants offered to the gods,
and those who wish to touch what is impure first put it aside and touch water,
so, O bulls among brāhmaṇas, those who wish to give shares to the other gods

children.text: bhāgān apaḥ spṛśanti sma tatra kā paridevanā ||
children.translated_text: touch water. What cause for lament is there in that?
But you, burned by my curse, will become perverse, O lowest of men;
deluded in mind, you will beget a son upon your own daughter.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ sa bhagavāñchaptvā dakṣaṃ devo jagatpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus cursed <s>Dakṣa</s>, that blessed god, lord of the world,
the greatly radiant deity fell silent and went away as he had come.
We bow always here to him whose eyes are like the moon, sun, and fire, whose moon-like face has lotus-petal eyes,
who rides the bull, who is a measureless mass of virtues, and who ever bears the moon.
Whoever should hear this episode marked by <s>Dakṣa</s>'s curse and the goddess's bodiless state,
or, disciplined in vow, should cause brāhmaṇas to hear it,
will be freed from all sin and attain the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Once, when <s>Kaśyapa</s>, best of bipeds, had come to his own house,
<s>Himavān</s> asked him a question: what indeed brings fame in the world?

children.text: kenākṣayāśca lokāḥ syuḥ khyātiśca paramā mune
children.translated_text: By what, O supreme sage, would imperishable worlds and fame be obtained,

children.text: tathaiva cārcanīyatvaṃ satsu taṃ kathayasva me ||
children.translated_text: and likewise worthiness to be worshipped among the good? Tell me that.
<s>Kaśyapa</s> said:
Through offspring, O mighty-armed one, all this is obtained.
My fame is through offspring, and <s>Brahmā</s>'s too is through the seers.

children.text: kiṃ na paśyasi śailendra yato māṃ paripṛcchasi
children.translated_text: Do you not see this, O lord of mountains, since you ask me?
I shall also relate what I once saw, O mountain.
As I was going to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, I saw standing in the sky
a celestial, resounding aerial car, incomparable and blameless.
Beneath it I heard cries of distress from a place like a pit.
Knowing those people by my austerity, I remained there, concealed on the spot.
Then there came there, O lord of mountains, a brāhmaṇa who was restrained and pure,
his self purified by bathing at sacred fords, established in supreme austerity.
Then, as that brāhmaṇa was walking, frightened by a tiger,

children.text: viveśa taṃ tadā deśaṃ sā gartā yatra bhūdhara ||
children.translated_text: he entered that region, O mountain, where the pit was.
In the pit he then saw sages hanging from a clump of vīraṇa grass,
afflicted and distressed by suffering, and that brāhmaṇa asked them:

children.text: ke yūyaṃ vīraṇastambe lambamānā hy adhomukhāḥ
children.translated_text: Who are you, hanging head-down from a clump of vīraṇa grass?
By what are you afflicted, and how will there be release for you, O sinless ones?
The ancestors said:
We are your ancestors, together with your grandfathers, you who have done no merit,
and your great-grandfathers; we suffer because of your evil deed.
This, O greatly fortunate one, is hell, taking the form of a pit,
and you yourself are the vīraṇa stalk; we hang upon you.

children.text: yāvattvaṃ jīvase vipra tāvadeva vayaṃ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: As long as you live, O brāhmaṇa, for just that long we remain here.
When you are dead, we, whose minds are sinful, shall go to hell.
If, after union with a wife, you beget offspring superior in virtues,
then through that we would each be released from this.

children.text: nānyena tapasā putra na tīrthānāṃ phalena ca
children.translated_text: Not by any other austerity, son, nor by the fruit of sacred fords,
so do this, O very wise one; rescue your ancestors from fear.

children.text: sa tatheti pratijñāya ārādhya ca vṛṣadhvajam
children.translated_text: Promising, 'So be it,' and propitiating the bull-bannered lord,
he raised his ancestors out of the pit and made them leaders of the gaṇas.

children.text: svayaṃ ca rudradayitaḥ sukeśo nāma nāmataḥ
children.translated_text: He himself, dear to <s>Rudra</s>, named <s>Sukeśa</s> by name,
honored and powerful, became a leader of <s>Rudra</s>'s gaṇas.
Therefore, having performed terrible austerity, beget offspring surpassing in virtues,
O lord of mountains; then you will obtain fame.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: sa evamukta ṛṣiṇā śailendro niyame sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the seer, the lord of mountains remained under observance

children.text: tapaścakāra vipulaṃ yena brahmā tutoṣa ha ||
children.translated_text: and performed abundant austerity, by which <s>Brahmā</s> was pleased.
Coming to him then, <s>Brahmā</s> said, 'I am the giver of a boon.',

children.text: brūhi tuṣṭo 'smi te śaila tapasānena suvrata ||
children.translated_text: Speak; I am pleased with you, O mountain of good vow, by this austerity.
<s>Himavān</s> said:
Blessed lord, I desire a son adorned with all virtues.

children.text: etadvaraṃ prayacchasva yadi tuṣṭo 'si naḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: Grant this boon, O lord, if you are pleased with us.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: kanyā bhavitrī śailendra sutā te varavarṇinī
children.translated_text: A daughter will be born to you, O lord of mountains, fair in complexion,
by whose power you will obtain abundant fame everywhere.
Worshipped by all the gods, surrounded by ten million sacred fords,
purifying and holy in every way even for the gods,

children.text: jyeṣṭhā ca sā bhavitrī te anye cānu tataḥ śubhe ||
children.translated_text: she will be your eldest; and after that there will be others too, O auspicious one.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Having spoken thus, <s>Brahmā</s> vanished right there.
In time that lord of mountains begot upon <s>Menā</s>
<s>Aparṇā</s>, <s>Ekaparṇā</s>, and likewise <s>Ekapāṭalā</s>.
<s>Ekaparṇā</s> resorted to a banyan leaf, and <s>Ekapāṭalā</s> to a pāṭala leaf;

children.text: āśrite dve aparṇā tu aniketā tapo 'carat
children.translated_text: those two took shelter in them, but <s>Aparṇā</s>, without a dwelling, practiced austerity
for a hundred thousand years, difficult for gods and demons to perform.
<s>Ekaparṇā</s> took food by means of a single leaf,
and <s>Ekapāṭalā</s> likewise subsisted on a single pāṭala leaf.

children.text: pūrṇe pūrṇe sahasre tu āhāraṃ tena cakratuḥ
children.translated_text: At the completion of each thousand years, they both took food by that means.

children.text: aparṇā tu nirāhārā tāṃ mātā pratyabhāṣata
children.translated_text: But <s>Aparṇā</s> was without food; her mother spoke to her,
forbidding her with 'u mā,' distressed by maternal affection.

children.text: sā tathoktā tadā mātrā devī duścaracāriṇī
children.translated_text: Thus addressed at that time by her mother, the goddess, performer of difficult austerity,
By that very name she is famous in the worlds and worshipped by the gods.
This whole world, both stationary and moving, belongs to those three maidens;
