it was obtained by their austerity, for as long as the earth will endure.
All three had austerity as their very bodies and were endowed with the power of yoga.
All were greatly fortunate, and all remained fixed in youth.
They are mothers of the world, and they are also celibate ascetics.
By their own austerity they always show favor to the worlds.

children.text: umā tāsāṃ variṣṭhā ca śreṣṭhā ca varavarṇinī
children.translated_text: Among them <s>Umā</s>, fair in form, was the best and most excellent.
Endowed with great yogic power, she attended upon <s>Mahādeva</s>.
And <s>Dattaka</s>, son of <s>Uśanas</s>, was her son, that descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.
But <s>Ekaparṇā</s>, wife of <s>Asita</s>, gave birth to a son, <s>Devala</s>.

children.text: yā tu tāsāṃ kumārīṇāṃ tṛtīyā hy ekapāṭalā
children.translated_text: The third of those maidens was <s>Ekapāṭalā</s>.
She attended upon <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>, the son of <s>Śataśalāka</s>.
Her sons too are remembered as <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Likhita</s>, not born from a womb.

children.text: umā tu yā mayā tubhyaṃ kīrtitā varavarṇinī
children.translated_text: But the <s>Umā</s> whom I have praised to you, fair in form,
then, through the yoga of her austerity, the entire three worlds
were seen to be filled with smoke; and <s>Brahmā</s> spoke these words:
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
O goddess, why are you tormenting the worlds with austerity, O exceedingly beautiful one?

children.text: tvayā sṛṣṭamidaṃ viśvaṃ mā kṛtvā tadvināśaya ||
children.translated_text: This universe has been created by you; do not destroy it after creating it.
For you uphold all these worlds by your own splendor.

children.text: brūhi kiṃ te jaganmātaḥ prārthitaṃ samprasīda naḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell us what you desire, O mother of the world. Be gracious to us.
The goddess said:

children.text: yadarthaṃ tapaso hy asya caraṇaṃ me pitāmaha
children.translated_text: O Grandfather, the purpose for which I am undertaking this austerity

children.text: jānīṣe tattvametanme tataḥ pṛcchasi kiṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you know in truth; why then do you ask me again?
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
O goddess, O creator of the worlds, the purpose for which you weary yourself with austerity:

children.text: sa tvāṃ svayaṃ samāgamya ihaiva varayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: he himself will come to you here and choose you.
He is the lord of all gods, the supreme one, the lord over the lords of all worlds.
We, together with the gods, are under his command and speak as his servants.

children.text: sa devadevaḥ parameśvareśvaraḥ svayaṃ tavāyāsyati lokapo 'ntikam
children.translated_text: That god of gods, lord over the supreme lords, will himself come to your abode, O protector of the world.

children.text: udārarūpo vikṛtābhirūpavānsamānarūpo na hi yasya kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: Noble in form, yet possessing a distorted beauty, he has no form equal to anyone's.
<s>Maheśvara</s>, dwelling in the mountain-world, lord of moving and unmoving beings, is the first and immeasurable one.
Without the moon he has a moonlike face, and here he has assumed a foremost, terrifying form.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: tataḥ sa bhagavāndevo brahmā tāmāha susvaram
children.translated_text: Then the blessed god <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to her in a pleasing voice:

children.text: devi yenaiva sṛṣṭāsi manasā yastvayā vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: O goddess, he by whose mind you were created, whom you have chosen,

children.text: sa bhartā tava deveśo bhavitā mā tapaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: that lord of gods will be your husband. Do not perform austerity any longer.

children.text: tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā brahmā vyāsa gireḥ sutām
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> circumambulated the mountain's daughter

children.text: jagāmādarśanaṃ tasyāḥ sā cāpi virarāma ha ||
children.translated_text: and disappeared from her sight; she too ceased her austerity.
Saying, "So be it," that goddess then
stood leaning on an <s>aśoka</s> tree that had grown at the door of her own hermitage.
Then <s>Hara</s>, marked by the moon and remover of the gods' distress, came there,

children.text: vikṛtaṃ rūpamāsthāya hrasvo bāhuka eva ca ||
children.translated_text: assuming a deformed appearance, short and with stunted arms.
He became crooked, with a bent nose, hunchbacked, and tawny at the tips of his hair;
with a distorted face he said, "O goddess, I choose you."
Then <s>Umā</s>, perfected in yoga, knew that <s>Śaṃkara</s> had come.
Pure in her inner feeling, and desiring to carry out the rite,
she spoke to him after having brought water of welcome and a honey-mixture,
honoring the brāhmaṇa, who was comfortably seated; she was devoted to brāhmaṇas.
The goddess said:
Blessed sir, I am not independent; my father is here, and so is <s>Araṇī</s>.

children.text: tau prabhū mama dāne vai kanyāhaṃ dvijapuṃgava ||
children.translated_text: They have authority over my giving away, O best of twice-born men; I am a maiden.
Go and ask my father, the imperishable lord of mountains.

children.text: sa ceddadāti māṃ vipra tubhyaṃ tadrucitaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: If he gives me to you, O brāhmaṇa, that will be pleasing to me.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then that blessed god, the lord, still deformed in just that way,

children.text: uvāca śailarājaṃ tamumāṃ me yaccha śailarāṭ ||
children.translated_text: said to the king of mountains, "O mountain king, give me <s>Umā</s>."
Recognizing him, despite his distorted form, as the imperishable <s>Rudra</s>,
and frightened of a curse, he was troubled in mind and spoke these words:
Blessed sir, I do not show contempt for brāhmaṇas, the divinities of the earth.
But hear what was previously intended, O great ascetic.
There will be a <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice ceremony) for my daughter, O honored brāhmaṇa.

children.text: varayedyaṃ svayaṃ tatra sa bhartāsyā bhavediti ||
children.translated_text: Whomever she herself chooses there, he shall be her husband.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Hearing the mountain's words, the blessed one whose banner is the bull,
came to the goddess and, great-minded, said this:

children.text: devi pitrā tavājñaptaḥ svayaṃvara iti śrutam
children.translated_text: O goddess, I have been told by your father that there is to be a <s>svayaṃvara</s>.

children.text: tatra tvaṃ varayitrī yaṃ sa te bhartā kilānaghe ||
children.translated_text: There, O sinless one, the one whom you choose will indeed be your husband.
Therefore I ask leave; I will go. You are hard to obtain, O fair-faced one.
How could you pass over a handsome man and choose one like me?
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: tenoktā sā tadā tatra bhāvayantī tadīritam
children.translated_text: When he had spoken thus to her there, she reflected on what he had said,
and on the feeling placed there by <s>Rudra</s>, and on the serenity of her own mind.

children.text: samprāpyovāca deveśaṃ mā te bhūd buddhir anyathā
children.translated_text: Having attained it, she said to the lord of gods, "Do not let your thought be otherwise.
I shall choose you, and no other being in any way.

children.text: atha vā te 'sti saṃdeho mayi vipra kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: Or if you have any doubt about me, O brāhmaṇa,
right here, O greatly fortunate one, I choose you, the object of my heart's desire."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: gṛhītvā stabakaṃ sā tu hastābhyāṃ tatra saṃsthitam
children.translated_text: Then, taking in both hands a cluster of blossoms that was there,

children.text: skandhe śambhoḥ samādāya devī prāha vṛto 'si me ||
children.translated_text: the goddess placed it on <s>Śambhu</s>'s shoulder and said, "You are chosen by me."
Then the blessed god, thus chosen by the goddess at that time,
spoke to that <s>aśoka</s> tree, as if bringing it to life with his voice.

children.text: yasmāttava supuṣpeṇa stabakena vṛto hy aham
children.translated_text: Because I was covered by your cluster of excellent flowers,
therefore, abandoned by old age, you will become immortal.
Taking any form you desire, bearing any flowers you desire, going wherever you desire, you will be beloved to me,
rich in flowers of every adornment and furnished with the fruits of every tree.
You will eat every kind of food and will stream with nectar,
and, possessing every fragrance, you will be firmly dear to the goddess.
Fearless in all worlds, you will wander in perfect happiness.
And this hermitage, exceedingly famous as <s>Citrakūṭa</s>,
whoever comes to it seeking merit will obtain the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
And even if he dies anywhere there, he will go to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Whoever here, endowed with observances, properly gives up his life,
he, joined with the goddess's austerity, will become a great lord of the gaṇas.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Having spoken thus then, the god took leave of the daughter of <s>Himavat</s>,
and the creator of the world, the lord of all beings, disappeared.
When that blessed one of immeasurable self had gone, the goddess too,

children.text: tata evonmukhī sthitvā śilāyāṃ saṃviveśa ha ||
children.translated_text: standing there with her face raised, sat down upon a rock.
With her face lifted after that great archer, the lord of creatures, had departed,
she shone then like a moonless night, downcast in mind.

children.text: atha śuśrāva sā śabdaṃ bālasyārtasya śailajā
children.translated_text: Then the daughter of the mountain heard the cry of a distressed child,
in a water-filled lake near the hermitage.

children.text: sa kṛtvā bālarūpaṃ tu devadevaḥ svayaṃ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: The god of gods, <s>Śiva</s> himself, had assumed the form of a child,
and for the sake of sport he was then seized by a crocodile in the middle of the lake.
Having resorted to yogamāyā, the cause of the arising of the manifest world,
he made that form in the middle of the lake and spoke this:
Let someone come here to rescue me, whose wits have been seized by a crocodile.
Alas, the misery! I am only a child, my desires and purposes not yet fulfilled,
and I shall go to death in the mouth of this evil crocodile.

children.text: śocāmi na svakaṃ dehaṃ grāhagrasto 'pi duḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: I do not grieve for my own body, though seized by the crocodile and suffering,

children.text: yathā śocāmi pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca tapasvinīm ||
children.translated_text: as I grieve for my father and my ascetic mother.
Hearing that I have reached death in the crocodile's mouth, both of them, distraught,
loving their dear son, having only one son, will surely give up their lives.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: śrutvā tu devī taṃ nādaṃ viprasyārtasya śobhanā
children.translated_text: Hearing the cry of that distressed brahmin, the beautiful goddess

children.text: utthāya pradrutā tatra yatra tiṣṭhatyasau dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: rose and ran there, to where that twice-born child was staying.
Moon-faced, she saw the boy, lovely in form,
being swallowed by the crocodile and standing there trembling.
And that excellent, splendid crocodile, seeing the goddess approaching,

children.text: taṃ gṛhītvā drutaṃ yāto madhyaṃ sarasa eva ha ||
children.translated_text: seized him and quickly went to the very middle of the lake.
As he was being dragged away, the radiant boy uttered a cry of distress,

children.text: athāha devī duḥkhārtā bālaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāvratā ||
children.translated_text: and then the goddess, pained by sorrow on seeing the child, she of great vows, said:
O king of crocodiles, great being, this child is an only son.
Release him, great-fanged one, quickly, you of terrible prowess.
The crocodile said:

children.text: yo devi divase ṣaṣṭhe prathamaṃ samupaiti mām
children.translated_text: O goddess, whoever first comes to me on the sixth day

children.text: sa āhāro mama purā vihito lokakartṛbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: was formerly ordained by the makers of the world to be my food.
So this one, great lady, on the sixth day, O daughter of the lord of mountains,

children.text: brahmaṇā vihito nūnaṃ nainaṃ mokṣye kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: has surely been assigned to me by <s>Brahmā</s>; I will not release him in any way.
The goddess said:
By the supreme austerity that I practiced on the peak of <s>Himavat</s>,

children.text: tena bālamimaṃ muñca grāharāja namo 'stu te ||
children.translated_text: release this child, O king of crocodiles. Reverence to you.
The crocodile said:

children.text: mā vyayaṃ tapaso devi kārṣīḥ śailendranandane
children.translated_text: Do not cause the wasting of your austerity, O goddess, daughter of the mountain lord.

children.text: nainaṃ mocayituṃ śakto devarājo 'pi sa svayam ||
children.translated_text: Even the king of the gods himself is not able to free him.
By the lord, fierce <s>Śarva</s>, the trident-bearer, when he was pleased with me,
immortality, invulnerability, and inexhaustible strength were granted,
as well as the power of seizing and releasing at my own will, and again unfailing knowledge.

children.text: dattaṃ tato bravīmi tvāṃ nāyaṃ mokṣamavāpsyati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I tell you: this boy will not obtain release.

children.text: atha vā te kṛpā devi bhṛśaṃ bāle śubhānane
children.translated_text: But if your compassion for the child is very great, O goddess of auspicious face,
I will tell you what to do; after that he will obtain release.
The goddess said:
O lord of crocodiles, quickly say what is not blamed by the good.

children.text: tatkṛtaṃ nātra saṃdeho mānyā me brāhmaṇā dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: That will be done; there is no doubt here. Brahmins are firmly worthy of honor to me.
The crocodile said:
Whatever austerity has been performed by you, even the least amount,
give all of that to me; then he will obtain release.
The goddess said:
Whatever merit I have made from birth onward, O great crocodile,

children.text: tatte sarvaṃ mayā dattaṃ bālaṃ muñca mamāgrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: all that has been given to you by me. Release the child before me.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then the crocodile blazed forth, enlarged by that austerity,
and at that time became hard to behold, like the sun at midday.

children.text: uvāca cedaṃ tuṣṭātmā devīṃ lokasya dhāriṇīm
children.translated_text: And, pleased in spirit, he spoke this to the goddess, the supporter of the world:
O goddess, what have you done, without deliberating, you of great vows?

children.text: tapaso hy arjanaṃ duḥkhaṃ tasya tyāgo na śasyate ||
children.translated_text: The acquisition of austerity is difficult, and its abandonment is not praised.

children.text: gṛhāṇa tapa etacca bālaṃ cemaṃ śucismite
children.translated_text: Take back this austerity and this child, O pure-smiling one.

children.text: tuṣṭo 'smi te viprabhaktyā varaṃ tasmāddadāmi te ||
children.translated_text: I am pleased with your devotion to the brahmin; therefore I give you a boon.

children.text: sā tv evamuktā grāheṇa uvācedaṃ mahāvratā
children.translated_text: But she, thus addressed by the crocodile, she of great vows, said this:
With full resolve, O great crocodile, this was done for the child's release.

children.text: na viprebhyastapaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhā me brāhmaṇā matāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Austerity is not superior to brahmins; brahmins are considered superior by me.

children.text: dattvā cāhaṃ na gṛhṇāmi grāhendra viditaṃ hi te
children.translated_text: And after giving, I do not take back, O lord of crocodiles; you know this well.

children.text: na hi kaścin naro grāha pradattaṃ punarāharet ||
children.translated_text: For no person, O crocodile, should take back what has been given.
This has been given by me to you; I do not take it back again.
Let it remain and delight in you, and let this child be released.

children.text: tathoktastāṃ praśasyātha muktvā bālaṃ namasya ca
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, after praising her, releasing the boy, and bowing
to the goddess, who had the true radiance of the sun, he disappeared right there.

children.text: bālo 'pi sarasastīre mukto grāheṇa vai tadā
children.translated_text: The boy too, then freed by the crocodile on the shore of the lake,
like a mass of wealth obtained in a dream, disappeared right there.
Then, thinking her austerity had been expended, the goddess, daughter of the lord of the snowy mountain,

children.text: bhūya eva tapaḥ kartum ārebhe yatnamāsthitā ||
children.translated_text: again undertook the effort to perform austerity.

children.text: kartukāmāṃ tapo bhūyo jñātvā tāṃ śaṃkaraḥ svayam
children.translated_text: Knowing that she wished to perform austerity again, <s>Śaṃkara</s> himself

children.text: provāca vacanaṃ vyāsa mā kṛthās tapa ityuta ||
children.translated_text: spoke these words, O <s>Vyāsa</s>: "Do not perform austerity."
"O goddess of great vows, this austerity has been given by you to me;
by that very act it will become inexhaustible for you a thousandfold."
Having thus received the excellent boon of the inexhaustibility of her austerity, the goddess,
awaiting the svayaṃvara, remained filled with pleasure and joy.

children.text: idaṃ paṭhedyo hi naraḥ sadaiva bālānubhāvācaraṇaṃ hi śambhoḥ
children.translated_text: The man who always recites this account of <s>Śambhu</s>'s conduct and power as a boy

children.text: sa dehabhedaṃ samavāpya pūto bhavedgaṇastasya kumāratulyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will, after the breaking of the body, become purified and become his attendant, equal to <s>Kumāra</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
On the broad back of <s>Himavat</s>, crowded with hundreds of aerial palaces,
in time there took place that svayaṃvara of <s>Śailaputrī</s>.
Then that mountain-king <s>Himavat</s>, skilled in meditation,
knowing that this had been enjoined by the god of gods for his daughter,
although he knew it, the great mountain, desiring to carry out the customary observance,
then proclaimed the goddess's svayaṃvara throughout all the worlds.
Among gods, Dānavas, Siddhas, and all inhabitants of the worlds,
"May my daughter choose <s>Parameśāna</s> before their eyes.
That alone is meritorious, praiseworthy, and approved as my prosperity";

children.text: iti saṃcintya śailendraḥ kṛtvā hṛdi maheśvaram ||
children.translated_text: thinking thus, the lord of mountains placed <s>Maheśvara</s> in his heart.
In the worlds as far as <s>Brahmā</s>'s realm, that best lord of mountains
made the region filled with jewels and had the goddess's svayaṃvara performed.
And as soon as the svayaṃvara of the mountain's daughter had been proclaimed in this way, O <s>Vyāsa</s>,
the gods and the others, inhabitants of the whole universe, came together, having assumed divine forms.
Seated on a fully blossomed lotus seat and surrounded by Siddhas and immeasurable yogins,
<s>Pitāmaha</s>, having been informed by that king of mountains, came there.
The king of the gods, bearing a thousand eyes, with an exalted form adorned by divine necklaces and garlands,
mounted <s>Airāvata</s>, chief of all lordly elephants, whose streams were made by flowing rut-fluid;

children.text: āruhya sarvāmararāṭ sa vajraṃ bibhrat samāgātpurataḥ surāṇām ||
children.translated_text: bearing the thunderbolt, that king of all the immortals came at the head of the gods.
With a divine form superior in splendor and majesty, illuminating all the quarters, <s>Vivasvān</s>

children.text: haimaṃ vimānaṃ sacalatpatākam āruhya āgāttvaritaṃ javena ||
children.translated_text: mounted a golden aerial chariot with fluttering banners and came swiftly, with speed.
With brilliant earrings blazing with jewels, in an aerial chariot resembling the fire and the sun in splendor,
the Brahmin son of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, the <s>Āditya</s> bearing the name <s>Bhaga</s>, came there.
Stout-limbed, with a well-formed body and necklace, equal in power to his splendor, strength, and command,

children.text: daṇḍaṃ samādāya kṛtānta āgādāruhya bhīmaṃ mahiṣaṃ javena ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛtānta</s>, taking up his staff, came swiftly, mounted on a fearsome buffalo.
With a broad body rising like a great mountain, and with a lovely garment studded with gold and other jewels,
<s>Samīraṇa</s>, supporter of the whole universe, mounted an aerial chariot and came there.
Scorching all the lords of gods and Asuras, entering into surpassing brilliance,
<s>Vahni</s> approached, and in the midst of the lordly gods stood blazing, wearing the dress of a suitor.
With limbs blazing with many jewels, moving through the world in an excellent divine aerial chariot,
the lord of all wealth, that king of kings, came quickly.

children.text: āpyāyayan sarvasurāsureśānkāntyā ca veṣeṇa ca cārurūpaḥ
children.translated_text: Refreshing all the lords of gods and Asuras, lovely in radiance and in dress, with a beautiful form,
<s>Śaśin</s> mounted an aerial chariot variegated with blazing great jewels and arrived.
Dark-limbed, in wonderfully variegated dress, garlanded with fragrant wreaths fastened among all his garlands,

children.text: tārkṣyaṃ samāruhya mahīdhrakalpaṃ gadādharo 'sau tvaritaṃ sametaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that mace-bearing one swiftly came, mounted on <s>Tārkṣya</s>, who was like a mountain.

children.text: tathāśvinau devabhiṣagvarau tu ekaṃ vimānaṃ tvarayābhiruhya
children.translated_text: Likewise the two <s>Aśvins</s>, the best divine physicians, quickly mounted a single aerial chariot;
the two charming, splendidly and beautifully dressed heroes came to the assembly of the gods.
Great-souled <s>Śeṣa</s>, bearing a thousand hoods flashing with the color of fire, blazing with the fiery sunlight of crystals,
together with other Nāgas, mounted an aerial chariot and came there.
Of the sons of <s>Diti</s>, the great Asuras, shining like fire, the sun, <s>Śakra</s>, and the wind,

children.text: varānurūpaṃ pravidhāya veṣaṃ vṛndaṃ samāgātpurataḥ surāṇām ||
children.translated_text: a multitude came before the gods, having put on dress appropriate for suitors.

children.text: gandharvarājaḥ sa ca cārurūpī divyaṅgamo divyavimānacārī
children.translated_text: And that handsome king of Gandharvas, moving divinely and traveling in a divine aerial chariot,
came there by <s>Śakra</s>'s command, accompanied by hosts of Gandharvas and by Apsarases.
Other gods too, lords among the dwellers in heaven, each separately assuming beautiful dress,
came, mounted on the backs of aerial chariots, as did Gandharvas, Yakṣas, serpents, and Kiṃnaras.
There, in the midst of the lordly gods, <s>Śacīpati</s>, his form marked by supreme royal authority,
deluded by the force and sovereignty of command, made excessive effort in vain.
She was the cause of the three worlds, the source of the world's birth, and the mother of those gods and Asuras;

children.text: patnī ca śambhoḥ puruṣasya dhāmno gītā purāṇe prakṛtiḥ parārthā
children.translated_text: she was the wife of <s>Śambhu</s>, of the luminous Puruṣa, sung in the Purāṇa as <s>Prakṛti</s>, existing for the sake of another.
Because of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s anger, she, the wife of the supreme lord, came to <s>Himavat</s>'s house for the sake of the task.

children.text: evaṃ yatastāṃ na viduḥ sureśā mohastatastānpara āviveśa
children.translated_text: Thus, because the lords of the gods did not recognize her, a supreme delusion then entered them.

children.text: varārthamājagmurato vimūḍhā īśena yasmād vṛḍitāḥ kṛtāste ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, bewildered, they had come for the sake of choosing the bride, since they had been confounded by <s>Īśa</s>.
Then, while the <s>apsaras</s> danced gracefully and the companies of <s>gandharvas</s> made lovely music,
and while hosts of gods, asuras, and other heaven-dwellers stood there in various forms and costumes,
the goddess, standing on a jewel-and-gold-adorned aerial car, her limbs fanned by waving chowries,

children.text: sarvartupuṣpāṃ susugandhamālāṃ pragṛhya devī prasabhaṃ pratasthe ||
children.translated_text: took up a very fragrant garland made of flowers of every season and set forth impetuously.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: mālāṃ pragṛhya devyāṃ tu sthitāyāṃ devasaṃsadi
children.translated_text: When the goddess stood holding the garland in the assembly of the gods,
while the gods headed by <s>Śakra</s> had arrived for the <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice ceremony),
<s>Śambhu</s>, wishing to test the goddess, became a five-tufted child,
and the mighty lord suddenly lay asleep on the surface of her lap.

children.text: akasmādatha taṃ devī śiśuṃ pañcaśikhaṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: Then the goddess suddenly perceived that five-tufted child situated there,
and, knowing him through yogic concentration, she rejoiced, filled with affection.
Then she, pure in resolve and having obtained the true fruit she desired,

children.text: nirvṛteva tadā tasthau kṛtvā hṛdi tameva tu ||
children.translated_text: stood there as if fulfilled, keeping that very one in her heart.

children.text: tato dṛṣṭvā śiśuṃ devā devyā utsaṅgavartinam
children.translated_text: Then the gods, seeing the child situated on the goddess's lap,
consulted together, saying, "Who is this here?" and, deeply distressed, became angry.
<s>Vṛtrahā</s> raised his arm and summoned his thunderbolt against him,
but that raised arm of his remained fixed just as it was.
It had been paralyzed by <s>Śambhu</s>, the god of gods, in the form of a child,

children.text: vajraṃ kṣeptuṃ na śaśāka bāhuṃ cālayituṃ na ca ||
children.translated_text: and he was unable to hurl the thunderbolt or even to move his arm.

children.text: bhago nāma tato deva ādityaḥ kāśyapo balī
children.translated_text: Then the powerful god named <s>Bhaga</s>, an <s>Āditya</s> born of <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
deluded, lifted a blazing mace and wished to hurl it.
At that time the blessed lord paralyzed his arm too in the same way.
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, shaking his head, looked at him in anger,

children.text: tasyāpi śiraso devaḥ khālityaṃ pracakāra ha ||
children.translated_text: and the god made baldness appear on his head as well.
Deluded, <s>Pūṣan</s> gnashed his teeth and looked at <s>Śarva</s>,
and, when he was merely seen by <s>Śambhu</s>, his teeth fell out.

children.text: yamasya stambhito daṇḍastejo vahneḥ śaśeḥ prabhā
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>'s staff was paralyzed, as were the splendor of fire and the radiance of the moon,
the strength of wind, and likewise that of all the other heaven-dwellers there.
The mighty lord likewise paralyzed their strength, splendor, and yogic power.

children.text: atha teṣu sthiteṣvevaṃ manyumatsu sureṣu tu
children.translated_text: Then, while those gods remained in that state, full of wrath,
<s>Brahmā</s>, deeply alarmed, respectfully entered meditation
and recognized the lord of the gods, who was seated on <s>Umā</s>'s lap.
Recognizing the supreme lord, he quickly rose with reverence,
bowed to <s>Śambhu</s>'s feet, and <s>Pitāmaha</s> praised him
with ancient Sāman chants and holy, secret names.

children.text: ajastvamamaro deva sraṣṭā hartā vibhuḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: You are unborn; you are immortal, O god, creator, destroyer, all-pervading and supreme.
You are the principle of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, the imperishable object of meditation.

children.text: amṛtaṃ paramātmā ca īśvaraḥ kāraṇaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: You are immortality, the supreme self, <s>Īśvara</s>, and the great cause.
You are the maker of <s>Brahmā</s>, the creator of <s>Prakṛti</s>, the creator of all, the supreme lord.

children.text: iyaṃ ca prakṛtirdevī sadā te sṛṣṭikāraṇam
children.translated_text: And this goddess is <s>Prakṛti</s>, always the cause of your creation.
Having assumed the form of your wife, she has come as the cause of the world.
Reverence to you always, O lord, and reverence always to the goddess as well.
By your favor, O lord of gods, and by your command, creatures have been created by me.
These beings beginning with the gods have been created, but, foolish, they are deluded by your yogic power.
Show grace to them, so that they may become as they were before.

children.text: tata evaṃ tadā brahmā vijñāpya parameśvaram
children.translated_text: Having thus petitioned the supreme lord at that time,
the greatly radiant <s>Brahmā</s> said this to all those paralyzed gods:

children.text: mūḍhāḥ stha devatāḥ sarve nainaṃ budhyata śaṃkaram
children.translated_text: You are all deluded, O deities; you do not recognize this <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
the god of gods, who has come here, the very cause of my own origination.

children.text: ayaṃ rudro mahādevaḥ śarvo bhīmaḥ kapardimān
children.translated_text: This is <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, the matted-haired one,

children.text: ugra īśāna ātmā ca ajaḥ śaṃkara eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, the self, the unborn one, and <s>Śaṃkara</s> himself.

children.text: devadevaḥ paraṃ dhāma īśaḥ paśupatiḥ patiḥ
children.translated_text: He is the god of gods, the supreme abode, the lord, <s>Paśupati</s>, the master.
He is the creator of the world, the sustainer of the world, and the cause of the world's continued existence.
Go swiftly for refuge, O lords of the immortals,
together with me, to this very lord of gods, the imperishable supreme self.
Then all those heaven-dwellers, still paralyzed as they were,
bowed mentally to <s>Śarva</s> with hearts purified in devotion.
Then the god of gods, <s>Maheśvara</s>, became gracious to them,
and at once restored the bodies of the deities to their former state.
When the restraint of all the gods had thus taken place,
the lord of gods manifested a three-eyed form, supremely wondrous,
because of whose radiance those gods begged the mighty lord for sight.
The supreme lord of gods gave them a supreme eye, endowed with the power to see his own form,
and then they saw the lord.
Seeing the supreme lord bearing the third eye,

children.text: brahmādyā nemire tūrṇaṃ sarva eva sureśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the lords of the gods, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, quickly bowed.

children.text: tasya devī tadā hṛṣṭā samakṣaṃ tridivaukasām
children.translated_text: Then the delighted goddess, in the presence of the heaven-dwellers,
placed the wreath-garland at the feet of him of immeasurable splendor.
Crying, "Well done, well done!" those deities again
bowed to the mighty lord together with the goddess, their heads resting on the ground.
Then, in the meantime, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, grandfather of the worlds,
greatly radiant, said this to the great mountain <s>Himavat</s>:

children.text: ślāghyaḥ pūjyaśca vandyaśca sarveṣāṃ nastvamadya hi
children.translated_text: Today you are praiseworthy, worthy of worship, and worthy of reverence for us all,

children.text: śarveṇa saha sambandho yasya te 'bhūdayaṃ mahān
children.translated_text: for this great relationship with <s>Śarva</s> has come to be yours.

children.text: kriyatāṃ cāśu udvāhaḥ kimarthaṃ sthīyate param ||
children.translated_text: And let the wedding be performed quickly; why is there any further delay?
Then <s>Himavān</s>, bowing to that god, replied:

children.text: tvameva kāraṇaṃ deva yena śarvādayaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: You alone are the cause, O god, through whom this favor from <s>Śarva</s> has come to me.
The grace has arisen suddenly, and you yourself are indeed also its cause.
Therefore arrange the wedding, O <s>Pitāmaha</s>, in whatever way and manner is proper.

children.text: tata evaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā girirājñaḥ pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having heard this speech of the king of mountains, <s>Pitāmaha</s>

children.text: udvāhaḥ kriyatāṃ deva iti devamuvāca ha
children.translated_text: said to the god, 'O god, let the wedding be performed.'
<s>Śaṃkara</s>, guardian of the world, said to that god, 'As you wish.'

children.text: tatkṣaṇācca tato vyāsa brahmaṇā kalpitaṃ puram
children.translated_text: At that very moment, then, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, a city was fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s>
for the wedding of <s>Maheśa</s>, adorned with many kinds of jewels.
Jewels, variegated gems, gold, and pearls too
came there in embodied form and adorned that excellent city.
The wonderful emerald ground was splendid with golden pillars,
with shining crystal walls and hanging pearl garlands.
In that charming city of <s>Śiva</s>, made for the wedding,
the great-souled <s>Maheśa</s>, god of gods, shone forth.
There the moon and sun, like two great jewels, illuminated it together.
The wind, smelling the delightful fragrance there,
blew with a pleasant touch, gladdening devotion toward the Lord.
The four oceans were there, and the foremost gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s>,

children.text: devanadyo mahānadyaḥ siddhā munaya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the divine rivers, the great rivers, the siddhas, and the sages too.
All the gandharvas and apsarases, nāgas, yakṣas, together with rākṣasas,
guhyakas, sky-goers, and other kiṃnaras and divine cāraṇas

children.text: tumbururnārado hāhā hūhū caiva tu sāmagāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tumburu</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Hāhā</s>, and <s>Hūhū</s>, singers of sāman chants,
taking jewels and musical instruments, then came to that city.
The sages there, all of them rich in austerity, sang Vedic hymns,
and, with delighted minds, recited auspicious wedding mantras.
All the mothers of the world and all the daughters of the gods
sang there joyfully at the wedding of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
The six seasons, bringing happiness with many fragrances,
stood there together in embodied form, saying, 'It is <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s wedding.'
With peacocks crying out and dancing everywhere, delighted
by the deep rumbling sound of masses of dark clouds,
lit by flickering, tawny, clear streaks of lightning,
and adorned with cranes white like white kumuda flowers,
with newly sprouted mushroom shoots and lovely fresh shoots rising from creepers and trees,
and resounding with languid frogs awakened by the affection of auspicious streams of rainwater,
for passionate women whose minds were raised high in pride toward their beloveds,
even when they were firmly resolved, she shattered that pride in a moment with the charming cries of peacocks.
And with the lovely form of <s>Mahendra</s>'s bow, shining brightly in three colors and curved like a crescent moon,
standing everywhere near masses of clouds, she was greatly resplendent.
With charming winds, fragrant from the touch of varied flowers and very cool from contact with dense water,
she made the beautiful rows of locks of the divine women tremble.
Her moon-disc was covered by thundering clouds; lovely dūrvā grass had sprung up from fresh showers of water.
She was gazed at respectfully and eagerly by travelers' wives, dimmed by the smoke of their sighs.
Rich with the sound of swan anklets and with swelling breasts,
girdled with moving lightning-vines and clear lotus eyes,
with swans frightened by the sound of masses of black clouds and lotus tips bent down by the fall of pure streams of water,
her whole body adorned with fragrant flower pollen, the rainy season came in splendor for the wedding of the mountain's daughter.
Freed from her bodice of clouds, with breasts emerging from lotus buds,
resounding with swan anklets and making all the directions charming,
with broad sandbanks as her hips and the cries of sārasas as her girdle,
captivating with the full beauty of her blooming blue-lotus eyes,
with ripe bimba fruit as the openings of her lips and smiling with kunda-flower teeth,
adorned with a line of hair dark like fresh dark creepers,
with the excellent necklace of moonbeams spreading over the white mansion of her breast,
delighting the minds of all the dwellers in heaven,
speaking in the sweet sound sung by swarms of intoxicated bees,
and splendid with beautiful earrings made of clusters of trembling kumuda flowers,
holding as fingers the shoots that had sprung from the tips of red aśoka branches,
adorned with garments made from masses of those flowers,
with red lotuses as the tips of her feet and rows of jāti flowers as her nails,
with beautiful thighs like plantain trunks and a face like the moon,
touching the gods lovingly, like a beloved woman, with the foremost hands of wind
mixed with lotus filaments, lovely autumn arrived.
Freed from the fold of her dark cloud-bodice, with the full moon's disc as her face, with blue lotuses as her eyes and lovely breasts bursting from lotus buds,

children.text: nānāpuṣparajaḥsugandhipavanaprahlādanī cetasāṃ tatrāgātkalahaṃsanūpuraravā devyā vivāhe śarat ||
children.translated_text: delighting minds with breezes fragrant with the pollen of many flowers, autumn came there for the goddess's wedding, with the ringing of royal swans as her anklets.
The two seasons, winter and the cold season, of surpassing radiance, came,
flooding the rocks of the mountain with exceedingly cold waters.
When those two seasons had arrived, sprinkling powdery frost,
<s>Himavān</s>, that best of mountains, quickly shone as if made of silver.
With that dense and unfathomable fall of frost,

children.text: agādhena tadā reje kṣīroda iva sāgaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Himācala</s> then shone like the ocean, the Ocean of Milk.
In the snowy places <s>Himavān</s> destroyed the trees,
as a wicked man, when his purpose has been achieved, suddenly destroys good courtesies.
That mountain shone with peaks covered by layers of snow,
like a king of the earth with great white parasols of rich splendor.
The white, broad, splendid, and beautiful
lofty mountain-peaks shone like palaces.
In the caves of that lord of mountains, crowded with flocks of many-colored deer,
streams of snow, white as moonbeams, fell like streams of cow's milk.
The winds, their bodies raised with much flower-pollen and very cool from contact with particles of snow,
blew gently, slowly shaking the very thin garments of the chiefs of the hosts of immortals.
Springtime, free from the faults of rough wind and cold, with newly burst mango shoots as ear-ornaments,
quickly came to <s>Himavat</s> in order to serve the daughter of the mountain.
When that season had come to the mountain with the wish to serve at the wedding of the mountain-daughter,
trees, shrubs, and thickets, garlanded with flowers, appeared on every side.
Fragrant, lovely, and cool breezes, their forms covered with masses of pollen from the tips of varied flowers,

children.text: manobhavodrekakarāḥ surāṇāṃ surāṅganānāṃ ca muhuḥ samīrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: blew again and again, arousing desire in the gods and in the women of the gods.
And the lotus-ponds, full of clear water and furnished with buds of lotuses and blue lilies,

children.text: īṣat samudbhinnapayodharāgrā nāryo yathā ramyatamā babhūvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: became most beautiful, like women whose breast-tips had only just begun to swell.

children.text: ṛtoḥ svabhāvācca madodbhavācca phullāsu śākhāsu nilīnapakṣāḥ
children.translated_text: From the nature of the season and from the arising of intoxication, the male cuckoos, their wings hidden in flowering branches,
sang very sweetly, delighting the minds of the women of the Thirty Gods.
The lake-waters, neither too hot nor too cold, tawny with powdered filaments,
and resonant with pairs of cakravāka birds, were drunk by the delighted chief elephants of the gods.
The priyaṅgu plants and mango trees, and the priyaṅgus with the mangoes too,
shone with their flower-clusters as if threatening one another.
On the snow-white peaks, the tilaka trees with masses of flowers
shone like elders assembled with some purpose in view.
There the flowering aśoka creepers, resting upon śāla trees, gleamed
like passionate women whose bodies hung upon the necks of their lovers.
The mālatī creepers, with masses of creeper-flowers sung over by swarms of intoxicated bees,

children.text: parasparaṃ hi mālatyo bhāṣantya iva rejire ||
children.translated_text: indeed shone as if they were speaking with one another.

children.text: nīlāni nīlāmburuhaiḥ payāṃsi gaurāṇi gauraiśca sanāladaṇḍaiḥ
children.translated_text: The waters were made blue by blue water-lilies, white by white ones with their stalks,
and intensely red by red ones, whose petals were half bitten by maddened bees.
In the broad waters, lotus-groves appeared golden in some places, emerald-green without interruption in others,
and in other lakes furnished with beryl-colored stalks; they arose everywhere.
There were delightful step-ponds, adorned with lotuses and blue lilies,
filled with the cries of many kinds of birds, and lined with rows of golden steps.

children.text: śṛṅgāṇi tasya tu gireḥ karṇikāraiḥ supuṣpitaiḥ
children.translated_text: The high peaks of that mountain, with karṇikāra trees in full bloom
and thickly rising upon them, seemed golden, O sage.
All the directions became rosy with pāṭala trees whose flowers had slightly opened
and whose forms were shaken by the wind.
On the mountain, blue aśoka trees, like peaks of mountains of black collyrium,
grew in bloom, as if competing with one another.
And forests of kiṃśuka trees, resounding with cīruvāka birds,
appeared on every slope of the mountain.
At that time the beauty of <s>Himavat</s> with its thickets of tamāla trees
was like masses of dark clouds hidden in its clefts.
With campaka trees, profuse in flowers, very broad-branched, and rising high,
<s>Himācala</s> then shone exceedingly, amid the chatter of intoxicated male cuckoos.

children.text: śrutvā śabdam ṛtumadakalaṃ sarvataḥ kokilānāṃ cañcatpakṣāḥ sumadhurarutaṃ nīlakaṇṭhā vineduḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing everywhere the sweet cries of cuckoos, maddened by the season, the blue-necked peacocks, their wings quivering, cried out very sweetly.
Strengthened by their sounds, <s>Anaṅga</s>, with flower-bow and arrows in hand, stood ready to pierce the limbs of the women of the gods.
Summer too, with sharp sunlight and mostly warm bodies of water,
came to <s>Himācala</s> in order to serve at the goddess's wedding.
And that season also, with many trees bearing masses of flowers,
adorned the peaks of the snowy mountain on every side.
The winds of that season too, very delightful there,
blew with the fragrance of widespread pāṭala, kadamba, and arjuna flowers.
The step-ponds became filled with masses of blossoming lotuses, their forms reddened by filaments,
and their banks resounded with flocks of kalahaṃsa birds.
Likewise the kuravaka trees too, their forms pale with flowers,
appeared on all the peaks, attended by rows of bees.
And on the broad slopes of the mountain
the bakula trees sent forth charming flowers on every side.
Thus, with every tree varied by flowers and with regions charming from the cries of many kinds of birds,
the six seasons arrived for the splendor of the wedding of the daughter of the snowy mountain, O best of sages.
Then, when this gathering of all beings had thus begun,
and the place was filled with hundreds of various musical instruments, <s>Brahmā</s>, my father himself,
adorned the daughter of the mountain with a wealth of suitable ornaments,
and the world-supporter himself took her and caused her to enter the city.
Then once again <s>Brahmā</s> informed the mighty <s>Īśa</s>:
"I shall offer the oblation into the fire, standing in the office of officiating priest."
If you give me permission, this ritual procedure should be performed by me.
<s>Śaṃkara</s>, the god of gods and lord of the world, said to that god:
Whatever is desired, O lord of the gods, do that just as you wish.
I will do all of your command, O <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the world.
Then, bowing down with a delighted heart, <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandsire of the worlds,

children.text: hastaṃ devasya devyāśca yogabandhe yuyoja ha ||
children.translated_text: joined the hand of the god and of the goddess in the marriage bond.
And having himself made <s>Fire</s>, standing near with joined palms,
with the embodied Vedic hymns and great mantras present there,
he made offerings according to the prescribed rite: clarified butter and that nectar too.

children.text: triśca taṃ jvalanaṃ devaṃ kārayitvā pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: And he caused the god to circumambulate that fire three times clockwise.
Releasing the joining of hands, together with all the gods
and with all his mind-born sons, with his inner self overjoyed,
when the time of the wedding had been completed, he bowed down to the bull-bannered one.
By yoga alone, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, the marriage of those two, <s>Umā</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>,

children.text: udvāhaḥ sa paro vṛtto yaṃ devā na viduḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: then took place in that supreme way, which the gods never know at all.
Thus I have told you all this auspicious svayaṃvara,
and also the god's wedding, supremely wondrous as it is heard.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then, when the marriage of <s>Bhava</s> of immeasurable splendor had taken place,
the gods, together with the grandsire, attained incomparable joy
and praised <s>Maheśvara</s> with chosen words, bowing down.
Reverence to the mountain-liṅga; reverence indeed to the lord of mountains.
Reverence to the one swift as the wind, to the deformed-eyed one, and to the unconquered one.
Reverence to the destroyer of afflictions and the giver of auspicious prosperity.
Reverence to the blue-crested one; reverence to the husband of <s>Ambikā</s>.
Reverence to the one whose form is wind; reverence indeed to the one of a hundred forms.
Reverence to the one whose form is <s>Bhairava</s>, and to the one with misshapen eyes.
Reverence to the thousand-eyed one and to the thousand-footed one.
Repeated reverence to the secret of the Vedas and to the limb of the Vedas.
Reverence to the restrainer of <s>Śakra</s>'s arm and to the sprout of the Veda.
Repeated reverence to the lord of the moving and unmoving, and to the pacifier.
Reverence to the liṅga that lies in the waters, and to the liṅga extended at the end of an age.
Reverence to the one with a garland of skulls; reverence to the one wreathed with skulls.
Reverence to the one holding a skull in his hand, to the fanged one, and to the mace-bearer.
Reverence to the bearer of the three worlds and to the one whose chariot is the seven worlds.
Reverence to the one holding a khaṭvāṅga staff, and to the remover of the distress of the <s>Pramathas</s>.
Reverence to the remover of the sacrifice's head and to the taker-away of black hair.
Reverence to the one who struck down <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye and removed <s>Pūṣan</s>'s teeth.
Reverence to the bearer of bow, trident, sword, and mallet.
Reverence to the death of Time and to the third-eyed one.
And reverence to the end-maker of Death; reverence to the mountain-dweller.
Reverence to the one of golden seed and to the wearer of serpent earrings.
Reverence to the destroyer of <s>Vāḍvala</s>'s yoga and to the guru of yogins.
Reverence to the one whose eyes are the moon and sun, and to the one with an eye on his forehead.
Reverence to the one who delights in the cremation ground and grants boons in the cremation ground.
Repeated reverence to the lord of deities, to the three-eyed one.
Reverence to the one whose laughter is a hundred thunderbolts, to the protector of brahmins, and to the unconquered one.
Reverence always to the householder-sage, to the matted-haired celibate.
Reverence to the shaven and half-shaven one; reverence to the lord of beings.
Reverence to the one practicing austerity in the waters, and to the giver of yogic sovereignty.
Reverence to the peaceful, restrained one, the maker of dissolution and creation.
Reverence to the maker of favor, and repeated reverence to the maker of stability.
Reverence to <s>Rudra</s>, to the <s>Vasu</s>, to the <s>Āditya</s>, and to the <s>Aśvin</s>.

children.text: namaḥ pitre 'tha sādhyāya viśvedevāya vai namaḥ
children.translated_text: Reverence to the Father, then to the <s>Sādhya</s>, and reverence indeed to the <s>Viśvedeva</s>.

children.text: namaḥ śarvāya sarvāya ugrāya varadāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Reverence to <s>Śarva</s>, to the all-form, to the fierce one, and to the giver of boons.

children.text: namo bhīmāya senānye paśūnāṃ pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Reverence to the terrible one, to the general, and reverence to the lord of beings.
Reverence to the pure one, to the licking one, and indeed to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
Reverence to <s>Mahādeva</s>, to the wondrous one, and reverence to <s>Citraratha</s>.
Reverence to the primary principle, to the knowable, to the effect, and to the cause.
Reverence to you as <s>Puruṣa</s>, and to the one who fulfills the wish of <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Reverence to the one who brings about the qualities of <s>Pradhāna</s> through union with <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Reverence to the activator in every way of <s>Prakṛti</s> and of <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Reverence to the knower of what is done and undone, and to the giver of connection with fruit.
Reverence to the knower of time everywhere, and to the maker of regulation.

children.text: namo vaiṣamyakartre ca guṇānāṃ vṛttidāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Reverence to the maker of differentiation and to the giver of activity to the guṇas.
Reverence to you, O lord of the gods of gods; reverence to you, O originator of beings.

children.text: śivaḥ saumyaḥ sukho draṣṭuṃ bhava somo hi naḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: Be auspicious, gentle, and pleasant for us to behold; be gracious to us, O lord.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Thus that blessed god, lord of the world, husband of <s>Umā</s>,
being praised by all the gods, said this to the immortals:

children.text: draṣṭuṃ sukhaśca saumyaśca devānāmasmi bho surāḥ
children.translated_text: I am pleasant to behold and gentle for the gods, O gods.

children.text: varaṃ brūta yatheṣṭaṃ ca dātāsmi vadatānaghāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ask for whatever boon you wish; I am the giver, so speak, sinless ones.

children.text: tataste praṇatāḥ sarve ūcuḥ sabrahmakāḥ surāḥ
children.translated_text: Then all those gods, bowing down and accompanied by <s>Brahmā</s>, said:
Let this boon, O blessed one, remain in your own hand:

children.text: yadā kāryaṃ tadā nastvaṃ dāsyase varamīpsitam ||
children.translated_text: when there is need, then you will give us the boon we desire.
Saying to them, 'So be it,' <s>Hara</s> dismissed the gods,

children.text: lokāṃśca pramathaiḥ sārdhaṃ viveśa bhavanaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then, together with the <s>Pramathas</s>, entered his abode and the worlds.
Whoever sings this wondrous festival of <s>Hara</s> in the presence of deities and brahmins,
on changing the body, becomes happy, equal to a matchless <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: pārāśarya stavaṃ hīdaṃ śṛṇuyādyaḥ paṭheta vā
children.translated_text: O son of <s>Parāśara</s>, whoever hears or recites this hymn
goes to the heavenly world and is honored by the gods like the king of the immortals.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
When the god had entered the dwelling and was seated on the excellent seat,
that cruel <s>Manmatha</s>, outside, became intent on piercing the god.
He was joined with improper conduct, evil-souled, the lowest of his family,
tormenting all the worlds and lacking compassion toward everyone.
He was an obstacle-maker for the sages and for their restraints together with vows,
and he had come together with <s>Rati</s> in the form of one called <s>Cakra</s>.
Then, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, at that assailant who wished to pierce the lord of gods,
he looked disdainfully with his third eye.
Then fire born from his eye, with thousands of garlands of flame,
enveloped the husband of <s>Rati</s> and burned him with all his equipment.
As he was being burned, afflicted, he cried out piteously in a broken voice,

children.text: prasādayaṃśca taṃ devaṃ papāta sa mahītale ||
children.translated_text: and, propitiating that god, he fell upon the ground.
Quickly <s>Manmatha</s>, burner of the world, with limbs surrounded by fire,
fell down and in a moment was reduced to ashes.

children.text: patnī tu karuṇaṃ tasya vilalāpa suduḥkhitā
children.translated_text: But his wife, deeply distressed, lamented piteously for him,

children.text: devaṃ devīṃ ca duḥkhārtā ayācat karuṇāyatī ||
children.translated_text: and, anguished by sorrow and seeking compassion, entreated the god and the goddess.

children.text: tasyāśca karuṇāṃ śrutvā devau tau karuṇātmakau
children.translated_text: Hearing her piteous appeal, those two compassionate deities
looked upon her, consoled her in her distress, and spoke to her.
"This one has surely been burned, blessed lady; his arising will not take place here.

children.text: aśarīro 'pi te kāle kāryaṃ sarvaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Yet even without a body, in due time he will accomplish all your purpose.
But when <s>Viṣṇu</s> becomes the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>, fair one,

children.text: tadā tasya suto 'yaṃ syātpatiste sa bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: then this one will be his son, and he will become your husband."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: tataḥ sā taṃ varaṃ labdhvā kāmapatnī śubhānanā
children.translated_text: Then, having obtained that boon, the beautiful-faced wife of <s>Kāma</s>
went to the place she desired, filled with joy and free from weariness.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ dagdhvā sa kāmaṃ tu śaṃkaro mūḍhacetasam
children.translated_text: Thus, having burned <s>Kāma</s>, whose mind was deluded, <s>Śaṃkara</s>
spoke to the daughter of <s>Himavat</s> about the devotion of the best of sages:

children.text: vasiṣṭho nāma viprendro māṃ kṛtvā hṛdi tapyate
children.translated_text: "A lord among Brahmins named <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, having placed me in his heart, is practicing austerity.
I shall go to grant him a boon, O great-vowed one."

children.text: evamuktvā sa devīṃ tu bhaktiprītyā tadā vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to the goddess then, the powerful Lord, delighted by devotion and love,
went near the sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, who was practicing austerity.
Then he approached that foremost and best of excellent sages, the highest of ascetics,
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the tiger among seers, who was performing supreme austerity.
When a thousand years were complete, as he blazed like fire,

children.text: uvāca bhagavāngatvā brūhi kiṃ te dadāni te
children.translated_text: the blessed Lord went to him and said, "Speak; what shall I give you?

children.text: dadāmi divyaṃ cakṣuste paśya māṃ sagaṇaṃ dvija ||
children.translated_text: I grant you divine sight; see me with my gaṇas, O twice-born one."

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sa tu tamīśānaṃ praṇamya śirasā prabhum
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that <s>Īśāna</s>, he bowed with his head to the Lord,
and, placing his joined palms upon his head, praised him with a joyful face.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said:
Homage to the golden liṅga; homage indeed to the Vedic liṅga.
Homage to the thousandfold liṅga; homage indeed to the fiery liṅga.
Homage to the ancient liṅga; homage indeed to the liṅga of revelation.
Homage to the wind-liṅga; homage indeed to the Brahman-liṅga.
Homage to the liṅga of the three worlds; homage indeed to the burning liṅga.
Homage to the mountain-liṅga; homage indeed to the liṅga of stability.
Homage to the secret liṅga, to the liṅga above the seven continents.
Homage to the liṅga of every aim, to the liṅga whose members are all worlds.
Homage to the unmanifest liṅga; homage indeed to the liṅga of intelligence.
Homage to the liṅga of egoity; homage indeed to the liṅga of the elements.
Homage to the liṅga of the senses; homage to the liṅga of the subtle elements.
Homage to the liṅga of the person; homage indeed to the liṅga of being.
Homage to the liṅga of every aim; homage indeed to the liṅga of darkness.
Homage to the liṅga above passion; homage indeed to the liṅga of goodness.
Homage to the sky-liṅga; homage indeed to the fire-liṅga.
Homage to the liṅga above wind; homage indeed to the sound-liṅga.
Homage to the liṅga praised by Ṛg verses; homage indeed to the Yajur-liṅga.
Homage to you as the Atharvan-liṅga; homage indeed to the Sāman-liṅga.
Homage to the liṅga that is a limb of sacrifice; homage indeed to the sacrifice-liṅga.
Homage to you as the endless liṅga, to the liṅga followed by the gods.

children.text: diśa naḥ paramaṃ yogamapatyaṃ matsamaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Grant us supreme yoga, and likewise offspring equal to me;

children.text: brahma caivākṣayaṃ deva śamaṃ caiva paraṃ vibho
children.translated_text: also imperishable brahman, O god, and supreme tranquility, O mighty Lord,

children.text: akṣayatvaṃ ca vaṃśasya dharme ca matimakṣayām ||
children.translated_text: imperishability of my lineage and an undying inclination toward dharma.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Thus, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, when that blessed one had been praised by great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
he became pleased, and, being pleased, said this to him.
The blessed Lord said:
"I am pleased with you; I grant all this that is in your mind:
supreme, subtle yoga, imperishable and fulfilling every desire.
And a grandson equal to you, divine and endowed with the power of austerity and yoga,

children.text: dadāni te ṛṣiśreṣṭha pratibhāsyanti caiva te ||
children.translated_text: I grant you, best of seers; and these will indeed become manifest for you.
Self-control, tranquility, fame, contentment, and freedom from anger

children.text: nityaṃ tava bhaviṣyanti amaratvaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will always belong to you, as will immortality in every way.
Invulnerability, irresistibility, and imperishability will always be yours,
as well as the unimpaired state of your lineage, O Brahmin, and imperishable delight in dharma.
Ask for still other boons too; I shall grant them, best of seers."
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said:
"Blessed Lord, all the future is known to you, best of gods.

children.text: na syāddhi tattathā deva yathā vā manyase prabho ||
children.translated_text: For that would not be otherwise, O god, than as you think it, O Lord."
The god said:

children.text: bhaviṣyaṃ nānyathā kuryāditi me niścitā matiḥ
children.translated_text: "I would not make the future otherwise: such is my settled thought.
I am the maker of the future; how could one make that otherwise?

children.text: tathā tannātra saṃdeho vihitaṃ yadyathā mayā
children.translated_text: So it is; there is no doubt here, as each thing has been ordained by me."
Therefore he will again grant you favor; your son will be imperishable.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Having spoken thus, the god <s>Kapardī</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
vanished in a moment while that brahmin-sage was looking on.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
After receiving the boons, what son did the blessed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, our grandfather,
beget, equal to himself in splendor?
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
By that boon-giving of the god of gods, <s>Śūlin</s>,
he begot upon <s>Arundhatī</s> one endowed with the power of austerity and yoga,
a son most devoted to brahman, named <s>Śakti</s>, the eldest of a hundred sons.
From his very childhood, that great-souled descendant of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>
had devotion with a supreme mind toward <s>Govṛṣadhvaja</s>.
Once, for the sake of offspring, he worshiped <s>Umāpati</s>.
Pleased with him, <s>Mahādeva</s> said, "I am the giver of boons."
Then, seeing that lord, he said this with bowed face:

children.text: kena stoṣyāmi te deva yastvaṃ sarvajagatpatiḥ
children.translated_text: "How shall I praise you, O god, you who are the lord of the whole universe?
You sustain all the worlds by yourself, O mighty lord, according to due order.

children.text: tvameva bhoktā bhojyaṃ ca kartā kāryaṃ tathā kriyā
children.translated_text: You alone are the enjoyer and the thing enjoyed, the agent, the effect, and also the action;
likewise you are the producer, the produced, and production itself in every way.
O mighty lord, I desire my own self, bearing the name of son and equal to me in qualities,

children.text: icchāmi dattaṃ deveśa eṣa me dīyatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to be given by you, O lord of gods; let this boon be granted to me."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
To him who spoke thus, the god, smiling, the best of speakers,

children.text: uvāca vacasā vyāsa diśaḥ sarvā vinādayan ||
children.translated_text: spoke in a voice that made all the quarters resound, O <s>Vyāsa</s>:

children.text: tvayāhaṃ yācitaḥ śakte sa ca te sambhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: "You have asked me, O <s>Śakti</s>; and that son will come into being for you,
equal to you, knowing all the Vedas, and your own, O foremost sage.
As a seed-self, arisen by itself in the form of a sprout,
does not, while being the seed-self, become some other transformation,
so this self of yours, arisen from self and called offspring,
will not, by its own self, become something that has passed into another transformation."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: evamuktvā tu taṃ devaḥ prahasya ca nirīkṣya ca
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to him, and having smiled and looked at him,
the exceedingly radiant yogin suddenly went into invisibility.
When <s>Mahādeva</s> had gone, <s>Śakti</s>, your grandfather,
reflected fully on that speech and thought, "It is just so."
Then, after a very long time had passed, O you of auspicious vows,
he too, made potent by great austerity and shining like fire,
placed an excellent embryo in <s>Adṛśyantī</s>, O very wise one.
When she had conceived, king <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>, enraged,
his mind seized by a rākṣasa, devoured the seer.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: kasmāt sa rājā tamṛṣiṃ cakhāda tapasānvitam
children.translated_text: Why did that king eat the seer, who was endowed with austerity?

children.text: rakṣasā sa kimarthaṃ ca hṛtacetā abhavannṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And for what reason did the ruler become deprived of his mind by a rākṣasa?
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
There was a king, for whom <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> served as sacrificial priest, named <s>Mitrasaha</s>, a lord,
the strong son of <s>Sudāsa</s>, equal in splendor to <s>Indra</s> and the moon.

children.text: tam āgamyocivāñ śaktiś cariṣye dīkṣito vratam
children.translated_text: Coming to him, <s>Śakti</s> said, "Consecrated, I shall undertake a vow.

children.text: tatra me niśi rājendra sadaiva piśitāśanam ||
children.translated_text: For that, O king, when I come here at night, always give me meat as food,
pure and endowed with every quality,
with no refusal attached, once, and in seclusion."
Told by him, "So be it," that great-minded one went away.
Then at that time a rākṣasa became hidden within that king,
and for his sake he did not then give orders to the cook, O best of sages.
When the day had passed, dear one, remembering it and self-restrained,
the lord of men summoned the cook and spoke like one distressed.
<s>Saudāsa</s> said:
"O <s>Amṛtavasu</s>, this morning I promised to the wise son of my guru
meat, a meal prepared for the night.

children.text: tatkuruṣva tathā kṣipraṃ kālo no nātyagād yathā ||
children.translated_text: Prepare it quickly in such a way that the time does not pass us by."
Thus addressed, the cook <s>Amṛtavasu</s> then said:
"O king, you did not tell us beforehand, O foremost of men.
At present there is no meat, not even a little of what is desired.
Because the meat itself was scant, because many people ate it,
and because it was given out without measure, nothing remains."
The king said:

children.text: jāne sarvopayogaṃ ca jāne cāduṣṭatāṃ tava
children.translated_text: "I know that everything has been used, and I know that you are not at fault.

children.text: jāne stokaṃ ca piśitaṃ kāryaṃ cedaṃ tathāvidham
children.translated_text: I know that the meat is little, and that this duty is of such a kind.

children.text: mṛgyatāṃ piśitaṃ kṣipraṃ labdhavyaṃ yatra manyase ||
children.translated_text: Search quickly for meat wherever you think it can be obtained."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Thus addressed, <s>Amṛtavasu</s> undertook a great effort.
Searching properly for meat, he still did not find it anywhere.
When he had not obtained flesh, he went by night to the great king
and spoke this meaningful statement to the lord of men:

children.text: rājanna piśitaṃ tv asti pure 'smiñchuci karhicit
children.translated_text: "O king, there is nowhere in this city any pure meat.
I am exhausted from searching. Command me: what shall I do for you?"
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
When the lord of men was thus addressed by the cook at that time,

children.text: novāca kiṃcittaṃ sūdaṃ tūṣṇīmeva babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: he said nothing to the cook, but simply remained silent.
Seeing that opening, a rākṣasa named <s>Rudhira</s>, impelled by <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
entered into the lord of men.
Then, possessed by that evil-minded rākṣasa <s>Rudhira</s>,
the brilliant king spoke softly into the cook's ear:
"Go now and bring human flesh from somewhere,
or donkey flesh, or camel flesh; you may prepare anything at all.

children.text: kimasau jñāsyate rātrau tvayā bhūyaśca saṃskṛtam
children.translated_text: How will he know at night, when it has again been prepared by you?"
And make it savory and fragrant; carry it out quickly.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Thus addressed by him, he then took human flesh,
O <s>Vyāsa</s>, from some dead, abandoned man who had wronged the king.
Then, at midnight,
he saw a best of sages, radiant like the sun and appearing like a hundred fires.
Having honored him properly with arghya, water for the feet,
and the finest excellent seat, he set food before him.
When that great ascetic touched the food that had been brought,
he became angry and, furious, spoke to the king as if burning him up.
<s>Śakti</s> said:
Lowest of kings, food fit for rākṣasas

children.text: na dīyate vidhijñena tvaṃ tu māmavamanyase ||
children.translated_text: is not given to brahmins by one who knows the rule; but you insult me.
Since you desire to give me this rākṣasa-like food,
therefore, by that act, you shall become a man-eater.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
When he had been addressed thus, the fiery king reflected on that matter,
and, his eyes reddened with anger and his mind possessed by a rākṣasa, said:
Since your reverence told me, "May you become a man-eater,"
therefore I shall eat you, O twice-born, together with your brothers.
After eating you, then, freed from the curse, for the sake of purification,
I shall practice pure austerity, restraining the host of my senses,
and, with your father’s permission, I shall dwell in heaven as I wish.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: tataḥ sa rājā svaṃ rājyamutsṛjya saha bhāryayā
children.translated_text: Then that king, abandoning his own kingdom together with his wife,
entered the forest, and there he became a mighty man-eater.
There, first, he devoured the great sage <s>Śakti</s> himself,
and then his hundred brothers, while <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> himself looked on.

children.text: tataḥ putravadhaṃ ghoraṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmasutaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the terrible slaughter of his sons, the lord, son of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: notsasarja tadā krodhaṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ kauśikaṃ prati
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> did not then let loose anger against <s>Kauśika</s>;
he was simply overwhelmed by great grief for his sons.

children.text: sa baddhvā mahatīṃ kaṇṭhe śilāṃ brahmasutaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: The lord, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, tied a great stone to his neck,
and, casting himself into a river, it ran apart in a hundred channels from fear;
the firm-vowed sages call that river <s>Śatadrū</s>.
Again, having bound himself with strong nooses, the self-controlled one cast himself into another river;
there he became free from bonds, and from then on that river was <s>Vipāśā</s>.
Then, reaching a forest, fasting and master of his senses,
he remained there living on air, tormenting his own body.
Then he heard the melodious sound of one person reciting the Vedas,
and there at once he regained his meditative composure.
Then a woman lovely in every limb, with full, high breasts,
stood before him: the wife of <s>Śakti</s>, her face and eyes wretched.

children.text: tāmuvāca kutastvaṃ vai kasyaiṣa śrūyate dhvaniḥ
children.translated_text: He said to her, "From where have you come, and whose sound is this that is heard?"

children.text: sovāca dīnayā vācā rudatī śvaśuraṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: Then, weeping, she said in a mournful voice to her father-in-law:
<s>Adṛśyantī</s> said:
Ever since you went out from the hermitage in grief for your sons, O guru,
from that time onward I have followed your reverence devotedly, though unseen.

children.text: adhīyānasya caivāyaṃ dhvaniḥ putrasya te vibho
children.translated_text: And this is the sound of your son’s son,

children.text: udarasthasya te sūnormā duḥkhe tvaṃ manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: your descendant in my womb, reciting, O lord; do not set your mind on sorrow.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
"Now, child, I have hope of life," he said;

children.text: kṣāntiṃ dhṛtiṃ ca saṃsthitya prayayāv āśramaṃ muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: established in forbearance and steadiness, the sage went to the hermitage.
As he was going to that hermitage, he saw on the path King
<s>Saudāsa</s>, his limbs smeared with fat and blood, red-eyed.
As he rushed at him with speed, the sage paralyzed him with mantras,
and then a supremely terrible rākṣasa came out of his body.
And he said to it, "Wicked one, I could burn you together with your kin;

children.text: dagdhena ca tvayā kiṃ me gaccha mukto 'si durmate ||
children.translated_text: but what use have I for you when burned? Go; you are released, fool."

children.text: tataḥ sa mukto dīnātmā rākṣasaḥ krūrakarmakṛt
children.translated_text: Then, released, that wretched rākṣasa, doer of cruel deeds,
fearfully bowed his head and went to <s>Kuśika</s>'s side.

children.text: gate niśācare rājā praṇamya śirasā munim
children.translated_text: When the night-roamer had gone, the king bowed his head to the sage,
and then sought to appease him; and he spoke these meaningful words:
There is no fault in you, O king of kings, for you were possessed by a rākṣasa;

children.text: kṛtāntena hatāḥ putrā nimittaṃ tatra rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: my sons were slain by fate; the rākṣasa was merely the instrument there.
Rule the kingdom of your father and grandfather, O king of kings, O lord;

children.text: brūhi kiṃ vā priyaṃ te 'dya karomi narapuṃgava ||
children.translated_text: or tell me what pleasing thing I may do for you today, O bull among men.
The king said:
O blessed unfailing one, I desire a son produced by you
in this queen, a great-souled one; do this kindness for me.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Saying, "So be it," that great-vowed sage then

children.text: putraṃ ca śoṇakaṃ nāma janayāmāsa nirvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: joyfully begot in that wife a son named <s>Śoṇaka</s>.

children.text: taṃ śoṇakaṃ tato rājye svaṃ putramabhiṣicya saḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having consecrated that <s>Śoṇaka</s>, his own son, in the kingship,
he quickly went to the forest with his wife, intent on austerity.
In time, too, a mighty son of <s>Śakti</s> was born for <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
a son by <s>Adṛśyantī</s>, named <s>Parāśara</s>.
The wise boy then regarded <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> as his father,
and repeatedly uttered, "Father, father," to his father’s elder.
Then one day, learning that his pure father had been eaten by a rākṣasa,
he then, with austerity and mantras, performed a rākṣasa-sacrifice.
There he, great in splendor, offered into the fire fifty crores
of rākṣasas, doers of cruel deeds; then <s>Brahmā</s> quickly came.
The lord, having approached and honored his son, together with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
and with the seers and deities, said this to <s>Parāśara</s>:
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Those deities of yours were falling through sacrifices preceded by mantras;
for this eighth station is such a primal place of the gods.
<s>Parāśara</s> said:
I, together with all the gods,
having burned the others, shall establish worlds there; there is no doubt.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: tasyaivaṃ garvitaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvā devaḥ pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this proud speech of his, the god, the Grandfather,
spoke these words in a gentle voice, soothing him:
The Grandfather said:
This has been done; there is no doubt, O great-minded one, just as you say.
Yet all this should be forgiven, out of the wish to do what is dear to us.

children.text: yaiste pitā mahābhāga bhakṣitaḥ saha sodaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Those by whom your father, O greatly fortunate one, was devoured together with his brothers,

children.text: ta evāgnau ca hotavyā viśvāmitrasya paśyataḥ
children.translated_text: they alone are to be offered into the fire while <s>Viśvāmitra</s> looks on;

children.text: anyeṣāṃ svasti sarvatra devānāṃ saha rākṣasaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for all others, may there be well-being everywhere, for the gods together with the rākṣasas.
Scorched by that resolve, he set forth the root of his anger;
O greatly fortunate child, restrain <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s son.
All the gods, with hands joined, bowed down to you, the great sage,

children.text: ṛṣayaścaiva te sarve vāgbhis tuṣṭuvire tadā ||
children.translated_text: and all those seers then praised you with words.
Then the greatly radiant one honored their words in return,
and, while <s>Viśvāmitra</s> looked on, spoke this in a melodious voice:

children.text: ya eṣāṃ brāhmaṇo vāpi kṣatriyo vā durātmavān
children.translated_text: Whatever evil-minded brahmin or kṣatriya among these
takes the side of the rākṣasas and makes retaliation,
him too, here itself, being enraged and endowed with the strength of ascetic yoga,
I shall strike down through the yoga of austerity and offer into the blazing fire.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then the gods, together with the gandharvas and with the Grandfather at their head,
knowing that power of his, honored <s>Parāśara</s>.
And when those wicked rākṣasas had then been offered,
he then drew the sattra to a close, with <s>Brahmā</s>'s approval.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: ya imaṃ śrāddhakāle vā daive karmaṇi vā dvijān
children.translated_text: Whoever, being pure, causes brahmins to hear this at the time of a śrāddha or in a rite for the gods,

children.text: śrāvayeta śucirbhūtvā na taṃ hiṃsanti rākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the rākṣasas do not harm him.
When a brahmin hears this account of <s>Parāśara</s>, born from no base source, born from pure speech and ritual action,

children.text: niśāmya vipraḥ kulasiddhisambhavaṃ na rākṣasaṃ gacchati yonisambhavam ||
children.translated_text: and arising for the attainment of lineage, he does not go to a birth in a rākṣasa womb.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ tava pitā vyāsa rakṣaḥsattraṃ samāharat
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, your father brought the rākṣasa-sattra to an end,
and after completing it he again practiced radiant austerity.
Coming to him, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, shining like the sun through austerity,
being filled with affection, spoke these meaningful, imperishable words:
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said:
The fathers, desiring sons, having performed exceedingly hard austerity,
used to produce a son endowed with austerity and knowledge.
This son of ours, possessed of knowledge and endowed with austerity,

children.text: kariṣyati gatiṃ caiva iti vedavido viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: will carry on our lineage and our destiny too: so the knowers of the Veda know.
You are endowed with austerity, possessed of knowledge, and endowed with fame;

children.text: putraḥ putravatāṃ śreṣṭho vihīnaḥ prajayā vibho ||
children.translated_text: you are a son, the best of those who have sons, O lord, yet without offspring.
Therefore, O best of vow-observers, discharge your debt to the fathers;
quickly beget a son, whether superior or equal.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Thus addressed by the immeasurable-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, that radiant one
reached Mount <s>Maināka</s> and practiced very difficult austerity.

children.text: tasya kālena mahatā tapasā bhāvitasya tu
children.translated_text: After a long time, when he had been purified by austerity,

children.text: umāpatirvaraṃ prādātsa ca vavre sutaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: the husband of <s>Umā</s> granted him a boon, and he chose an auspicious son.
Having obtained the boon, he came back and sought, for the sake of a son,

children.text: kṣetraṃ supariśuddhaṃ ca svaputro yatra sambhavet ||
children.translated_text: a very pure field in which his own son might be born.
Wandering about, he then saw <s>Kālī</s>, who had become the daughter of the king of fishermen,
a maiden connected with the fathers, divine in form.
She had been born from the womb of a fish, formerly through eating <s>Vasu</s>'s seed,
the excellent apsaras <s>Adrikā</s>, auspicious and filled with <s>Brahmā</s>'s splendor.

children.text: tasyāṃ sa janayāmāsa varaṃ dattvā mahātapāḥ
children.translated_text: In her the great ascetic begot, after granting a boon,
you, the source of austerities and the promulgator of śrauta and smārta rites.
And your son was <s>Śuka</s>, the best of those who know yoga;

children.text: tasya putrāśca catvāraḥ kanyā caikā sumadhyamā ||
children.translated_text: his sons were four, and there was one slender-waisted daughter.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
How did the enmity of <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> arise,
and how again did it pass away? I wish to know this.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: parāśare tu garbhasthe vipratvaṃ gādhije gate
children.translated_text: While <s>Parāśara</s> was still in the womb, and when <s>Gādhi</s>'s son had attained brahminhood,
on the <s>Sarasvatī</s> in <s>Kurukṣetra</s> were the hermitages of them both.
There, remembering the enmity, the wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
while <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> looked on, slew a hundred sons in anger.
Then that mighty sage, the powerful <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, said there
to the <s>Sarasvatī</s> in private: O great river, bring me <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>
here as he is bathing, swept along by your great current.

children.text: saivamuktā tu taṃ gatvā vasiṣṭhaṃ prāha duḥkhitā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, she went to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and, distressed, told him
what <s>Gādhi</s>'s son had said; and he said to the great river:

children.text: evaṃ kuru mahābhāge māṃ nayasva yathepsitam
children.translated_text: Do so, O greatly fortunate one; take me as you wish.

children.text: mā te krūraḥ sa gādheyaḥ śāpaṃ dadyāt sudustaram ||
children.translated_text: May that cruel son of <s>Gādhi</s> not give you a curse very hard to overcome.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: gādheyasya tataḥ sā tu juhvato 'gniṃ divākare
children.translated_text: Then, while <s>Gādhi</s>'s son was offering into the fire, when the sun
had reached midday, that auspicious river quickly brought <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> by her current.
Seeing that best of sages, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, carried away by the current,
He said: "Since he was swiftly carried off by you through deceit,
therefore, by this deed, you shall have blood as your water."
Cursed by <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, that river, giver of happiness to the worlds,
carried blood, and also flesh and fat.
Then, when sages had come there in connection with the <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred fords),
they showed favor to her, through which she became a river of clear water.
Then, after a long time, by the power of great austerity,

children.text: vasiṣṭhasya ca tāṃ kṣāntiṃ jñātvā sa ṛṣipuṃgavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and knowing that forbearance of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, that bull among sages,
<s>Viśvāmitra</s>, of great splendor, abandoned his hostility toward <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
Thus those two excellent sages abandoned their mutual enmity.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: ya imaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ brāhmaṇāñ śrāvayīta vā
