children.translated_text: Whoever regularly hears this, or causes brahmins to hear it,
crosses difficult, hard-to-cross dangers with tireless manly effort.
Endowed with modesty, manliness, generosity, graceful conduct, and courage, and wearing bright, lovely garments,
he becomes equal to the king of all the immortals and sports in <s>Tripiṣṭapa</s> as he himself desires.
Thus, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, that was what happened between <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>:

children.text: vairaṃ samāptaṃ lokānāṃ hitārthaṃ punareva ca ||
children.translated_text: their enmity came to an end, again for the welfare of the worlds.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
Tell me fully and without omission everything that the two lords of gods, <s>Umā</s> and <s>Hara</s>,
did when they came together, O great sage.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
When the faultless <s>Umā</s> and <s>Hara</s> came together with one another,
they joined a brahmin of the lineage of <s>Śālaṅka</s> with a boon.
And that son, not born from a womb, after propitiating the supreme lord,
obtained equality with <s>Rudra</s> and shone as the great lord of the <s>gaṇas</s>.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: kathaṃ nandī samutpannaḥ kathaṃ cārādhya śaṃkaram
children.translated_text: How was <s>Nandī</s> born? And how, after propitiating <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
did he attain equality with <s>Śambhu</s>, and also the office of doorkeeper?
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: abhūdṛṣiḥ sa dharmātmā śilādo nāma vīryavān
children.translated_text: There was a righteous sage, powerful, named <s>Śilāda</s>.
His livelihood was by gleanings; therefore he came to be called <s>Śilāda</s>.
That brahmin saw his ancestors hanging in a pit,
their line cut off, having fallen into a dreadful hell.
They, desiring offspring, said to him: "Worship the imperishable god, the lord of the world;
worship <s>Mahādeva</s> for the sake of a son, O best of twice-born men."
After he had performed austerity for a thousand years, the trident-bearer,
<s>Śarva</s>, <s>Soma</s>, surrounded by the <s>gaṇas</s>, said, "I am the giver of boons."
Seeing that <s>Soma</s>, lord of lords, he bowed at the feet of the lord,
and with a voice choked by joy he praised the lord of the gods:
Reverence to the highest god, to great-souled <s>Maheśa</s>;
reverence to the creator of all the lords of gods, to the lord of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Reverence to the destroyer of <s>Kāma</s>'s body, to the cause of the arising of <s>yoga</s>;
reverence to the mountain-dweller, to the creator who is reached by meditation.

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ pataye nityaṃ devānāṃ pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Reverence always to the lord of sages; reverence to the lord of gods.

children.text: vedānāṃ pataye caiva yogināṃ pataye namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And reverence indeed to the lord of the Vedas; reverence to the lord of yogins.
Constant reverence to <s>Pradhāna</s>; reverence to the principle called immortal.

children.text: varadāya ca bhaktānāṃ namaḥ sarvagatāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Reverence to the giver of boons to devotees, and reverence to the all-pervading one.
Reverence to the creator of the subtle elements, senses, gross elements, transformations,

children.text: sraṣṭre ca pataye caiva namaśca prabhaviṣṇave ||
children.translated_text: and the qualities, and also to their lord; reverence to the mighty one.

children.text: jagataḥ pataye caiva jagatsraṣṭre namaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: Reverence always to the lord of the world and to the creator of the world;
constant reverence to the lord of <s>Prakṛti</s>, to the one who goes beyond <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Constant reverence to the lord, to the power attained by <s>yoga</s>,
to the source and destruction of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and to the giver of every desire.
Constant reverence to the refuge; reverence to the one whose limbs are smeared with ash.
Reverence to you, whose hand holds an iron implement; reverence to the lord of splendors.
Reverence to the bearer of sun, wind, fire, water, moon, sky, and earth,
who stands always eternal; reverence to the creator of the three worlds.
O god, how can there be any rest from praising you, who are to be praised,
when you alone are the cause of this world's continuance and destruction?
O lord of gods, I am without refuge and seek refuge from you;
taking hold of your supreme grace, become the giver of boons, O maker of all.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: yaḥ stotrametadakhilaṃ paṭhate dvijanmā prātaḥ śucirniyamavānpurato dvijānām
children.translated_text: The twice-born man who recites this whole hymn in the morning, pure, disciplined, before brahmins,
is not harmed by <s>brahmarākṣasas</s>, night-wanderers, <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, two-footed beings, serpents, or <s>Pūtanā</s>-spirits.
Then that blessed god, being praised together with <s>Umā</s>,
said, "I am the giver of boons. Speak what is in your mind."
When the god had spoken thus, <s>Śilāda</s> worshipped him then,

children.text: uvāca cedaṃ deveśaṃ sa vācā sajjamānayā ||
children.translated_text: and with a faltering voice he said this to the lord of gods:

children.text: bhagavanyadi tuṣṭo 'si yadi deyo varaśca me
children.translated_text: "Blessed lord, if you are pleased, and if a boon is to be given to me,
I desire a son equal to yourself, deathless and not born from a womb."
Then the three-eyed god, pleased when thus addressed,
said to him, "So be it," and vanished right there.
When that great archer had gone, the highly honored sage
returned to his own hermitage and then told the sages.
Praised by them, and then in time, O excellent sage,
wishing to sacrifice, he ploughed his own sacrificial ground with a plough.
As that furrow was being ploughed, there arose from it
a boy, seen to be like the fire of dissolution.

children.text: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā tathodbhūtaṃ kumāraṃ dīptatejasam
children.translated_text: Seeing that boy, thus arisen and blazing with splendor,
he thought, "This is a <s>rākṣasa</s>," and out of fear did not approach him.
The boy too, arisen in that way, saw his father blazing with splendor.
He approached, dejected in spirit, and said, "Father, father!"
But when, although he was being addressed as "father," he did not welcome him,
then <s>Vāyu</s>, in the sky, spoke to <s>Śilāda</s> in a pleasant voice.
<s>Vāyu</s> said:
O son of <s>Śālaṅkāyana</s>, that son of yours who was formerly given by the god <s>Śambhu</s>,

children.text: ayonijaḥ purā dattaḥ sa eṣa pratinandaya ||
children.translated_text: born without a womb, is this very one. Welcome him.
Since this child is always a maker of joy for you, O best of twice-born men,
therefore this son of yours will be called <s>Nandī</s> by name.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then, at <s>Vāyu</s>'s words, he embraced <s>Nandin</s>.
Taking him to his own hermitage, he brought there that increaser of joy,
and he performed for him the rites beginning with the cūḍā and the upanayana.
After doing so, he taught him all the Vedas together with their ancillary sciences, without remainder,
as well as Ayurveda, Dhanurveda, Gandharva lore, and the science of words.
He taught what concerns the behavior of elephants and the marks of men and women,
all the crafts, and also the knowledge of omens.

children.text: bhūtagrāmacikitsāṃ ca mātṝṇāṃ caritaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: He taught the healing of the host of beings, and what concerns the conduct of the Mothers,
and all the movements and behavior of serpents, whatever they may be.
O <s>Vyāsa</s>, in just five years he had learned all of this.
He was skillful, pure, undaunted in spirit, pleasant-spoken, and free from envy,
always beloved by all people, and a delight to the mind and eyes.

children.text: tasyātha saptame varṣe ṛṣī divyau tapodhanau
children.translated_text: Then, in his seventh year, two divine seers rich in austerity,
both of great splendor, came to <s>Śilāda</s>'s hermitage.
After honoring them according to rule, <s>Śilāda</s>, of very great austerity,
saw that they were comfortably seated on seats with the highest honor.
They were named <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, endowed with the power of austerity and yoga,
and they understood all beings in the three worlds, both moving and unmoving.
Then, having been permitted by them, he sat down on an excellent seat.
Seated there, delighted, he praised them with pleasing words.
They asked him, "Is your auspicious son, who gives you satisfaction, well?
Is he intent on recitation? Is he the continuation of <s>dharma</s>?
Does the boy never disrespect elders or teachers?
Is he disciplined, and does he give satisfaction to the good?"
Thus addressed, the radiant <s>Śilāda</s>, affectionate toward his son,
spoke of him as virtuous and as one who properly increases the family lineage.

children.text: tamāhūya sa tuṣṭyā tu putraṃ nandinamacyutam
children.translated_text: Then, joyfully calling his steadfast son <s>Nandin</s>,
he made <s>Nandin</s> bow his head at the feet of the two.

children.text: tau tu tasyāśiṣaṃ devau prayuṅkto dharmanityatām
children.translated_text: Those two divine ones gave him their blessing: constant adherence to <s>dharma</s>,
devotion in serving his teacher, and likewise imperishable worlds.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then, noticing that blessing of the two gods,
<s>Śilāda</s> dismissed <s>Nandin</s> and, afraid, questioned the two best of seers.
<s>Śilāda</s> said:
Revered sages, you are truthful and know the course of all embodied beings.

children.text: kimarthaṃ mama putrasya dīrghamāyur ubhāv api
children.translated_text: Why did neither of you best of sages properly bestow
a blessing of long life upon my son?
<s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> said:
Dear one, this son of yours, esteemed by all, is short-lived.
From now he will sustain his life for only one more year.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then, scorched by grief and distressed, he fell to the ground.
After sending away the two excellent seers, he lamented alone.

children.text: tasya śokādvilapataḥ svaraṃ śrutvā sutaḥ śubhaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the voice of him lamenting from grief, his auspicious son
<s>Nandin</s> came, and then saw his father deeply distressed.
<s>Nandin</s> said:

children.text: kena tvaṃ tāta duḥkhena dūyamānaḥ prarodiṣi
children.translated_text: Father, by what sorrow are you being tormented, so that you weep?

children.text: duḥkhaṃ te kuta udbhūtaṃ jñātumicchāmyahaṃ pitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From where has this sorrow of yours arisen? I wish to know, father.
<s>Śilāda</s> said:

children.text: putra tvaṃ kila varṣeṇa jīvitaṃ samprahāsyasi
children.translated_text: Son, you are said to be about to give up your life within a year.
Those two sages spoke thus, and therefore anguish has entered me.
<s>Nandin</s> said:

children.text: satyaṃ devaṛṣī tāta na tāv anṛtam ūcatuḥ
children.translated_text: Father, the divine seers are truthful; those two did not speak falsely.

children.text: tathāpi tu na mṛtyurme prabhaviṣyati mā śucaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even so, death will not prevail over me. Do not grieve.
<s>Śilāda</s> said:

children.text: kiṃ tapaḥ kiṃ parijñānaṃ ko yogaḥ kaḥ śramaśca te
children.translated_text: What austerity, what special knowledge, what yoga, or what effort do you have,
by which you will deceive death when it is at hand? Tell me.
<s>Nandin</s> said:

children.text: na tāta tapasā mṛtyuṃ vañcayiṣye na vidyayā
children.translated_text: Father, I shall not deceive death by austerity, nor by knowledge.
By the grace of <s>Mahādeva</s> I shall conquer death, and in no other way.

children.text: drakṣyāmi śaṃkaraṃ devaṃ tato mṛtyurna me bhavet
children.translated_text: I shall behold the god <s>Śaṅkara</s>; then death will not exist for me.

children.text: naṣṭe mṛtyau tvayā sārdhaṃ ciraṃ vatsyāmi nirvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When death has been destroyed, I shall dwell long and happily together with you.
<s>Śilāda</s> said:
After I had practiced exceedingly difficult austerity for a thousand years,

children.text: mahādevaḥ purā dṛṣṭo labdhastvaṃ me yataḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahādeva</s> was formerly seen by me, and you were obtained by me from him, my son.
But you, not greatly matured in austerity, have only one year.
How will you behold <s>Mahādeva</s>? This I wish to know.
<s>Nandin</s> said:

children.text: na tāta tapasā devo dṛśyate na ca vidyayā
children.translated_text: Father, the god is not seen by austerity, nor by knowledge.
<s>Parameśvara</s> is seen by a pure mind and by devotion.
If you release me, I shall go and soon behold the three-eyed one,

children.text: draṣṭā tāta na saṃdeho visṛjāśu tatastu mām ||
children.translated_text: father; there is no doubt. Therefore quickly let me go.
If <s>Yama</s> were to come upon me while I stood before your eyes, as you expect,
he would not strike me. Therefore, father, I shall go from here.

children.text: tiṣṭhantaṃ vā śayānaṃ vā dhāvantaṃ patitaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Whether one is standing, lying down, running, or fallen,

children.text: na pratīkṣati vai mṛtyuriti buddhvā śamaṃ vraja ||
children.translated_text: death does not wait. Knowing this, attain calm.

children.text: avatīrya jalaṃ divyaṃ bhāvaṃ śuddhaṃ samāsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having descended into the divine water, he established himself in a pure disposition.
Having practiced the <s>Raudra</s> chapter, then I shall see <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
And while I am reciting, disciplined and devoted to the state of <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: na mṛtyukālā bahavaḥ kariṣyanti mama vyathām ||
children.translated_text: the many moments of death will not cause me distress.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Considering him as one who spoke thus, speaking with pure speech,
the great ascetic, his spirit uncast down, sent his son away with difficulty.

children.text: abhivandya pituḥ pādau śirasā sa mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Having bowed with his head to his father's feet, that very illustrious one,
circumambulated him and set out, exceedingly resolved.
Having bowed to all the seers, that sage of noble mind, wishing to see him,
went to the god <s>Hara</s>, the remover of the distress of those who bow.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: nirgato 'tha tato nandī jagāma saritāṃ varām
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nandī</s>, having gone out from there, went to the best of rivers,
known as <s>Bhuvanā</s>, which brings happiness to all worlds.
Entering it, the wise one, one-pointed, stationed himself in a pool,
and then, afraid of death and composed, he recited the <s>Rudras</s>.
As he was reciting there itself, intent on that and desiring that blessing,

children.text: koṭirekā yadā japtā tadā devastutoṣa ha ||
children.translated_text: when one crore had been recited, then the god was pleased.
The blessed lord <s>Śarva</s>, fierce and wearing matted locks, came to him and said,

children.text: nandiṃstuṣṭo 'smi bhadraṃ te varaṃ vṛṇu yathepsitam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Nandī</s>, I am pleased; welfare to you. Choose whatever boon you desire."
Having bowed, he spoke to <s>Hara</s>, the remover of the distress of those who bow:
"I wish to recite a second crore, O powerful lord of the blessed ones."
Saying, "So be it," the god also went away as he had come.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: so 'vatīrya tato bhūyaḥ prayatātmā tathaiva ha
children.translated_text: Then he descended again, self-controlled, just as before,
and recited another crore, meditating only on <s>Rudra</s>.
Then, when the second crore had been completed, the bull-bannered one
came to him and said, "I am the giver of boons."
He said, "Blessed lord, destroyer of Time, I wish to recite a third crore also,
by your grace, O lord of gods, O mighty one."
Again the blessed lord replied, "So be it,"

children.text: uktvā jagāma svaṃ veśma devyā saha mahādyutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and after speaking, the greatly radiant one went to his own abode with the goddess.
Then he recited yet another, a third crore of the <s>Rudras</s>.
After that the twice-born one became like the sun at the end of an age.
When the three crores had been completed by him, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, whose brilliance was like fire,
the god <s>Soma</s>, together with the gaṇas, approached that place.

children.text: sa taṃ kareṇa saṃgṛhya uddhṛtya salilācca ha
children.translated_text: Taking him by the hand and lifting him out of the water,
and wiping <s>Nandī</s> with the tip of his hand, the destroyer of Time spoke:
The god said:
"O <s>Śailādi</s>, I am the giver of boons to you, pleased by this austerity.

children.text: sādhu japtaṃ tvayā dhīmanbrūhi yatte manogatam ||
children.translated_text: Well have you recited, wise one; tell me what is in your mind."
<s>Śailādi</s> said:

children.text: japeyaṃ koṭimanyāṃ tu bhūyo 'pi tava tejasā
children.translated_text: "May I recite yet another crore, again through your power.

children.text: varametaṃ vṛṇe deva yadi tuṣṭo 'si me vibho ||
children.translated_text: I choose this boon, O god, if you are pleased with me, O mighty lord."
The blessed lord said:

children.text: kiṃ te japtena bhūyo 'pi tuṣṭo 'smi tava sarvathā
children.translated_text: "What need have you of reciting further? I am wholly pleased with you.

children.text: yadyattvaṃ vṛṇuṣe kāmaṃ sarvaṃ tat pradadāni te ||
children.translated_text: Whatever desire you choose, I shall grant all of that to you.
<s>Brahmā</s>hood, or <s>Viṣṇu</s>hood, <s>Indra</s>hood, or the state of <s>Vāyu</s>,

children.text: ādityo bhava rudro vā brūhi kiṃ vā dadāni te ||
children.translated_text: be <s>Āditya</s> or <s>Rudra</s>; tell me, what shall I give you?"
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Thus addressed by the god, he bowed his head to his feet
and praised the destroyer of the cities, of <s>Kāma</s>'s body, of the sacrifice, and of the mountain.
<s>Nandī</s> said:
Homage to the god beyond the gods; homage indeed to the great god.
Homage indeed to the destroyer of <s>Kāma</s>'s body, to the blue-throated one.
Homage to the destroyer of <s>Tuṣita</s>, and to the burner of the three worlds.
Homage indeed to the fierce staff of Time, to the wielder of the fierce staff.
Homage to the one with the blue topknot; homage to the thousand-headed one,
and to the thousand-handed one, and to the thousand-footed one.
To the one whose hands and feet are everywhere, whose eyes and faces are everywhere,
whose hearing is everywhere, and who stands enveloping all.
Homage to you who are golden-colored, and likewise beyond the senses.
Homage indeed to the golden-liṅga, to the all-liṅga.
Homage to the one whose color is moon and sun, to the lord of yoga, the unconquered,
and to the one who holds the <s>Pināka</s> bow, and who holds spear and club.
To the mace-bearer and sword-bearer, and to the holder of the axe,

children.text: rathine varmiṇe caiva maheṣvāsāya vai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to the chariot-warrior, the armored one, and indeed to the great archer, homage.
Homage to the one with a trident in hand and to the holder of the fierce staff.
Homage to the lord of the gaṇas; homage to the lord of the <s>Rudras</s>.
Homage to the thousand-eyed one; homage indeed to the hundred-eyed one.

children.text: ādityānāṃ ca pataye vasūnāṃ pataye namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the lord of the <s>Ādityas</s> and to the lord of the <s>Vasus</s>.
Homage to the lord of earth; homage to the lord of space.
Homage to the lord of heaven, and homage to the husband of <s>Umā</s>.
Homage to the lord of yoga and to the giver of all yoga,
to the meditator, to the one meditated upon, and to the one praised by meditators.
To Death, to the staff of Time, to <s>Yama</s>, the great-souled one,
and to the lord of gods, and to the one of divine bodily frame.
To sacrifice, to the giver of wealth, to heaven, and to the giver of birthlessness,
to the impeller of all the gods, to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) of many forms.
To the immortal, the excellent one, and the one praised by all the gods,
and to the cutter off of <s>Brahmā</s>'s head, and of the great-souled sacrifice.
To the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>, the fierce one, and the remover of all inauspiciousness,
to the one whose form is half the body of <s>Umā</s>, and to the one with an eye in his forehead.
To the splitter of <s>Mahiṣa</s> and <s>Andhaka</s>, to the creator, indeed to the supreme one,

children.text: brahmaṇo gurave caiva brahmaṇo janakāya ca ||
children.translated_text: and to the teacher of <s>Brahmā</s>, and to the father of <s>Brahmā</s>,
and to the teacher of <s>Kumāra</s>, and to the giver of boons to <s>Kumāra</s>.
Obeisance indeed to the plough-bearing one, to the pestle-slaying one, to the one of great laughter.
To him whose fierce hand holds the noose of death, whose sacred thread is <s>Takṣaka</s>,
whose vehicle is a cloud with lightning, and likewise who rides the bull.
To him who dwells on <s>Himavat</s> and <s>Vindhya</s>, who dwells on Mount <s>Meru</s>,
who dwells on <s>Kailāsa</s>, and who is the friend of the lord of wealth.
To him who gave half of his body to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and who grants boons to him as well,
who knows all beings equally and has compassion for all beings.
To him who is the inner being and the presiding reality of the elements, and who gives life to living creatures,
to him as mind, as the one who thinks, and indeed as supreme self-regard.

children.text: budhyamānāya buddhāya draṣṭre vai cakṣuṣe namaḥ
children.translated_text: Obeisance to him as the one becoming aware, as the awakened one, as the seer, and indeed as sight.

children.text: namaste sparśayitre ca tathaiva sparśanāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Obeisance to you as the toucher, and likewise as touch.

children.text: namaste rasayitre ca tathaiva rasanāya ca
children.translated_text: Obeisance to you as the taster, and likewise as taste.

children.text: namo ghrāṇāya ghrātre ca śrotre śrotrāya caiva hi
children.translated_text: Obeisance to smell and to the smeller, and indeed to hearing and to the hearer.

children.text: hastine caiva hastāya tathā pādāya pādine ||
children.translated_text: To him who has hands, and to the hand itself; likewise to the foot and to him who has feet.

children.text: namo 'stvānandakartre ca ānandāya ca vai namaḥ
children.translated_text: Obeisance to him who creates bliss, and obeisance indeed to bliss itself.
To speech, and then to the possessor of speech, and likewise to the subtle element, the great-souled one.

children.text: sūkṣmāya caiva sthūlāya sattvāya rajase namaḥ
children.translated_text: To the subtle and likewise to the gross; obeisance to <s>sattva</s> and to <s>rajas</s>.
And constant obeisance to <s>tamas</s>, and to the knower of the field, the unconquered one.
Obeisance to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to the order of the worlds, to the lord of creatures.
To <s>Manu</s>, to the seven sages, to the one who is heated by austerity and who heats.
Obeisance to the one devoted to brahmins, then to the pure one, and likewise to <s>Durvāsas</s>.
To the craftsman, to the lord of crafts, to the learned one, to <s>Viśvakarman</s>.
Obeisance to <s>Atri</s> and to <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and likewise to <s>Aṅgiras</s>.
To <s>Pulaha</s>, to <s>Pulastya</s>, and to <s>Kratu</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, and <s>Anala</s>.

children.text: dharmāya rucaye caiva vasiṣṭhāya namo 'stu te
children.translated_text: Obeisance to you as <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Ruci</s>, and as <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
Obeisance to the being, to the lord of beings, to the lord of the <s>Kuṣmāṇḍas</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhate dravate caiva gāyate nṛtyate 'pi ca
children.translated_text: To him who stands and who runs, and likewise who sings and also dances,
to the irresistible and the inviolable, to the ageless and the deathless.
To the imperishable and undecaying, and likewise to the unobstructed.
To him who cannot be entered by anyone, who is visible and whose form is invisible.
To him who is subtler even than the subtle, all-pervading, great-souled.
Obeisance to you, blessed three-eyed one; obeisance to you, blessed <s>Śiva</s>.
Obeisance to you, lord of all worlds; obeisance to you, creator of the world.
I do not desire sovereignty over the gods, nor the state of <s>Brahmā</s>, nor again
the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O lord of gods, nor even the state of <s>Indra</s>, O protector of beings.
I desire, O <s>Īśāna</s>, the eternal and imperishable state of being one of your gaṇas.

children.text: nityaṃ tvāṃ sagaṇaṃ sāmbaṃ prasannaṃ saparicchadam
children.translated_text: I wish always to see you with your gaṇas, with <s>Ambā</s>, gracious and attended by your retinue,

children.text: draṣṭumicchāmi deveśa eṣa me dīyatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O lord of gods; let this boon be granted to me.

children.text: tvaṃ no gatiḥ purā deva tvaṃ caivārtāyanaṃ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: You were formerly our refuge, O god; and you alone are the resort of the afflicted, O lord.

children.text: śaraṇaṃ ca tvamevātha nānyaṃ paśyāmi karhicit ||
children.translated_text: And you alone are my shelter; I never see any other.

children.text: tvayā tyaktasya caivāśu vināśo nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: For one abandoned by you there is swift destruction; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: anyāṃ gatiṃ na paśyāmi yasyā ātyantikaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: I see no other course whose good is ultimate.

children.text: anuraktaṃ ca bhaktaṃ ca tvatparaṃ tvadapāśrayam
children.translated_text: Receive me, O god, always attached, devoted, intent on you, and dependent on you.

children.text: pratīccha māṃ sadā deva eṣa me dīyatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let this boon be granted to me.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
The man who rises in the morning and recites this with undistracted mind,
after the breaking up of the body, will become equal to <s>Nandīśvara</s>.
And whoever hears this constantly, or has it recited among twice-born men,
having obtained the fruit of a horse sacrifice, is honored in <s>Rudra</s>'s world.

children.text: śrutvā sakṛdapi hy etaṃ stavaṃ pāpapraṇāśanam
children.translated_text: Having heard even once this hymn that destroys sin,

children.text: yatra tatra mṛto vyāsa na durgatimavāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: wherever he may die, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, he will not fall into a bad state.

children.text: yo 'dhītya nityaṃ stavametamagryaṃ devaṃ sadābhyarcayate yatātmā
children.translated_text: If, having studied this foremost hymn daily, the self-controlled man always worships the god,

children.text: kiṃ tasya yajñairvividhaiśca dānaistīrthaiḥ sutaptaiśca tathā tapobhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: what need has he of various sacrifices, gifts, sacred bathing places, severe austerities, or acts of tapas?
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then the lord of the gods, seeing him endowed with supreme devotion,
his eyes filled with tears, wretched, bowing his head at his feet,
grasped him with his two very gentle hands, the remover of supreme distress,

children.text: utthāpya nayane somaḥ aśrupūrṇe mamārja ha ||
children.translated_text: raised him up, and <s>Soma</s> wiped his eyes that were filled with tears.
Then, satisfied in heart, he spoke to him with words that seemed to refresh him,
while the lord looked upon all the leaders of the gaṇas together with the goddess.
The god said:

children.text: jāne bhaktiṃ tava mayi jāne cārtiṃ tavānagha
children.translated_text: I know your devotion to me, and I know your pain, O sinless one.
O son of <s>Śilāda</s>, hear the outcome of all this.
You shall be immortal, abandoned by old age, forever free from suffering,
imperishable and undecaying, together with your father and your circle of friends.
You shall be dear to me and a lord of gaṇas, possessing my strength and my valor.

children.text: iṣṭo mama sadā caiva mama pārśvagataḥ sadā
children.translated_text: You shall always be dear to me, and always stationed at my side.
You shall have my form and be endowed with the power of great yoga.
I grant you a prosperous island, the milk ocean, source of nectar,
as a dwelling place; there you shall delight forever.
Then the greatly radiant one removed from himself a lotus-made garland,
and fastened it upon <s>Nandin</s>, divine in form.

children.text: sa tayā mālayā nandī babhau kaṇṭhāvasaktayā
children.translated_text: With that garland hanging upon his neck, <s>Nandin</s> shone forth,
three-eyed, ten-armed, splendid, like a second <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Then the blessed <s>Hara</s>, taking him by the hand,

children.text: uvāca brūhi kiṃ te 'dya dadāni varamuttamam ||
children.translated_text: said, 'Tell me what supreme boon I should give you today.'
And this hermitage of yours, made potent by your austerity,

children.text: japyeśvara iti khyāto mama guhyo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will be known as <s>Japyeśvara</s>, sacred and secret to me.
For a yojana all around, the field will be divine, surrounded by hosts of gods,
thronged with siddhas and cāraṇas, and served by hosts of apsarases.

children.text: siddhikṣetraṃ paraṃ guhyaṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It will become a supreme, secret field of siddhi; there is no doubt.
Whatever a person does by deed, mind, or speech,

children.text: śubhaṃ vāpyaśubhaṃ vātra sarvaṃ bhavitṛ tacchubham ||
children.translated_text: whether auspicious or inauspicious, here all that will become auspicious.

children.text: jāpyaṃ mānasaṃ tulyaṃ vai rudrāṇāṃ tadbhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Mental recitation there will indeed be equal to the recitation of the Rudras.

children.text: yatra tatra mṛtā martyā yāsyanti tava lokatām ||
children.translated_text: Mortals who die there, wherever they may be, will go to your world.
Then the great ascetic took water that had flowed from his matted hair, pure as a necklace,
and, saying, "Become a river," released it.

children.text: sā tato divyatoyā ca puṇyā maṇijalā śubhā
children.translated_text: Then she, with divine water, holy, auspicious, and with jewel-like water,
filled with haṃsas and kāraṇḍavas and adorned with cakravākas,
provided with groves of lotuses and blue lotuses, began to flow as a great river.
And assuming the form of a woman, with joined palms and her head bowed,
lotus-and-blue-lotus-petal-eyed, she stood before <s>Mahādeva</s>.
Then the god spoke to that river, who had presented herself in person:
"Since, O goddess of auspicious face, you have issued from the water of my matted hair,

children.text: tasmāj jaṭodā nāmnā tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi saridvarā ||
children.translated_text: therefore you shall be named <s>Jaṭodā</s>, best of rivers.

children.text: tvayi snānaṃ tu yaḥ kuryācchuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever bathes in you, pure and with a restrained mind,
will obtain the fruit of a horse sacrifice and be honored in <s>Rudra</s>'s world."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, in the presence of the goddess, made brilliant <s>Nandīśvara</s>
bow at her feet, saying, "This is your son."
She smelled his head and, stroking him with her two hands,
out of motherly love she bathed him with three streams born from her breasts,
with milk white as a conch, while the goddess looked upon the god.
Those three streams of hers flowed forth like a flood-bearing river.
Then <s>Hara</s> called that holy river <s>Trisrotasī</s>.
Seeing the three-streamed river, the Bull was exceedingly delighted.
He bellowed; and from that sound another river then arose.
Because that great river had issued from the bellowing of the bull,

children.text: tasmāḍ ḍhitkirikāṃ tāṃ vai uvāca vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s> called it <s>Ḍhitkirikā</s>.
The god then fastened on him his own wondrous and supremely marvelous
golden crown, and earrings born of nectar.

children.text: taṃ tathābhyarcitaṃ vyomni dṛṣṭvā meghaḥ prabhākaraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him thus honored in the sky, the shining cloud,
fit to be a vehicle of the gods, sprinkled him, rumbling and endowed with lightning.
When he had been consecrated, two streams flowed forth strongly.
Because one river emerged from the gold and began to flow,
<s>Mahādeva</s> called it by the name <s>Svarṇodakā</s>.
Because a second holy river began to flow

children.text: prāvartata nadī puṇyā ūcur jambūnadīti tām ||
children.translated_text: from the auspicious crown made of jāmbūnada gold, they called it <s>Jambūnadī</s>.
This is the place called <s>Pañcanada</s>, situated near <s>Japyeśvara</s>.
The fruit of these rivers, beginning with <s>Jaṭodā</s>, has been explained by the great-souled one.

children.text: tacca pañcanadaṃ divyaṃ devaṃ japyeśvaraṃ ca tam
children.translated_text: That divine <s>Pañcanada</s> and that god <s>Japyeśvara</s>:
one who has fasted for three nights, goes there, bathes, and worships the trident-bearing lord,
becomes an attendant of <s>Nandīśvara</s>, dwelling in the Milk Ocean.
But whoever gives up his hard-to-abandon breaths at <s>Japyeśvara</s>,
whether according to rule or otherwise, becomes a gaṇapati of mine.
He is ever equal to <s>Nandīśvara</s>, eternal, undecaying, and imperishable,

children.text: mama pārśvādanapagaḥ priyaḥ saṃmata eva ca ||
children.translated_text: never departing from my side, dear and approved by me.

children.text: japyeśvaraṃ pañcanadaṃ ca tadvai yo mānavo 'bhyetya jahāti deham
children.translated_text: The human being who approaches <s>Japyeśvara</s> and that <s>Pañcanada</s> and leaves his body

children.text: sa me sadā syādgaṇapo variṣṭhastvayā samaḥ kāntivapuśca nityam ||
children.translated_text: will always be my foremost lord of gaṇas, equal to you and eternally possessing a lovely form and radiance.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Those mighty lords of gaṇas, all lords over the lords of gods,

children.text: praṇamya devaṃ devīṃ ca idaṃ vacanamabruvan ||
children.translated_text: bowed to the god and the goddess and spoke these words:
"Blessed lord, destroyer of the enemies of the gods, god of gods, husband of <s>Ambikā</s>,

children.text: kimarthaṃ vayamāhūtā ājñāpaya kṛtaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: for what purpose have we been summoned? Command us; that thing is already done.

children.text: kiṃ sāgarāñchoṣayāmo yamaṃ vā saha kiṃkaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Shall we dry up the oceans, or <s>Yama</s> together with his servants?
Shall we slay Death, or shall even non-death not exist today, O lotus-born one?

children.text: baddhvendraṃ saha devaiśca saviṣṇuṃ saha vāyunā
children.translated_text: Having bound <s>Indra</s> together with the gods, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> together with <s>Vāyu</s>,
shall we, greatly enraged, bring the daityas along with the dānavas?
Whose terrible calamity shall we cause today at your command?
Or whose festival today, O god, rich with every desired object?"
To all of them as they spoke thus and bowed down, the god, tender toward his devotees,
<s>Bhava</s>, lord of the gaṇas, spoke after honoring the gaṇas.
The god said:
"Listen to the purpose for which you, benefactors of the world, have been summoned here.
After hearing it, with disciplined selves, carry it out without hesitation.
This <s>Nandīśvara</s> is our son, the lord over the lords of all.
He is dear, your foremost leader, and your composed commander.
Therefore, by my command, all of you, being in agreement,
consecrate him as commander, the great lord of yoga, your master.
From today onward this auspicious <s>Nandīśvara</s>
shall be dear to you, endowed with honor, your immortal commander and lord."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: evamukte bhagavatā gaṇapāḥ sarva eva te
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One had spoken thus, all those gaṇapatis
agreed, saying "So be it," and then brought the requisites.
They brought for him a divine, auspicious seat, the support of his form,
made of jāmbūnada gold, resembling <s>Meru</s>, and delightful.
It was made of refined gold, shining with beautiful gold,
hung with strings of pearls and radiant with jewels and gems,
and covered with a net of little bells, with pillars made of vaiḍūrya.
a pavilion furnished with beautiful jewels and facing every direction;
having made it, they made in its center that excellent, auspicious seat.
Before it they made a dark-blue footstool, shining like diamond,
for the placement of his feet, and two kalaśa vessels at its sides,
filled with the finest waters and with their mouths covered by lotuses.
Having established the fire in front, and also a bull at the side,

children.text: savatsāṃ surabhiṃ cāpi tasya pārśve 'tha dakṣiṇe ||
children.translated_text: and a milk-cow with her calf on his right side,
an auspicious parasol with a hundred ribs, made of jāmbūnada gold,
shining with a back white like conch, pearl necklace, and water,
a moon-white fan with a very lovely golden handle,
and a garland of lotuses attended by rows of bees,
the gaṇa-lords brought there, together with golden <s>nandyāvartas</s>,

children.text: punarvasuṃ ca puṣyaṃ ca dvau matsyau varuṇālayau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Punarvasu</s> and <s>Puṣya</s>, and two fish, dwellers in <s>Varuṇa</s>'s realm,

children.text: svastikaṃ vardhamānaṃ ca śrīvatsaṃ caiva kāñcanam
children.translated_text: a svastika, a vardhamāna, and a golden śrīvatsa,
reed-stalks and bamboos, and also a maiden who had been honored,

children.text: airāvataṃ supratīkaṃ gajāv etau ca pūjitau
children.translated_text: <s>Airāvata</s> and <s>Supratīka</s>, those two honored elephants,

children.text: dhvajaṃ ca pūjitaṃ divyaṃ śaṅkhaṃ caivenduvarcasam ||
children.translated_text: an honored divine banner, and a conch with the radiance of the moon,
a thousand golden kalaśa vessels of splendid brilliance,

children.text: rājatānāṃ sahasraṃ ca pārthivānāṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: a thousand silver ones, and likewise a thousand earthen ones,
and a thousand copper vessels, divine and shining like fire,

children.text: vāsoyugaṃ vṛkṣajaṃ ca virajaḥ sūkṣmameva ca ||
children.translated_text: a pair of garments made from tree-fiber, stainless and very fine,
and a golden crown, well fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,

children.text: kuṇḍale cāmale divye vajraṃ caiva varāyudham ||
children.translated_text: two spotless divine earrings, and the vajra, the excellent weapon,

children.text: paṭṭisaṃ ca mahaddivyaṃ śūlaṃ cāśanimeva ca
children.translated_text: a great divine paṭṭisa, a trident, and a thunderbolt,
a cord made of jāmbūnada gold, and also a pair of armlets,
a necklace with limbs variegated by jewels, and rocanā and rucaka too,

children.text: nalabhāṃ pāriyātraṃ ca varṣaṃ kaṅkaṇim eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nalabhā</s>, <s>Pāriyātra</s>, <s>Varṣa</s>, and <s>Kaṅkaṇī</s>,
divine darbha grass, sacrificial fuel, ghee, and incense as well;
from every side the unwearied gaṇa-lords, approved by the gods, brought them.
Then the directions, the oceans, <s>Varuṇa</s> together with <s>Dhaneśvara</s>,
<s>Yama</s>, <s>Agni</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, and the Moon and Sun together with the planets,
all the star-forms, the lunar mansions, and <s>Dhruva</s> as well,
the <s>Rudras</s>, rākṣasas, yakṣas, the two <s>Aśvins</s>, daityas, and dānavas,
gandharvas and apsarases, and <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s>,
the earth, the oceans, the regions, and the mountains,
trees, creepers, and powerful herbs,
all rivers assembled, and every kind of animal as well.

children.text: lokasya mātaraścaiva pṛthivī svarga eva ca
children.translated_text: The mothers of the world, and the earth and heaven too,
beings, primordial nature, and all the senses,

children.text: tīrthāni caiva sarvāṇi dānāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: all sacred fords, and many kinds of gifts,
the Ṛcs, Yajuses, Sāmans, and also the Atharvāṅgirases,
sacrifices, rites, offerings, and observances,
all the meters, piśācas, and beings of divine origin,
<s>Brahmā</s> and the seers, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> with his attendants as well, came there.
When all of them had arrived, the Blessed One whose banner is the bull,
ordered <s>Pitāmaha</s> to perform the whole procedure of the rite.
There he made each kalaśa vessel furnished with every herb,
filled it with waters, and covered its mouth with lotuses.

children.text: jayāṃ ca vijayāṃ caiva siṃhīṃ vyāghrīṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Jayā</s> and <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Siṃhī</s> and <s>Vyāghrī</s> likewise,
<s>Suvarcalā</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, <s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, and <s>Punarnavā</s>,
<s>Kumārī</s>, <s>Candrakāntā</s>, and also <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s>,
<s>Ādityavarcas</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>, and <s>Śrīniketanā</s>,
and likewise <s>Kumudvatī</s>: those herbs they then placed in them,
in all the earthen vessels at that time, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, all the lords of the gaṇas.

children.text: sauvarṇeṣu tu sarveṣu tīrthāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: But in all the golden vessels the Blessed One placed the various sacred fords,
and all kinds of gifts as well.

children.text: rājateṣu ca kumbheṣu mantrāṃśchandāṃsi caiva ha
children.translated_text: In the silver jars he placed the mantras and the meters too,
and various other rites, desired offerings and other offerings alike.
In all the udumbara-wood vessels he placed the rivers and the oceans,
and the Blessed One set in them austerities and observances too.
There the mighty lord filled and consecrated each kalaśa vessel,

children.text: veṣṭayitvā ca sūtreṇa devebhyaḥ pradadau vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: wrapped it with a cord, and gave it to the gods.

children.text: sa jagrāha tadā brahmā ekaṃ kalaśamātmanā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> himself took one kalaśa vessel,
and gave one to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and one to wise <s>Indra</s>.
<s>Pitāmaha</s> gave the others to the gaṇapas and to the seers.
Then, after seating him upon that seat, the great-minded
<s>Brahmā</s> worshiped him and then himself consecrated him.
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, then <s>Śakra</s>, and the seers together with the immortals,
and all those lords of the gaṇas consecrated <s>Nandin</s>.
Then he himself gave the divine pair of garments and divine fragrances,

children.text: keyūre kuṇḍale caiva mukuṭaṃ hārameva ca
children.translated_text: the armlets, earrings, crown, and necklace,

children.text: paṭṭisaṃ śūlavajre ca aśanīṃ ca dadau svayam ||
children.translated_text: the paṭṭisa, trident, vajra, and thunderbolt.
<s>Devendra</s> took up the parasol, and <s>Vāyu</s> the fan,
while the seers, headed by <s>Pitāmaha</s>, praised him.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> said:
Homage to the king of the <s>Kuṣmāṇḍas</s>, and to him whose hand raises the vajra,
to the grandson of <s>Śālaṅkāyana</s>, to him who arose from the furrow of the plough,
and to the son of <s>Śilāda</s>, the performer of <s>Rudra</s>'s japa.
Homage to the god devoted to <s>Rudra</s>, who lies within the waters.

children.text: gaṇānāṃ pataye caiva bhūtānāṃ pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the lord of the ganas, and likewise homage to the lord of beings.
Homage to the god who is the son of <s>Uma</s>, who bears the pattisa weapon.
Homage to him who is terrible with tusks, and who has an eye on his forehead.
Homage to the crusher, the most excellent one, and to him who is devoted to <s>Isana</s>.
Homage to the brave superintendent of the gate, the lord of <s>Suyasa</s>.
Homage to him who wears the foremost garland, and to him who dwells in the Milk Ocean.
Homage to the great lord of the ganas and to the great lord of yoga.
Homage to <s>Dindimunda</s>, the fierce one, who delights in the single syllable.
Homage to the imperishable and immortal one, the ageless and deathless one.

children.text: paśūnāṃ pataye caiva jetre mṛtyostathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Homage likewise to the lord of animals, and also to the conqueror of Death.
Homage to him whose speed is like the wind, to the omniscient and unconquered one.
Homage likewise to him of many heads and many feet.
Homage to the crowned one, the earringed one, whose arms are great clubs.
Protect all the gods and all the ganas, O god; homage be to you.
<s>Sanatkumara</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ stutvā tato devastasmai vyāsa mahātmane
children.translated_text: Having praised the great-souled god in this way, O <s>Vyasa</s>,

children.text: prāñjaliḥ prayato bhūtvā jayaśabdaṃ cakāra ha ||
children.translated_text: he stood with joined palms and disciplined mind, and uttered a cry of victory.

children.text: tato gaṇā jayety ūcus tato devāstato 'surāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the ganas cried, "Victory!" and then the gods and then the asuras did the same.

children.text: tataḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni brahmā śakrastathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Then all beings, and <s>Brahma</s> and <s>Sakra</s> likewise, cried out.
Then the lords of the ganas, filled with joy and delighting him,
sounded conches, kettledrums, patahas and adambaras, flutes and panavas, krikavans and govisanikas,
as well as dindimas, venukas, and mardalas everywhere.
The lords of the ganas played them, gladdening him, full of joy.
<s>Sanatkumara</s> said:
The mortal who constantly recites this hymn to <s>Nandisvara</s>, made by the gods,

children.text: paṭheta satataṃ martyaḥ sa gacchenmama lokatām ||
children.translated_text: will attain my world.
Whoever goes to sleep after saying, "Homage to <s>Nandisvara</s>,"

children.text: tasya kuṣmāṇḍarājebhyo na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit ||
children.translated_text: has no fear anywhere from the kings of the Kusmandas.
Wherever this most highly worshiped hymn is regularly established,

children.text: na bhayaṃ tatra bhavati grahebhyo vyāsa sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: there, O <s>Vyasa</s>, there is never any fear from the planets.

children.text: nandīśvaraṃ ye praṇamanti martyā nityaṃ prasannendriyaśuddhasattvāḥ
children.translated_text: Those mortals who bow daily to <s>Nandisvara</s>, their senses clear and their nature purified,

children.text: te devadevasya sahādriputryā iṣṭā variṣṭhāśca gaṇā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: become dear and most excellent ganas of the god of gods together with the daughter of the mountain.
<s>Sanatkumara</s> said:
Then <s>Bhava</s>, lord of the deities, lord of being and non-being,
honored the gods who had come there and spoke to the <s>Maruts</s> concerning the maiden.
The lord, together with <s>Sakra</s> and the Grandfather,
summoned by name those <s>Maruts</s> of great speed, great strength, and great power.
"Your daughter <s>Suyasa</s> is fortunate and of divine beauty.

children.text: dātumarhatha tāṃ subhrūṃ snuṣāṃ mahyaṃ mahābalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: You mighty ones should give that fair-browed girl to me as a daughter-in-law."
The <s>Maruts</s> said:
"You are the lord of us, of her, and likewise of the whole world,
O lord of the three worlds, but you should not have to ask.

children.text: tvayaiva deyā grāhyā ca tvaṃ no gatiranuttamā
children.translated_text: She is to be given and received by you yourself; you are our unsurpassed refuge.
Do not, by asking, make us appear as outsiders, O illustrious one.
Our father is the blessed <s>Kasyapa</s>, and <s>Marici</s> is our grandfather.
The father of our grandfather is <s>Brahma</s>, and you are the grandfather even of him.
Since you are our grandfather, you should not make us strangers."
When the lord of gods had been addressed in this way by the <s>Maruts</s>, those best of gods,
he brought <s>Suyasa</s>, the daughter of the <s>Maruts</s>, at that very moment.
There <s>Brahma</s>, the grandsire of the worlds, himself became his hotar priest,

children.text: kaśyapaśca tathodgātā atriḥ sāma svayaṃ jagau
children.translated_text: and <s>Kasyapa</s> likewise was the udgatar, while <s>Atri</s> himself sang the Saman.
The gods <s>Atharvan</s> and <s>Angiras</s> also performed the office of brahman priest.
<s>Narada</s>, <s>Parvata</s>, the singer <s>Citrasena</s>,

children.text: viśvāvasū ruciścaiva hāhā hūhū tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Visvavasu</s>, <s>Ruci</s>, and also <s>Haha</s> and <s>Huhu</s>,
as well as the renowned <s>Salisiras</s> and <s>Gandamandaka</s>,
<s>Iti</s>, <s>Indravaha</s>, <s>Yajnavaha</s>, and then <s>Daksina</s>:
these and other gandharvas sang with sweet voices.

children.text: urvaśī caiva rambhā ca ghṛtācī pūrvacittyapi
children.translated_text: <s>Urvasi</s>, <s>Rambha</s>, <s>Ghrtaci</s>, and <s>Purvacitti</s>,
as well as <s>Tilottama</s>, <s>Visvaci</s>, and other beautiful apsarases,
greatly fortunate, danced a dance that charmed the gods.
<s>Sanatkumara</s> said:
Thus, O <s>Vyasa</s>, that peerless and faultless wedding
of the wise <s>Nandin</s>, chief of the ganas, took place.

children.text: tataḥ sa tu kṛtodvāho nandī gatvā mahāmanāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the great-minded <s>Nandi</s>, after the marriage had been performed,

children.text: pādānvavande devasya devyā brahmaṇa eva ca
children.translated_text: went and bowed at the feet of the god, of the goddess, of <s>Brahma</s>,

children.text: śilādasya ca lokeśaḥ śriyā paramayā yutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and of <s>Silada</s>; the lord of the world was endowed with supreme splendor.
The god said:

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva putra tvaṃ snuṣā ceyaṃ tava priyā
children.translated_text: "Choose a boon, my son, and this beloved daughter-in-law of yours too.

children.text: varaṃ dadāmi te vatsa anayā sahamīpsitam ||
children.translated_text: Dear child, I grant you the boon you desire together with her."
<s>Nandi</s> said:
"Blessed lord, if you are pleased, let my devotion to you be firm.

children.text: sadā ca tuṣṭo bhava me sāmbaḥ saha gaṇeśvaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And always be pleased with me, together with <s>Amba</s> and the lords of the ganas.

children.text: pitaraṃ caiva me deva utpādakam imaṃ prabho
children.translated_text: And this father of mine, O god, who brought me into being, O lord,
you should unite with your favor, O giver of desires."
The god said:
"I, together with the lord of the ganas, will always be very pleased with you, O <s>Nandisa</s>.

children.text: pārvatyā sahito dhīmann idaṃ ca śṛṇu me vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with <s>Parvati</s>, O wise one, hear this further word of mine.
Always beloved and most excellent, endowed with supreme lordly power,
a great yogin, a great archer, of great strength and valor,

children.text: ajayyaścaiva jetā ca pūjyejyaśca sadā bhava
children.translated_text: unconquerable and a conqueror, always worthy of worship and sacrifice: become so.

children.text: ahaṃ yatra bhavāṃstatra yatra tvaṃ tatra cāpyaham ||
children.translated_text: Where I am, there you are; and where you are, there I too am.

children.text: ayaṃ ca te pitā vipraḥ paramaiśvaryasaṃyutaḥ
children.translated_text: And this brahmin father of yours will be endowed with supreme lordly power.
He will become my superintendent of ganas, a great lord of the great ganas."
And I grant him this <s>Vaibhrāja</s> mountain, moving at will and entirely golden,
adorned with divine mansions and crowded with people.
With it he will wander through all worlds just as he desires.
And his dwelling on <s>Śrīparvata</s> will be greatly worshiped.

children.text: bhṛgau tasmiṃśca yaḥ prāṇāṃstyakṣyate vai sudhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: The truly righteous man who gives up his life at that <s>Bhṛgu</s> precipice
will move at will in <s>Vaibhrāja</s> and become his gaṇapa.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then the greatly blessed goddess gave a boon to <s>Śailādi</s>.
He said, "May my devotion to you always be unfailing."
Then <s>Marutsutā</s> also, urged by both of them,

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇu yatheṣṭaṃ vai tāv idaṃ pratyuvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: was told, "Choose whatever boon you wish," and she replied this to the two of them:

children.text: yuvayorastu bhaktirme tathā bhartari caiva hi
children.translated_text: "May my devotion be toward you two, and likewise toward my husband.

children.text: nityaṃ cānapagā syānme dharme ca matiruttamā
children.translated_text: May it always be unfailing, and may my mind be excellent in <s>dharma</s>.
This is the boon I desire, O two lords of gods, givers of a thousand boons."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then the two delighted gods said, "This will be so for you, O bright-smiling one,"
to that daughter-in-law of lovely complexion.
Then all his gaṇas, desiring what was dear to the god, approached him,
and those great-souled ones gave a boon; the golden-radiant one chose:

children.text: yuṣmāsu mama bhaktiśca aiśvaryaṃ cāpi saṃmatam
children.translated_text: "May I have devotion toward you, and sovereignty approved by you,

children.text: vaśyāśca yūyaṃ sarve me priyo yuṣmākameva ca ||
children.translated_text: and may all of you be subject to me, while I am dear to you as well."
The gaṇas said:
"You are our counsel and assent, our going and our return.
You are the lord of all of us and the lord even of the gods.
You are foremost among the <s>Kuṣmāṇḍas</s>, and mighty among the <s>Rudras</s>.
You are the doorkeeper of afflictions and likewise of the <s>Pramathas</s>.

children.text: mahābalo mahāyogī senānīs tvaṃ hi no mataḥ
children.translated_text: You are very strong, a great yogin, and we regard you as our commander.

children.text: tvaṃ bhūto bhūtanetā ca nāyako 'tha vināyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are a spirit and leader of spirits, a guide and also <s>Vināyaka</s>.
You are lord of the grahas and bearer of a fierce staff.
You are the foremost warrior, destroyer of enemies; you are a hero, you are lord of heaven.
You are of great majesty and dwell in the Milk Ocean.
You are the abode of <s>Japyeśvara</s> and made manifest by <s>Japyeśvara</s>.
You are the nurturer of all beings, the giver of boons, worshiped by givers of boons.
Be our giver of boons, O <s>Bhūteśvara</s>, O lord."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: sa evaṃ gaṇapaiḥ sarvaiḥ stuto nandīśvaro vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: Thus praised by all the gaṇapas, the powerful <s>Nandīśvara</s>

children.text: uvāca praṇataḥ sarvānbrūta kiṃ karavāṇi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: bowed and said to all of them, "Tell me what I should do for you."

children.text: ta evamuktā gaṇapāḥ sarva eva mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: All those gaṇapas, mighty as they were, when thus addressed,
spoke to him, knowing the god's divine disposition, in the presence of the god of gods:
"You have been made our lord of gaṇas by the god <s>Śambhu</s>.
You have been consecrated by us as leader, giver of <s>dharma</s>.
Therefore be auspicious and gentle, virtuous even toward the unvirtuous.
Endowed with patience, purity, and self-restraint, always do what is dear to us."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
When he had been addressed thus, he bowed to them all with great respect,
placed his joined palms on his head, and then praised the gaṇapas.
<s>Nandī</s> said:

children.text: namo vaḥ sarvabhūtebhyo namo yogibhya eva ca
children.translated_text: "Homage to you, all beings; homage also to the yogins.
Homage too to the homeless ones, and likewise homage to the lords of yogins.

children.text: namaḥ kāmacarebhyaśca nama ugrebhya eva ca
children.translated_text: Homage to those who move at will, and homage also to the fierce ones.
Again and again homage to deaths, to <s>Yamas</s>, and to times of death.
Homage to those with golden garlands, and also to all who uphold <s>dharma</s>.
Homage to you who slay, and likewise to those who cannot be slain.
Homage to the supreme yogins, and again and again homage to the matted-haired ones.
Homage to you whose forms are invisible, and likewise to those of altered form.
Homage to those clothed in bark, and also to those clothed in skins.
Homage to those with white garments and garlands, and again and again homage to those with variegated garlands.
Again and again homage to those who run, those who rush, and those who have set forth.

children.text: namo munibhyo gāyadbhyo japadbhyaśca namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to sages, to those who sing, and again and again homage to those who mutter prayers.
Homage to those in the form of <s>Śarabhas</s>, and also to those of a hundred forms.
Homage to those dwelling on mountains, and also to those in tiger form.
Homage to those in cat form, and also to crows and kokas.
Homage to those in divine form, and likewise to the winds.
Homage likewise to fires and waters, and likewise to the <s>Varuṇas</s>.
Homage to those in the form of <s>Dhaneśa</s>, and also to those of every form.
Homage to those with belly-faces, and also to those with faces of every kind.
Homage to those of dwarf form, and also to those of lovely form.
Again and again homage to those who nourish gods, asuras, and human beings.

children.text: namo vaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ namo vaḥ sarvataḥ śubhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to you among all beings; homage to you, auspicious ones, on every side.
Homage to you who seize, and likewise homage to those who release.
Homage to you who are auspicious, and likewise to those who are inauspicious.
May you be gentle and auspicious to me, O leaders of the gaṇas.

children.text: iti stutā gaṇapatayo mahābalāḥ śubhairvacobhiḥ suraśatrunāśanāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus praised with auspicious words, may the mighty gaṇapatis, destroyers of the enemies of the gods,

children.text: diśantu me sukhamatulaṃ sukhapradā balaṃ ca vīryaṃ sthiratāṃ ca saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: bestow on me incomparable happiness, since they grant happiness, and strength, valor, and steadiness in battle.

children.text: tapo 'kṣayaṃ sthānamathātulāṃ gatiṃ yaśastathāgryaṃ bahu dharmanityatām
children.translated_text: May they grant imperishable austerity, an incomparable station and destiny, foremost fame, and abundant constancy in <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: diśantu sarvaṃ manasepsitaṃ ca me sureśvarāḥ puṣṭimanuttamāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: May those lords of the gods grant me everything desired by my mind, and also unsurpassed prosperity."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Whoever regularly recites these two hymns of <s>Nandī</s> and the lords of gaṇas
is freed from all sins, as if after the concluding bath of an aśvamedha.
At the later twilight, by reciting, one should cast off the sin committed by day;
or at the earlier twilight too, by reciting, one should cast off what was done through the whole night.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then all those gaṇapas, having been praised by that wise one
and dismissed, bowed down to <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s> and departed.

children.text: devāśca sarvalokāśca tato devaḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the god himself, the lord of the gods and of all the worlds,
the great-minded one, having created the house of <s>Nandīśvara</s> and having granted

children.text: īpsitaṃ saha devyā vai jagāma sthānamavyayam ||
children.translated_text: what was desired, went with the goddess to the imperishable place.

children.text: ya imaṃ nandino janma varadānaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: The brahmin who reads, or causes to be heard, this birth of <s>Nandin</s>

children.text: abhiṣekaṃ vivāhaṃ ca paṭhedvā śrāvayīta vā
children.translated_text: and likewise the granting of the boon, the consecration, and the marriage,
when dead, goes to dwelling in the same world as <s>Nandīśvara</s>.

children.text: yo niyatastu paṭhetprayatātmā sarvamimaṃ praṇato bhavabhaktyā
children.translated_text: But whoever, disciplined and with purified self, bowed down with devotion to <s>Bhava</s>, reads all this,

children.text: so 'pi gataḥ paralokavicārī nandisamo 'nucaro hi mama syāt ||
children.translated_text: he too, having gone to the next world and considering the world beyond, shall become my attendant, equal to <s>Nandin</s>.
